docs.title: PCS Analyzer
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer is a desktop application for the analysis, fitting and visualization of pseudocontact shifts (PCS) in paramagnetic molecular systems. It connects molecular structures with experimental NMR data to calculate PCS, fit magnetic susceptibility tensors and examine agreement with the chosen model.

Quick Start Installation Examples

docs.title: Main interface
docs.text:
Structure and PCS data, analysis results and calculation controls in the main workspace.

See Interface Overview for the layout and Projects and Persistence for saving an analysis or reopening projects.

docs.title: Analysis capabilities
docs.text:
• Structure-based analysis

    Load molecular geometries, assign the paramagnetic centre and calculate PCS with axial or rhombic tensor components. Account for symmetry and torsional averaging when the experimental assignments require it.

    Structures · Averaging

  • PCS fitting and diagnostics

    Fit tensor parameters and orientation, inspect residuals and compare conformer populations or complementary observables under their stated models.

    Fitting · Residuals

  • Scientific visualization

    Inspect molecular geometry and PCS fields through polar plots, projections and 3D views, and export figures for further analysis or presentation.

    2D PCS · 3D structure

docs.text:

docs.title: PCS model
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer uses a point-dipole PCS model with an axial default and an optional rhombic contribution. Structure, centre, tensor orientation and averaging must match the experiment you intend to interpret. Paramagnetic shift differences are not automatically pure PCS.

Polar contours and G_ax vs PCS are axial diagnostics. Tensor-aware tables and views follow the active prediction model.

Equations, input units and definitions are given in PCS Theory and Tensor Conventions. The method references distinguish background literature from the assumptions of the implemented workflows.

Some documentation topics remain incomplete. Review Current Limitations and the assumptions of the workflow you intend to use.

docs.title: Modules and workbenches
docs.text: NMR Workbench processes spectra and prepares reviewed shift observations. PCS Workbench compares point-dipole and distributed PCS fields using its own ORCA/grid inputs. External side tools are installed and launched through Module Manager.

docs.text:

docs.title: Examples and Practice Data
docs.text: Use Quick Start to begin with your own structure and PCS data. The examples below are optional exercises for learning a workflow or checking how a known dataset behaves.

docs.title: Find and open the files
docs.text:
Use the example files supplied with the same PCS Analyzer release as your application. In a source checkout they are under examples/; in the portable build, examples/ is beside the executable. Keep each example's directory intact. The repository examples directory contains the same practice inputs. Use the tutorials below for instructions; no Python generation scripts are needed.

  • Portable application: extract the full release archive, then open the examples/ directory beside the executable.
  • Source files: extract the matching release's source archive and use its examples/ directory. For an FID, download the directory contents together; a GitHub HTML file preview is not an input file.

Open .pcsp files with File → Open PCS Project.... They already contain the saved structure and analysis inputs. Save your practice results to another path. For FID exercises, open the dataset in NMR Workbench as directed by the tutorial; a FID directory is not a PCS project.

For a prepared project, do not load its neighbouring XYZ or reimport its CSV unless the tutorial asks you to. Those files let you inspect or import individual inputs; the project already contains them. Reloading a structure starts a different preparation workflow and can replace the restored inputs.

docs.title: Choose an exercise
docs.text:
Paths below are relative to examples/. Within each tutorial, short paths such as noisy/demo.pcsp are relative to that tutorial's demo directory. CSV files used alongside a project come from the same scenario directory, unless another location is explicitly given.

Learn to… Starting file or directory Expected result and tutorial Fit tensor orientation and compare rhombicity standard_fitting_demo/mode_b/demo.pcsp Known axial/rhombic values 12 / 3 E-32 m³; standard fitting tutorial also covers Modes A/C and axial/rhombic diagnostic pairs Derive PCS from observed/reference shifts nmr_pcs_fitting_demo/direct/start.pcsp Twelve reviewed targets; fitted tensor 12 / 3 under the stated contact assumptions; NMR-to-PCS tutorial Compare conformer populations and reliability multi_conformer_demo/informative/demo.pcsp Compare informative and indistinguishable conformer signatures; Multi-Conformer tutorial Fit PCS and RDC together joint_pcs_rdc_demo/noisy/demo.pcsp Known-tensor recovery with noise; a separate rank-deficient case is rejected; Joint PCS+RDC tutorial Fit a simplified PRE model pre_demo/noisy/demo.pcsp Effective correlation time near 3 ns; compare a restricted-bound case; PRE tutorial Compare lanthanides and separate shift contributions multi_lanthanide_demo/noisy/demo.pcsp Tensor, Reilley and series diagnostics at 300 K; Multi-Lanthanide tutorial Search a selected torsion conformer_search_demo/demo.pcsp About +45° rotation with fixed atoms retained; Conformer Search tutorial Inspect averaging and viewer representations averaging_visualization_demo/groups.xyz Detect the supplied synthetic groups and compare representations; averaging tutorial Process raw NMR or import prepared shifts nmr_workflow_demo/ Five picked peaks and four sample assignments in the FID exercise; FID/CSV tutorial Track a VT series nmr_vt_demo/FID/Paramagnetic/ Five temperatures, four tracks and Curie-model comparisons; VT tutorial Inspect a molecular PCS case documentation_demo/Nd_iPr2BA3_demo/Nd_iPr2BA3_axial.pcsp Supplied structure and experimental shift lists; see the interpretation notes below Practice measured-FID processing documentation_demo/Yb_iPr2BA3_demo/PROTON_01.fid/ A measured proton spectrum; use the processing recipe below

docs.title: Interpret the examples
docs.text:
Synthetic examples have known generating assumptions. Their small residuals or successful recovery test those assumptions and the calculation; they do not establish accuracy for an experimental molecule. Follow each tutorial's numerical checkpoints and limitations. The FID/VT teaching signals are simulated spectra, not measured evidence for the toy structure.

The Nd molecular project retains a saved axial tensor and averaging settings. On opening, its G_ax diagnostic uses all assigned visible points, including iPr data. That regression need not reproduce the stored tensor. Contact shifts, conformation and shared/averaged assignments require review before choosing a scientific fitting subset. The project does not restore a historical subset; do not select points solely to improve R². See the dataset notes below.

The Yb acquisition is measured, but its Demo A/B labels are illustrative annotations, not established molecular assignments. Its processing exercise does not validate a PCS model or connect the Yb spectrum to the Nd structure. Available acquisition conditions and processing parameters are recorded below.

PCS Workbench PDE calculations need a matching ORCA tensor/geometry output and spin-density grid. Tensor inspection needs only ORCA; tensor transfer also needs a matching Analyzer document. That pair is not included in these examples; see its input requirements.

docs.title: Nd molecular project
docs.text:
The supplied Nd(iPr₂BA)₃ example contains:

File Contents Nd_iPr2BA3.xyz Pre-aligned 103-atom structure; Nd is Ref 1. Nd_iPr2BA3_paramagnetic_shifts.csv Paramagnetic shifts in ppm, keyed by structure Ref ID and used as δ_Exp. Nd_iPr2BA3_axial.pcsp Embedded structure, assignments, methyl symmetry averaging and phenyl rotational averaging. Nd_iPr2BA3_observed_shifts.csv Observed Nd sample shifts, δ_obs in ppm. La_iPr2BA3_observed_shifts.csv Diamagnetic La reference shifts, δ_dia, with corresponding Ref IDs.

The saved project uses axial prediction, Δχ_ax = −3.90816 E-32 m³, and no rhombic contribution. Three phenyl groups use uniform full rotations with 24 samples per group. All elements and ligands are visible; original/reference overlays are off.

To inspect this case:

  1. Choose File → Open PCS Project... and open examples/documentation_demo/Nd_iPr2BA3_demo/Nd_iPr2BA3_axial.pcsp.
  2. Check 103 raw atoms with Nd at Ref 1 and assigned δ_Exp values in the main table. Do not reimport the CSVs for this prepared-project exercise.
  3. Open G_ax vs PCS to inspect the current diagnostic. Its fitted slope is calculated from the displayed points; it is not the saved −3.90816 tensor value.
  4. Follow Averaging and Visualization to compare representations without refitting the tensor. Save any changes to a new path.

The supplied structure and experimental shift lists have no accompanying publication/CIF identifier or complete experimental-methods record. Establish sample conditions, assignment evidence and diamagnetic-reference suitability before treating them as an experimental benchmark.

The observed-shift pair can also be used in Shift Analysis and PCS Preparation. Blank cells are unassigned; numeric zeros remain data. Direct subtraction is a derivation preview, not evidence that every difference is pure PCS. Inspect assignments, targets and possible contact contributions before fitting.

docs.title: Yb measured FID
docs.text:
Keep fid and procpar together in PROTON_01.fid/. Open that directory through NMR Workbench → Open Dataset Folder…, or its fid through Open FID File…. Launch NMR Workbench from the Tools Ribbon first, then use its File menu. The measured Varian/Agilent acquisition metadata identifies ¹H, approximately 399.9 MHz, benzene-d₆ and 298.15 K. Non-scientific identifiers and system paths were anonymized; raw FID and scientific acquisition parameters were retained, with processing parity checked.

For the documentation spectrum, start with a fresh import and Preview/Apply each operation once in this order:

Operation Parameters Exponential apodization 2 Hz Manual phase P0 = 131.9°, P1 = 1049°, pivot = 0 ppm Baseline arPLS, lambda = 1e9 Positive peak picking Height 2%, prominence 2%, minimum separation 100 points

With these settings, the supplied acquisition gives 17 positive picked peaks. Peak detection does not assign those peaks to molecular sites.

These are dataset-specific processing choices. The vendor ppm reference is retained; no independent calibration, publication identifier or validated molecular assignments are supplied. Demo A/B labels are illustrative only. This Yb processing exercise is separate from the Nd/La PCS example and does not transfer Yb observations to the Nd structure. See FID processing.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer is distributed as a portable Windows application and can also be run from the Python source code. The prebuilt release is Windows-only; source operation on other platforms depends on the local Python, Tk, Qt, and VTK environment and is not verified by the portable-release workflow.

Use the version selector in the documentation header to match your application release. latest refers to the latest published stable manual; dev, when available, describes unreleased work. Archived versions retain their own pages and images. The current source manual targets 1.4.0.

docs.title: Windows portable version
docs.text:
The portable distribution includes its Python runtime and does not require a separate Python installation.

  1. Download the latest Windows release from the PCS Analyzer releases page.
  2. Extract the complete archive to a writable folder.
  3. Run the PCS Analyzer executable from the extracted folder.
  4. Keep the distributed executable, lib, and other bundled folders together.

Do not run the executable from inside the compressed archive.

docs.title: Running from source
docs.text:
Python with Tkinter is required.

git clone https://github.com/boseokhong/PCS-analyzer.git
cd PCS-analyzer
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py

The dependency roles are:

Role Packages Requirement level Core calculations and interface numpy, scipy, matplotlib, pandas, and Python Tkinter Required for the main application and scientific workflows. Excel import/export openpyxl Required for .xlsx input and output; CSV workflows do not use it. NMR vendor data and automatic phasing nmrglue Required for Bruker and Varian/Agilent data import, Bruker digital-filter correction, and NMR Workbench Auto Phase. NMR baseline correction pybaselines Required for NMR Workbench Whittaker baseline methods, including AsLS and arPLS (Auto Baseline). PyVista visualization pyvista, vtk Required by the PyVista-based 3D PCS and Workbench viewers. Qt-backed structure viewer pyvistaqt, qtpy, PySide6 Required when opening the interactive PyVista Qt structure viewer. Chemical Map layout and cleanup rdkit Optional at runtime. Enables CoordGen and RDKit 2D layouts and chemical structure cleanup; Graph 2D remains available without it. Drag and drop tkinterdnd2 Enables drag-and-drop; the application falls back to ordinary Tk when it is unavailable. GIF output imageio Used by PyVista GIF export. Alternate theme engine ttkbootstrap Present in the full dependency set, but the current default UI uses standard ttk styling. FFT acceleration pyfftw Optional at runtime. PCS Workbench falls back to numpy.fft when it is unavailable. Module version and compatibility checks packaging Required for application/plugin version comparison and compatibility checks in the Module Manager.

requirements.txt also installs the optional packages pyfftw and rdkit. Their runtime requirements and fallback behavior are listed above.

docs.title: Structure-file support
docs.text:
The main structure loader accepts:

Format Behavior .xyz Reads standard XYZ, headerless coordinate lists, and several common indexed/atomic-number variants. .out Reads the last Cartesian coordinate block from an ORCA output file. .log Uses the same ORCA coordinate-block parser as .out.

ORCA coordinates in Bohr are converted to Ångström. See Loading Structures for the accepted layouts and parsing details.

docs.title: Portable Windows release
docs.text:
Extract a new release into a separate folder instead of overwriting the current installation. Before removing the old folder, preserve:

lib/app_settings.json
plugins/

Copy those items into the corresponding locations in the new release, start it, and verify settings and plugins before deleting the previous folder.

Update checking is not automatic installation

Help → Check for Updates... compares the installed version with the latest GitHub release and can open the release page. PCS Analyzer does not download, replace, or restart the application automatically.

docs.title: Source checkout
docs.text:
Update the checkout using the Git workflow appropriate for that local repository, then refresh its environment if the requirements changed:

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.text:

docs.title: Interface Overview
docs.text: PCS Analyzer combines molecular coordinates, PCS calculations, experimental data, fitting, diagnostics, and visualization in a multi-document workspace.

docs.title: Main interface
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer main workspace. Area Purpose Menu bar Opens and saves projects/workspaces, exports data, and launches viewers, workbenches, settings, and help. Ribbon Groups project, data, and tool commands; a contextual page follows the selected analysis. Document tabs Switches between separate PCS analyses. Molecular data table Shows visible atoms, transformed coordinates, geometrical factors, calculated PCS, and experimental values for the active document. Analysis area Contains regression, rhombicity diagnostics, fitting, and conformer search. Control Panel Sets tensor, orientation, averaging, visibility, and display options for the active document; also provides tool shortcuts.

Drag the horizontal divider between the table and analysis area to change how much space each receives. Moving it to an edge collapses that area; use the edge divider to restore it. The document tabs remain above the split. The Control Panel normally docks on the right and can also dock on the left.

docs.title: Ribbon
docs.text:
Page Commands Home Load XYZ, Open Project, Save Project, and output actions Save XYZ, Plot Data, Table. Data Import PCS, Export Template, Paste, Undo, Clear; PCS viewers (2D PCS, 3D PCS, Projection) and structure viewers (3D Structure, Chemical Map). Tools Workbenches (NMR and PCS), Modules (Module Manager, Arrange modules and loaded module launchers), then Application (Settings). Contextual page Commands for the selected analysis, such as selection and regression, fitting, or conformer search. Its label follows the outer analysis tab.

Selecting an analysis tab, or returning to its controls, selects the contextual Ribbon page. In Advanced Fitting and Conformer Search, its commands also follow the selected inner tab. Data remains available when another analysis is selected, so importing PCS does not require returning to the regression tab. Unavailable commands appear disabled.

Use the Ribbon chevron or double-click a Ribbon tab to collapse or expand its command area. In narrow windows, More commands ▾ provides access to the commands on that Ribbon page.

The active Ribbon tab has a coloured underline; hovering an inactive tab adds a faint neutral underline without changing the layout. Command groups use short, subtle dividers. The contextual tab reserves enough width for the available analysis names, so switching between long and short names keeps its outline and underline steady. Theme and font changes recalculate that space. The adjacent Undo/Redo controls beside Help use matching 16-pixel mirrored icons (scaled for display DPI). Their background and border appear on hover; keyboard focus retains a solid outline. Disabled controls use neutral grey icons. These presentation states do not change history scope, keyboard shortcuts, or the dropdown commands.

docs.title: Document tabs and active analysis
docs.text:
Click a document tab to make it active. The main table, tensor and orientation controls, experimental PCS assignments, and standard fitting results/history then refer to that document. Save Project and the File export commands use the active document.

  • + creates an empty document. Use it before loading a second raw structure.
  • Open Project opens a .pcsp in a document tab; reopening an already open path activates its existing tab.
  • Load XYZ replaces the structure in the active document. Save existing work first.
  • Drag tabs to reorder them. Use × or middle-click to close a tab; modified documents prompt for a save decision.
  • Right-click a tab for Save, Save As..., Duplicate Document, Project Name..., Tab Color, Close, Close Others, or Close All. An asterisk marks unsaved changes.

Project files (.pcsp) store scientific analysis state. Workspace files (.pcsw) record the project paths and tab arrangement; save the projects before relying on a workspace to reopen them. See Projects and Persistence. File → Open Workspace... replaces the open document set after resolving unsaved changes.

Check the document name in secondary-window titles when comparing analyses. The NMR Workbench retains its PCS-document binding when the main active tab changes; use Rebind to Active PCS Document there when needed. See the NMR Workbench workflow and Chemical Map for assignments and site mapping.

docs.title: Menu bar
docs.text:
Menu Main paths File Load XYZ..., Recent files, Open PCS Project..., Save PCS Project, Save PCS Project As..., Save All; Open Workspace..., Save Workspace, Save Workspace As...; Save current XYZ..., Save plot data..., Save table..., Exit. View 2D PCS Plot, 3D PCS Plot, 3D Structure, Chemical Map, Projection. Modules Module Manager..., PCS Workbench, NMR Workbench, and commands from successfully loaded external plugins. Settings Open settings... for General and Appearance options, including startup viewers, recent files, default inputs, export DPI, theme, and fonts. Help Documentation (F1), Keyboard Shortcuts..., Check for Updates... (checks for a release without installing it), and About PCS Analyzer.

Load XYZ... remains the first File command. New/Close Document are accessed through the document tab's + / × or Ctrl+N / Ctrl+W, rather than File menu entries. Workspace and export commands remain directly available in File.

In Settings → Open settings... → Appearance, Theme determines both the base palette and accent colors. There is no separate Accent color selector.

Available palettes are Light, Dark, and their Teal, Violet and Slate variants. The default is Light. UI font changes affect control sizes and responsive layouts; use the workspace dividers and scrollbars as needed.

Load XYZ... accepts XYZ and supported ORCA .out/.log files despite its label. See Loading Structures, File Formats, and Plugins for details.

docs.title: Molecular data table
docs.text:
The table columns are Ref, Atom, X, Y, Z, G_ax, δ_PCS, and δ_Exp.

  • Ref identifies atoms by structure-file order; filtering does not renumber them.
  • X, Y, and Z are transformed coordinates relative to the PCS centre.
  • G_ax is the axial geometrical factor.
  • δ_PCS follows Prediction model: Axial, or Full tensor with the rhombic term included only when Enable Δχ_rh is on. Polar contours and G_ax vs PCS remain axial diagnostics; see Prediction policy.
  • δ_Exp is the assigned experimental PCS in ppm.

Double-click a δ_Exp cell to enter a value or leave it blank to clear it. Bulk import, template export, paste, undo, and clear actions are on Ribbon → Data → Experimental PCS. The Color toggle and residual threshold legend remain beside the table. See Experimental-data Import and Export.

The table and linked plots share atom selection. Selecting a row highlights its corresponding point in supported open views; clicking a linked atom or point selects and scrolls to its table row. In G_ax vs PCS, Lasso or Box selects a regression subset. Use Fit to fit that subset and Clear Selection to return to all assigned points. A single highlighted atom and a regression subset serve different purposes.

docs.title: Analysis areas
docs.text:
Tab Purpose G_ax vs PCS Axial regression of experimental PCS against the geometrical factor, with an optional forced origin, subset selection, and plot export. Rhombicity Check Examines axial-fit residuals for angular or rhombic trends. Rhombicity Table Compares axial/rhombic factors, predictions, and residuals; contains Enable Δχ_rh, rhombic susceptibility input, and structure Z-axis rotation. Fitting Mode A · Ligand-donor, Mode B · Euler, and Mode C · Full tensor + metal, with input selections, results, and fit history. Advanced Fitting Specialized Multi-Conformer, Joint PCS+RDC, PRE, and Multi-Lanthanide analyses. Conformer Search Structure constraints, search options, candidate results, and preview/apply actions.

Use Fitting Overview for inputs and result application, Rhombicity Diagnostics for interpretation, and Conformer Search for structure-search usage.

In Fitting, use the Fit settings header to hide/show configuration while keeping the recorded Result available. Advanced workspaces have their own input-section collapse and report/plot dividers. Shared actions remain in the contextual Ribbon. Worked examples: Multi-Conformer, Joint PCS+RDC, PRE, and Multi-Lanthanide/Reilley.

docs.title: Control Panel
docs.text:
Sections can be independently expanded or collapsed by clicking their headers. Drag a section's ⠿ handle to reorder it and scroll to reach sections below the visible area. The title-bar dock button switches sides; drag the boundary toward the docked edge to collapse the panel, then click or drag the collapsed boundary to restore it.

Section Controls and interpretation Tensor Δχ_ax in ×10⁻³² m³, tensor status, Details… (Rhombicity Table, or ORCA source details after tensor transfer), and Prediction model. Orientation Structure X/Y controls (Z is in Rhombicity Table) or Tensor Euler (ZYZ) angles: two representations of the molecular-to-tensor orientation. Plot & display PCS range and Interval in ppm, Half / Quarter (0–90°), atom radii/scale, visual bonds, Update, and Reset. Symmetry averaging Current averaging status and Options... for local and rotational averaging. Element visibility Elements and Ligands filters, including all/none actions. These affect the visible table and current analysis, not just appearance. Susceptibility details Molar susceptibility input, auto-calculation, and derived tensor components with display-unit selection. Quick tools User-selected viewer, workbench, and module launchers.

Reset layout restores the section order, expansion state, and default pinned tools. It is distinct from Plot & display → Reset, which resets PCS data and controls. Layout and pinned-tool preferences are application settings shared across documents.

In Quick tools, use the header's settings icon to open Customize Tools. Search available tools, choose which to pin, set their Pinned order with Up/Down, and Apply. Unpinning a tool removes its shortcut; viewers and workbenches remain available from the Data/Tools Ribbon and menus. Plugin launchers are available when registered by loaded plugins.

See Coordinate System, Tensor Conventions, and Symmetry Averaging for the scientific meaning of these controls.

docs.title: Help and keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
Help → Documentation opens the online manual in your default browser. Help → Keyboard Shortcuts... opens a reusable, non-modal reference window with document, navigation, edit-history and help groups. Shortcuts are fixed; this window does not customize bindings. File/View menu entries show their shortcuts on the right.

Shortcut Action Ctrl+N Create a new PCS document tab Ctrl+O Open a .pcsp project Ctrl+S Save the active project; choose a path for its first save Ctrl+Shift+S Save the active project under another name Ctrl+W Close the active document, retaining its unsaved-change prompt Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab Next/previous document in tab order, wrapping at either end Ctrl+Z Undo a document edit Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z Redo a document edit F1 Open Documentation

Document/file/navigation/help shortcuts apply within the main window, including its input controls. They do not trigger from auxiliary windows or while a modal dialog owns the grab. Ctrl+Tab changes document tabs rather than analysis tabs. Entry/text controls retain their local Undo/Redo editing behavior; see document Undo/Redo for its scope. No shortcut is assigned to fitting execution or Reset.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Continue with Quick Start for a first analysis and save/reopen workflow.

docs.title: Plugin Distribution Design Notes
docs.text: These notes retain the v0.1 distribution design direction for plugin authors and maintainers. They are not additional release guarantees. For current behavior, use Module Manager, Installation and distribution, Manifest and PluginApp.

docs.title: Implemented baseline
docs.text: PCS Analyzer currently supports a GitHub-hosted catalog, Browse/Installed/Updates, release downloads with SHA-256 verification, new-package manifest/version and compatibility validation, staged local installation, backup replacement, attempted rollback/removal and visible session/operation diagnostics. register(app) and register_tool() are implemented. Plugins remain unsandboxed, Python dependencies are not resolved, and PluginApp remains unversioned. Updated files require a restart to become the executing code.

docs.title: Distribution responsibilities
docs.text:
The developer repository describes and maintains the plugin: source, tests, issues, documentation, licenses and release assets. The distribution catalog selects which release URL, digest, version and compatibility/lifecycle metadata PCS Analyzer offers. Publishing a developer release does not automatically update that catalog.

For a release, keep the public ID stable and align manifest version, release tag, ZIP name and catalog version. Prefer an explicit release ZIP containing one manifest and its declared entry; include resources and third-party notices. Calculate its SHA-256 from the exact published bytes. Test installation and replacement from a clean application session before requesting catalog inclusion.

Catalog inclusion and labels do not certify security or scientific validity. The software's available categories/lifecycle states are metadata; a formal approval, review or governance policy must be documented separately if adopted.

docs.title: Current interface limits
docs.text: Standalone modules use the current unversioned wrapper. Existing app.state access and descriptive state_access do not implement permission boundaries. There is no implemented API-version negotiation or guaranteed schema stability; see PluginApp before relying on host internals.

docs.title: Author checklist
docs.text: Use the canonical development checklist and manifest field reference. Document supported application versions and optional dependencies, defer work until tool launch, and report errors at the plugin UI boundary. Preserve standalone execution separately when provided. Test source and packaged application environments, including Windows file locks and restart behavior.

docs.title: Projects and Persistence
docs.text: A .pcsp project embeds the structure and PCS analysis inputs needed to continue an analysis. A .pcsw workspace remembers which saved projects to open and which document is active. Tables, figures and XYZ exports serve reporting or exchange; they do not replace a project.

docs.title: Saving a project
docs.text:
Commands are available in File and the Home Ribbon. The active document is the selected document tab; its table, analysis and Control Panel are the ones being saved by Save or Save As.

Command Scope Save PCS Project / Save Project Save the active document to its current .pcsp path; ask for a path if untitled. Save PCS Project As... / Save As Save the active document under a new path. Save All Save every modified project document, asking for paths for modified untitled documents. Cancellation stops the remaining saves; earlier saves remain saved. Save Workspace / Save Workspace As... Save project references and tab order, not unsaved changes within those projects.

Saving is explicit. Save projects before saving their workspace, and keep original structure and experimental source files for independent reproducibility.

docs.title: Tensors from PCS Workbench
docs.text:
Send tensor to PCS Analyzer applies the selected ORCA tensor to the active document as one Undo/Redo action. Save the .pcsp project to retain that tensor and its source information. Ordinary physical edits can show Modified from ORCA in Tensor state; Details retains the original import information.

The Workbench session itself is separate: loaded files, density, calculated field and camera are not saved in the Analyzer project. Keep the source files and Workbench presets/exports needed to reproduce that calculation.

docs.title: Undo and Redo
docs.text:
Use Ctrl+N for a new document, Ctrl+O to open a project, Ctrl+S to save, Ctrl+Shift+S to save under another name, and Ctrl+W to close with the existing unsaved-change prompt. Ctrl+Tab/Ctrl+Shift+Tab navigate document tabs. Help and keyboard shortcuts describes their window scope and reference list.

The two arrow buttons beside Help operate on the active document. Click an arrow to undo or redo one recorded edit; its small dropdown shows the session history. Hovering a row highlights all steps up to that row. Clicking it restores those steps together. The dropdown supports Up/Down, Enter and Escape.

Currently recorded edits are Apply to Tensor for standard Mode B/C, Conformer Search Apply Candidate and Revert, main-table δ_Exp edits, CSV/Excel/clipboard shift-import Apply, δ_Exp/δ_obs/δ_dia Clear, and PCS transfers from NMR Workbench. Confirmed Δχ_ax/Δχ_rh edits, rhombic enablement, Structure XYZ and Tensor Euler ZYZ edits, and explicit metal-centre assignment are recorded as well. Main-window XYZ/ORCA structure loading is recorded as one coupled structure/data edit. The existing Undo import command is also recorded. Control Panel Reset is recorded as one document action, including the standard Fit History that Reset clears. Selecting Axial or Full tensor (Axial + Rhombic) in the Control Panel is one recorded edit. Undo/Redo restores the selected model and refreshes its PCS table, plots and open NMR predictions. The stored tensor parameters and rhombic enablement are retained; Full tensor uses the rhombic term only when that term is enabled. Finish pending tensor/orientation edits before selecting a different model. Selecting the current model does not add history. Observations, uncertainties, provenance and prior import buffers are restored with their corresponding values. Mode A retains its existing geometry-preview workflow. Fit History and Conformer Search result records remain available when an application is undone. Reset retains its existing standard Fit History clearing behavior; Undo restores those records. Redo restores recorded values; it does not rerun fitting or search.

Fitting Preview Geometry and Clear Preview are separate recorded actions. Preview redraws immediately. Mode A/B retain current tensor strengths; Mode C uses fitted Δχ input values as well as its temporary orientation/refined centre. Undoing Preview restores the previous geometry and tensor values. Clear Preview removes only temporary geometry and keeps current tensor settings; Undo restores the removed preview. Assigned-centre coordinates and raw atoms are not replaced. Stored fit reports remain available, with their existing validity checks.

Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y (also Ctrl+Shift+Z) invoke document Undo/Redo outside text and entry controls. Those controls retain their own editing shortcuts. Finish or cancel pending tensor/orientation input edits before using document Undo/Redo. Changes to scientific inputs outside the recorded history can block restoration; the next recorded Apply starts a new history boundary.

Each document keeps up to 100 edits in memory. New edits after Undo discard the redo branch. Saving keeps the current scientific state, but does not serialize the session history. Closing and reopening a project starts with an empty history. Zoom, row/plot selection and residual-colour display settings are not recorded here. Other import workflows are outside this history scope.

Structure loading first reads and validates the file and requested centre. Cancel or a parsing/centre error leaves the working document unchanged. A successful replacement starts a new Ref domain and clears the previous PCS shift layers, structured observations, transfer provenance/import buffers, rotational groups and incompatible temporary geometry. Undo restores those values with the old structure, assigned centre and visibility; the canonical tensor and recorded fit/search reports are retained. Redo uses the embedded accepted values even if the input file has since moved or been deleted. Recent-file entries remain a session log, and row selections are cleared during replacement/restoration.

Confirm Δχ_ax with Enter or Update (leaving an edited field also confirms it). Enter confirmation works while Plot & display is collapsed; keypad Enter uses the same confirmation command. With a Mode C geometry preview active, a confirmed Δχ_ax edit also changes its working preview tensor value while retaining its centre/orientation and the original recorded fit. Undo restores both values. Confirm Δχ_rh through its existing Apply/Update action. Confirm orientation with Enter or by leaving the field. A pointer drag across an orientation slider is one history entry; keyboard steps are individual edits. Switching documents or starting another recorded operation finishes any held drag in its original document.

Reset clears the main working structure/Refs/centre, coupled shift inputs, temporary geometry and structure-specific rotational groups, restores the configured axial/range defaults and returns to the axial prediction policy. Undo also restores the previous range entries, visibility, rotational enablement and standard Fit History. Advanced-tool inputs/options/results and recorded Conformer Search candidates remain separate. Opening the app does not create a Reset history item. If fit records are subsequently imported or otherwise changed outside edit history, restoring Reset is blocked to avoid overwriting those records.

To change the assigned metal centre, right-click a raw atom row in the main table and choose Set Ref … as metal center (clear preview). The coordinates come from that Ref's absolute raw position in Å, not the displayed rotated table coordinates. This action clears any geometry preview without deleting fit/search results. Undo restores the previous assigned centre and preview together.

Undoing an NMR-to-PCS transfer changes the PCS destination, not the source NMR session or its historical transfer receipts. Redo restores the recorded PCS data without rereading source files or repeating preparation. Clearing or editing legacy δ_Exp does not change the existing precedence of structured observations.

docs.title: Opening a project
docs.text:
Choose File → Open PCS Project.... The embedded structure can be opened without the original XYZ/ORCA file; its recorded source path is provenance. Drag-and-drop is also available when the optional drag-and-drop support is installed (only the first file of a multi-file drop is processed).

After opening, verify the assigned centre, tensor/prediction model, experimental targets, visibility and averaging. Dependent tables and plots are recalculated; a project is not an exact restoration of every open window.

docs.title: What the current project restores
docs.text:
Analysis state Restored Structure and centre Original/working coordinates, Ref IDs, assigned metal Ref and position. Tensor and orientation Δχ_ax, Δχ_rh, rhombic enablement, Axial/Full prediction model and equivalent XYZ orientation, including orientation entered as Tensor Euler ZYZ. Experimental data δ_Exp, δ_obs, δ_dia and structured PCS observations, including grouped targets, uncertainties and source information. Averaging and visibility Local symmetry and rotational settings/groups; element and ligand filters. Residual colouring Shared main/Rhombicity Table cutoffs and Color state. Invalid or missing cutoffs use 0.10/0.30 ppm; missing Color defaults to off. These settings affect classification only. Standard fitting Mode, fit options, initialization and weighting; complete Fit History runs, labels and inspected/latest run references. Selecting fit-list rows remains transient. Conformer Search Embedded input geometry/PCS, recorded search conditions, candidate coordinates and metrics, original reports, fixed/bond selections, displayed candidate and queued preview. An explicitly applied candidate stays applied; reopening never applies a pending candidate. Geometry preview Active Mode A/B/C preview. Mode C retains its XYZ degree orientation, absolute metal centre in Å and preview tensor values separately from the assigned metal position. Multi-Conformer fitting Explicit mappings, per-file geometry/metal/frame, inclusion and initial/fixed populations, selected observations, fit conditions and the last recorded result with all attempted starts and contributions. Optional reliability evaluation retains its assumptions, bootstrap/fold runs, intervals and group suggestions. Imported pending mappings remain pending. Joint PCS+RDC RDC Ref pairs/labels and errors, selected PCS observations, field/temperature/weighting settings and the last verified recorded result, including its detached execution inputs and diagnostics. Reopening does not refit or apply the tensor. PRE Proton Γ₂ observations and uncertainties, field/moment/preset/bounds/error settings and the last verified recorded result with detached execution inputs. Reopening neither refits nor changes the main tensor. Multi-Lanthanide Typed PCS/δ_para datasets, Ref mapping, inclusion, conditions and verified recorded results per analysis, including the recorded coefficient identity. Loading validates by deterministic linear replay without installing a new run or applying a tensor. Principal display settings PCS levels/domain and supported structure, projection and PCS-field controls; live plots are regenerated.

For the molecular viewer, .pcsp restores Element/PCS color mode and atom-label visibility. Appearance, PCS palette/range, axes and Figure options are saved separately through File → Visualization settings in the viewer. That JSON file does not save a structure or camera. Atom size and bond tolerance remain shared main-application display controls. See 3D Structure Viewer for the settings scope.

Stored fit reports retain their original parameters and per-observation predictions; they are not refitted on load. Check Current, Stale or Unknown before applying them. Restoring a report does not automatically apply its tensor. See Fit History.

For a prepared example that saves a Multi-Conformer fit and its reliability record, see the Multi-Conformer tutorial.

docs.title: State that is transient or only partially restored
docs.text:
State Limitation Live interaction Open windows, positions, zoom/hover, row/plot selections and import undo are not restored. Search history The latest Conformer Search candidate set is retained, not a history of every search. Older projects containing only scalar search summaries cannot reconstruct candidates. General preferences Theme, fonts, recent files, startup defaults, ribbon module order and plugin settings are separate application settings. Export-DPI values recorded in a project are not reapplied by the current loader.

Current projects restore an active Mode C preview without refitting or applying the result to the canonical tensor. In older files that saved only the preview mode/enabled flag, the missing centre and orientation cannot be reconstructed; the incomplete preview is disabled. Inspect the saved run and use Preview again if its status allows. Apply Tensor retains the assigned metal centre; it does not adopt the refined position. Main predictions after applying a Mode C result can therefore differ from the original fit report. Record whether a figure used this temporary preview, including its refined centre, and retain the corresponding fit-run JSON.

docs.title: NMR work is saved separately
docs.text: Use NMR Workbench → VT Series → Manage VT Series… → Files → Save NMR session… for a recoverable .nmrsession, including single-temperature and prepared-data work. It retains session-owned committed spectra, processing, peaks, observations and series/tracking evidence where present. A .pcsp can retain handed-off PCS observations, but does not restore the complete NMR workflow. Read-only PCS-project shift projections remain owned by the PCS project. Save both files when continuing both analyses. See NMR Sessions.

docs.title: Workspaces are project references
docs.text:
A .pcsw contains the ordered paths to saved projects and the active project reference. It embeds no structure, fit results, NMR acquisition or unsaved scientific changes. Modified untitled documents must first be saved as projects; empty untitled tabs are omitted. Modified projects with existing paths must also be saved separately to preserve their latest changes.

Open Workspace... replaces the current document set after resolving unsaved changes. Missing projects are reported and skipped; an invalid available project prevents replacement. Nearby files use relative references where possible; files on another drive or farther away may use absolute paths. Relative paths are resolved from the workspace folder. Share the projects with the workspace and preserve their folder layout; a workspace file alone is not portable data.

docs.title: Compatibility behavior
docs.text:
Older supported project sections are loaded with defaults for missing options; verify prediction model and averaging when exchanging projects across versions. Older complete standard results can become history entries; summary-only records cannot recover full reports. Malformed optional history is reported rather than shown as a valid result.

Best-effort loading is not a guarantee of identical behavior across releases. Keep backups, record the application version and review recalculated outputs. Prefer application controls to editing project files by hand.

See File Formats and reproducibility and Quick Start.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Start a PCS analysis with your own molecular structure and experimental PCS values. This guide takes you from loading the files to an initial diagnostic and a saved project. For installation, see Installation.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Prepare:

  • a molecular structure in XYZ or supported ORCA .out/.log format;
  • the identity of the paramagnetic centre; and
  • experimental PCS values in ppm, with assignments to atoms in that structure.

δ_Exp means experimental PCS, not an absolute observed chemical shift. If you have paramagnetic and diamagnetic shifts instead, start with Observed and Diamagnetic Shifts. For raw FIDs, use the NMR Workbench first.

Need practice data? The examples guide lists starting files and expected results. A prepared .pcsp already contains its structure and saved settings: open it with File → Open PCS Project..., then follow its tutorial instead of repeating the raw-data preparation below.

docs.title: 1. Open the application and load your structure
docs.text:
Start the portable executable, or run python main.py from the source root. Choose Home → Load XYZ on the Ribbon or File → Load XYZ.... The chooser accepts XYZ and supported ORCA .out/.log files despite the command name. For ORCA, the last recognized Cartesian-coordinate block is loaded.

Loading replaces the structure in the active document. To keep an existing analysis, save it and click + in the document tab strip before loading another structure.

See Loading Structures if your file is not recognized.

docs.title: 2. Assign and check the centre
docs.text:
In Input center atom, enter the element label as written in the file, for example Nd. The first exact match becomes the PCS centre.

Check its Ref ID in the main table. If the structure contains several atoms with that label, right-click the intended raw atom row and choose Set Ref … as metal center (clear preview).

Ref IDs follow structure-file order, starting from 1. Keep that ordering when preparing assignments; the same Ref number in another structure need not refer to the same atom. Use Control Panel → Element visibility → Elements to show the nuclei needed for the analysis. Filtering does not renumber them.

docs.title: 3. Import your experimental PCS values
docs.text:
Use the table template to avoid ambiguous atom-label matching:

  1. On Data → Experimental PCS, choose Export Template.
  2. Save CSV or XLSX and fill the δ_Exp column in ppm. Preserve Ref values.
  3. Choose Import PCS and select the completed file.
  4. Review the mapped Ref IDs, values and proposed actions in the preview.
  5. Select the intended rows and choose Apply.

For a few values, double-click individual δ_Exp cells. Paste is also available; see Import and Export for its formats and mapping rules.

Checkpoint: the intended visible rows contain your PCS values on the correct Ref IDs. Blank and zero are different: blank means unassigned; zero is data.

For exchange-averaged or grouped observations, review structured targets before entering the same resonance on several atom rows. Group members are not additional independent measurements.

docs.title: 4. Check the model and coordinate frame
docs.text:
For an initial axial diagnostic, select Control Panel → Tensor → Prediction model → Axial. If you already have Δχ_ax, enter it in units of 10⁻³² m³ per molecule and press Enter. Check external values against Tensor Conventions.

The Orientation controls define the structure relative to the tensor frame. An axial diagnostic is meaningful only for the orientation being examined; the default orientation is not an estimate of your sample's tensor direction. If orientation is unknown, use orientation fitting with enough independent observations.

Check symmetry and torsional averaging if your assignments represent exchanging groups. PCS range, Interval and the Half/Quarter polar view adjust the display; they do not fit the tensor.

docs.title: 5. Inspect the initial diagnostic
docs.text:
Select G_ax vs PCS. With at least two suitable visible assignments, the all-point regression updates automatically. It estimates an axial susceptibility from the slope for the current geometry/frame; it does not apply that estimate to the main tensor.

  • Check the point count against the observations you intended to analyze.
  • Inspect the line, intercept and residuals. Use Force origin only when justified by your model.
  • Select a table row or plotted point to check its Ref ID and values.
  • If inspecting a scientifically justified subset, use Lasso or Box, then Fit. Clear Selection returns to all assigned points.

A poor correlation can reflect orientation, assignments, non-PCS contributions, structural differences or averaging. A high R² alone does not validate those assumptions. See Residual Analysis.

docs.title: 6. Choose further analysis if needed
docs.text:
Your question Continue with What tensor orientation best matches my PCS? Standard fitting, especially Mode B Do axial residuals suggest a missing rhombic contribution? Rhombicity Diagnostics Do I need to refine the metal position as well? Full Tensor Fitting How do I compare conformers or combine other observables? Advanced workflows

For standard fitting, refresh the inputs, select the required PCS observations and choose the mode before Run Fit. Mode A also needs donor atoms. Review the report and residuals before using Apply Tensor or Preview; running a fit alone does not apply its tensor. The Fitting Overview explains the different application/preview behavior of each mode.

docs.title: 7. Save and reopen your project
docs.text:
Choose Home → Save Project or File → Save PCS Project (Ctrl+S). Save to .pcsp; keep your original structure and experimental files alongside it as source data. Use Save PCS Project As... when you want a separate copy.

Reopen with File → Open PCS Project... and check the centre, assignments, tensor/frame, averaging and diagnostic point count. A project restores analysis data and supported results, not every open window or selection. See Projects and Persistence for save/reopen scope. NMR work also requires its own .nmrsession.

To retain a set of document tabs, save their projects first and then save a workspace. A .pcsw contains references to those projects, not embedded data.

If you get stuck, see Troubleshooting. For the terms used here, see the Glossary.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with the section matching your current task. When asking for help, include the application version, file type, exact message and the steps leading to it. Use a small shareable input when possible; remove personal paths or confidential sample information from reports.

docs.title: My structure does not load
docs.text: Use File → Load XYZ... for .xyz or supported ORCA .out/.log files. XYZ rows need an element and three numeric coordinates. For conventional XYZ, keep the comment line after the atom-count line even when it is blank. ORCA input needs a recognized Cartesian-coordinate block; the last one is used. See Loading Structures for other accepted row layouts.

docs.title: The wrong atom is the centre
docs.text: The loading dialog matches the element label exactly and uses its first occurrence. Check capitalization and the Ref ID. To choose another raw atom, right-click its table row and use Set Ref … as metal center (clear preview). Canceling the loading dialog leaves the working document unchanged.

docs.title: Experimental values appear on the wrong atoms
docs.text: Export a fresh Data → Export Template from the loaded structure and preserve its Ref column. Ref IDs follow file order; they are not portable between differently ordered structures. Review mapped IDs and skipped rows before Apply. Repeated element labels make atom-label-only matching ambiguous. See Import and Export.

docs.title: The G_ax plot is empty or has the wrong point count
docs.text:
Check that numeric δ_Exp values are present and the relevant elements are visible. The all-point regression needs at least two suitable points. Use Clear Selection if an old Lasso/Box subset is active.

Grouped PCS observations need not appear as separate δ_Exp cells for each atom. Inspect the Fitting PCS observations list and the structured-target explanation.

docs.title: Rhombicity Check has no diagnostic plots
docs.text: Load the structure, provide δ_Exp and establish the orientation, then choose Update Diagnostic. It needs at least three valid points and uses a selection from Fitting when present. See Rhombicity Diagnostics.

docs.title: A fit rejects my inputs or the result looks implausible
docs.text:
In standard Fitting, choose Refresh, check Mode details and select the required PCS observations. Mode A also requires donor atoms. There must be enough independent observations to constrain the chosen parameters; the fact that a run starts does not establish sufficiency.

Check the centre, assignments, orientation, tensor units, averaging and possible non-PCS contributions. Inspect residuals and compare starting assumptions rather than accepting a result from R² alone. See Fitting Overview and Quality Metrics.

docs.title: Apply is unavailable or the result is Stale
docs.text: Stale means the recorded result no longer matches the relevant working inputs. Review the changes and rerun with the intended data. Unknown means validity could not be established. Do not substitute a historical report for a new fit. Standard fitting mode and advanced workflow also determine what can be applied; see Fit History and the relevant workflow tutorial.

docs.title: The main tensor did not change after Run Fit
docs.text: Running a fit records a result. Applying it or previewing its geometry is a separate action, and the fields transferred depend on the mode. See Running and applying a fit.

docs.title: A viewer does not open when running from source
docs.text: Read the error and check the dependency table in Installation. The Qt-backed structure viewer needs PySide6, qtpy and pyvistaqt; PyVista viewers also need VTK. Install dependencies in the Python environment actually launching PCS Analyzer. Optional viewer support and main calculations have different requirements. Preserve the complete folder layout of a portable installation.

docs.title: Reopening a file did not restore my whole session
docs.text:
.pcsp saves the supported PCS analysis state; .pcsw references saved projects; .nmrsession saves NMR work. A workspace alone contains neither embedded projects nor unsaved changes. See Projects and Persistence and NMR Sessions before choosing what to save.

For module installation or loading errors, use Module Troubleshooting. Other known scientific and workflow limits are listed in Current Limitations.

docs.title: Conformer Search Constraints
docs.text: Conformer Search combines molecular-graph rules with soft numerical penalties. These mechanisms restrict a search, but they are not a force field and do not prove that a candidate is chemically stable.

docs.title: Connectivity and rotatable bonds
docs.text:
The tool first builds a graph from interatomic distances and covalent radii. The default cutoff is 1.30 times the sum of the two covalent radii. Automatic metal connectivity is deliberately conservative:

  • recognized N, O, F, P, S, Cl, Br, I, As, and Se contacts may be retained as metal–donor bonds;
  • metal–carbon and metal–metal contacts are skipped by default; and
  • other close metal contacts that do not pass the donor policy appear under ⚠ Skipped contacts.

In ② Rotatable bonds, use the contextual Ribbon's Remove Bond to mark a detected connection as false and Add Bond to supply missing connectivity. Manual removal overrides automatic detection, and manual addition can restore a contact rejected by the automatic policy. Rebuilding connectivity also rebuilds the rotatable-bond list and lock state.

A detected bond is offered as rotatable only when it joins two non-hydrogen atoms, is not a ring bond, has a neighbour on each side, and does not include the metal. Metal-mediated paths are excluded from ring detection. This is a topology rule, not a bond-order or electronic-structure analysis.

docs.title: Fixed atoms and bond locking
docs.text:
The metal is always fixed implicitly. User-selected atoms in ① Fixed atoms influence which dihedrals remain available and add a numerical constraint in the objective.

With Anchor mode (recommended for tetrapodal/tripodal ligands) enabled, a fixed atom directly at the rotating-side anchor can remain the pivot while the arm beyond it rotates. A fixed atom deeper in the rotating subtree locks the bond. With Anchor mode disabled, any fixed atom in the rotating subtree, including the directly bonded anchor, locks the bond. The latter is stricter and can leave no free dihedrals.

The local Filter element selector and contextual Ribbon Fix All Shown, Unfix All, and Invert actions only change which atoms are marked. Use Ribbon → Apply Locks to recalculate and inspect the lock classification before running.

docs.title: Position mode
docs.text:
For Constraint model: position, the objective adds a large quadratic penalty for Cartesian displacement of fixed atoms from their input coordinates. Bond locking is the primary protection; the positional term is a soft numerical backstop.

Position mode is appropriate when the selected atoms should remain at the same XYZ positions. It does not restrain every unselected atom, perform geometry optimization, or enforce experimental distance restraints.

docs.title: Angular mode
docs.text:
For Constraint model: angular, each fixed atom is represented by its unit direction from the metal. The objective penalizes changes in those directions while allowing the metal–atom radii to change. It also penalizes non-hydrogen atoms within the coordination search region when their metal distance falls below an element-dependent lower bound derived from covalent radii and donor offsets.

Angular mode therefore preserves selected metal-centred directions, not exact Cartesian positions or exact metal–donor distances. Radial changes are reported as diagnostics. Only atoms marked fixed contribute a directional constraint; the short-distance coordination screen is broader and applies to nearby non-hydrogen atoms.

docs.title: Rigid-body anchor constraints
docs.text:
In Rigid-body anchor rotation, fixed atoms other than the metal are used as anchors. Axis mode defines the metal-centred rotation axis:

Axis mode Axis construction first Metal-to-first-anchor direction. bisector Normalized sum of the metal-to-anchor unit directions; with one anchor it reduces to first. connecting First-anchor to second-anchor direction, shifted to pass through the metal; with fewer than two anchors it falls back to first.

Lock mode determines which coordinates can change:

Lock mode Preserved behavior rigid_with_axis All non-metal atoms, including the anchors, rotate together as one rigid body around the axis. angular_only Anchor Cartesian coordinates remain fixed; all other non-metal atoms rotate around the anchor-defined axis. angular_radial_free Anchor directions from the metal remain fixed, their radii are fitted within Radial bounds rel., and the other non-metal atoms rotate.

The radial bounds are multiplicative factors of each initial metal–anchor distance. The rigid-body objective also includes clash and short metal-contact penalties. The dihedral Constraint model selection is not used by this branch.

docs.title: Clash and geometry penalties
docs.text:
The clash term is a smooth quadratic penalty for close non-bonded atom pairs based on van der Waals radii. Bonded and graph-near pairs are excluded from the normal clash screen. A final integer clash count is reported with each candidate.

The clash and coordination terms are heuristic search penalties. They do not include electronic energy, solvent, bond stretching energy, conformational entropy, or a complete treatment of coordination chemistry. A zero clash count is therefore a useful screen, not evidence that the geometry is a physical minimum.

See Optimization for how these penalties combine with the PCS residual objective.

docs.title: Conformer Search Optimization
docs.text: Conformer Search minimizes a bounded, composite objective. The tensor parameters, tensor orientation, metal position, and experimental PCS values remain fixed while structural variables change.

docs.title: Dihedral torsion search
docs.text: Each selected free bond contributes one dihedral variable bounded from −180° to +180°. Applying a variable rotates the graph subtree on the side away from the metal when that side is identifiable; otherwise the smaller subtree rotates. Bond lengths, bond angles, and ring coordinates are not independently optimized.

docs.title: Rigid-body anchor rotation
docs.text: The principal variable is a rotation angle φ from −180° to +180° around the selected metal-centred axis. With angular_radial_free, one additional bounded radial variable is added for each anchor. The default relative radial interval is 0.8–1.2 times the initial metal–anchor distance.

docs.title: Composite objective
docs.text:
The base data term is the unweighted sum of squared PCS residuals:

\[ S_{\mathrm{PCS}} = \sum_i\left(\delta_{i,\mathrm{calc}}-\delta_{i,\mathrm{Exp}}\right)^2. \]

The optimizer then adds applicable heuristic terms:

  • a non-bonded clash penalty in both search modes;
  • a fixed-atom Cartesian penalty in dihedral Position mode;
  • fixed-direction and short metal-contact penalties in dihedral Angular mode; and
  • anchor-direction and short metal-contact penalties in the applicable rigid-body lock modes.

The final search score is therefore not a pure experimental χ², physical energy, or probability. It has no uncertainty weighting and should not be compared numerically with fit statistics from an unrelated workflow.

docs.title: Dihedral search stages
docs.text:
When Use global search (Differential Evolution) is enabled, the dihedral workflow runs:

  1. SciPy differential evolution over every selected angle in the full −180° to +180° bounds; then
  2. bounded SciPy L-BFGS-B local refinement of low-cost members from the final population.

Optimization level selects Quick, Balanced, or Thorough differential-evolution iteration and population settings. Editing DE iterations or Population size selects Custom. The current search uses a fixed random seed, so otherwise identical inputs and settings are intended to be repeatable.

If global search is disabled, local refinement starts only from the input dihedral vector. That path explores a local basin and currently supplies only one starting point, even if Output mode: top_n requests more candidates. Local refinement cannot be assumed to find the global minimum.

docs.title: Rigid-body search stages
docs.text:
Rigid-body mode does not use differential evolution. It scans φ on the number of Grid steps specified by the user, selects one or more low-cost grid starts, and refines each with bounded L-BFGS-B. The global-search checkbox and DE iteration/population controls apply to dihedral mode, not this rigid-body branch.

A finer grid samples the periodic rotation more densely but does not add other rigid-body degrees of freedom. The local stage can still converge several starts to the same minimum.

docs.title: Candidate ranking and deduplication
docs.text:
Local results are sorted by the complete objective, including penalties. The interface then reports PCS RMSD, R², Q factor, clashes, constraint drift, and per-atom residuals for interpretation. A candidate with the lowest PCS RMSD need not have the lowest composite objective if it incurs a geometry penalty.

With Output mode: top_n, Top N limits the retained list and Min. angle difference [deg] removes near-duplicate solutions. Dihedral candidates are compared component by component in their stored angle vectors; the current dihedral deduplication does not wrap +180° and −180° as neighbouring values. Rigid-body φ deduplication does use periodic angle differences.

These candidates are alternative local solutions from one search, not a statistically sampled conformer ensemble. Their ordering does not supply populations or confidence intervals.

docs.title: Comparison and export
docs.text:
The Results tab retains the candidate list and report. Its contextual Ribbon provides View, Select, Correlation, Save XYZ, Save Report and candidate Apply / Revert / Discard actions. This workflow supports:

  • a text report for the active candidate;
  • a calculated-versus-experimental PCS plot and residual bars;
  • a polar structure comparison of the original and up to five candidates;
  • selection of a candidate for main-window preview/application;
  • a multi-model XYZ containing the checked candidates; and
  • a TXT report for the active candidate.

The structure comparison can be saved as PNG, PDF, or SVG. The exported XYZ records candidate rank, RMSD, and R² in each model comment. Review the coordinates and diagnostics directly; an optimized score alone does not validate the chemical structure.

For metric definitions, see Fit-quality Metrics. For the distinction between structural search and tensor fitting, return to the Conformer Search overview.

docs.title: Conformer Search
docs.text:
Applying or reverting a conformer is recorded in the active document's Undo/Redo history. Undo restores the previous working structure while keeping search candidates and their recorded reports. Revert to the original structure remains a separate action; its own change can also be undone. The session history is not saved in project files.

Conformer Search changes molecular coordinates to find structures whose calculated PCS values agree with the current experimental PCS data. It uses the current metal position, susceptibility tensor, and tensor orientation as fixed calculation inputs; it does not refit those quantities. The result is therefore a structural search under the supplied PCS model, not an alternative to tensor fitting.

The tool is available in the main analysis notebook as 🔍 Conformer Search. Its embedded workflow has four tabs: ① Fixed atoms, ② Rotatable bonds, ③ Run & Options, and ④ Results.

The contextual Conformer Search Ribbon follows the selected inner tab. Shared actions are on that Ribbon; the analysis area retains input controls, candidate tables and reports. The standalone tool can still show its original local buttons. The instructions below describe the embedded workflow.

docs.title: Search and constraint choices
docs.text:
Two separate choices define a search:

Choice Options Meaning Search mode Dihedral torsion search Varies selected rotatable-bond dihedral angles while preserving the bond lengths, bond angles, and ring geometry implied by the input structure. Rigid-body anchor rotation Rotates a rigid molecular fragment around a metal-centred axis defined by selected anchor atoms. This is intended for closed chelates or other rigid fragments without a useful free dihedral. Constraint model for a dihedral search position Keeps fixed atoms near their original Cartesian positions. angular Keeps the metal-centred directions of fixed atoms while allowing radial changes, and penalizes short metal–atom contacts.

Rigid-body search uses its own Axis mode and Lock mode controls rather than the dihedral Constraint model. See Constraints for exactly what each option preserves.

docs.title: Inputs inherited from PCS Analyzer
docs.text:
Before using Conformer Search Ribbon → Sync Main, the main window must contain:

  • a loaded structure;
  • experimental δ_Exp values matched to structure Ref IDs;
  • a valid metal assignment and metal coordinates; and
  • the tensor magnitude, rhombic component, and orientation intended for the comparison.

Syncing creates an internal conventional XYZ representation and a Ref, δ_exp PCS table for the search. Only Ref IDs that have δ_Exp values are included. The PCS terminology and matching rules are described in Experimental PCS and Import and Export.

Orientation convention in the embedded hand-off

Sync Main converts the main window's active extrinsic XYZ orientation to the search calculator's intrinsic ZYZ representation while preserving the same molecular-to-tensor rotation matrix. The displayed angle numbers can differ; the physical orientation is unchanged. Raw molecular coordinates and the metal position remain in the same absolute frame. Standalone search inputs and --euler-zyz still use ZYZ. Earlier source versions copied XYZ numbers directly, so rerun searches made with nonzero orientations in those versions. See Coordinate Handling and Tensor Conventions.

docs.title: End-to-end workflow
docs.text:
1. Load the structure and experimental data in the main window, assign the metal centre, and set the tensor inputs.
  2. Open 🔍 Conformer Search, select ③ Run & Options, and choose Sync Main on its contextual Ribbon. Review the imported structure, PCS point count, metal position, tensor, and orientation summary.
  3. In ① Fixed atoms, mark donor or rigid-core atoms that should constrain the search. The metal is fixed implicitly. Choose Ribbon → Apply Locks to rebuild and inspect the lock classification.
  4. For Dihedral torsion search, review the automatically detected bonds in ② Rotatable bonds, correct false or missing connectivity if necessary, and select the free bonds to vary. For Rigid-body anchor rotation, the selected fixed atoms other than the metal become the anchor list.
  5. In ③ Run & Options, choose the search mode, constraints, optimization level, and candidate output settings. Choose Ribbon → Run Search.
  6. In ④ Results, compare candidate metrics and the per-atom PCS report. Ribbon → View overlays the original and up to five candidates in a 0–180° or folded 0–90° polar structure view. Correlation shows calculated-versus-experimental PCS and residuals.
  7. Use Ribbon → Select to send a chosen result to the main window as a preview. Apply commits the preview to the current raw structure; Discard removes the preview without changing the current structure; Revert restores the initially loaded structure.
  8. Use Ribbon → Save XYZ for selected candidates and Save Report for the active text report. Save the structure comparison from Save figure… in its viewer.

Applying a candidate updates the current raw geometry and recalculates the effective representation when symmetry or torsional averaging is active. Current projects retain the latest candidate set, reports, search inputs and selection state without needing the original temporary XYZ/CSV files. Reopening restores results without rerunning the search or applying a pending preview. Changed host inputs disable Apply while results remain available for review/export. Older summary-only projects cannot reconstruct candidates. See Projects and Persistence.

docs.title: What the result means
docs.text:
Changing the current search's tensor/centre, constraints, fixed/bond selection or manual connectivity blocks Apply for an older result. Execution settings such as iteration count alone do not invalidate an existing candidate. Sync Main explicitly replaces inputs and clears the old set; save/export it first.

The candidate report provides RMSD, R², Q factor, per-atom calculated PCS and residuals, clash counts, and constraint diagnostics. Candidate generation and ranking also include geometry penalties, so a candidate is not ranked by PCS RMSD alone. The reported metrics describe agreement under the fixed tensor and selected structural model; they do not establish a unique conformation or a thermodynamic population.

See Optimization for the objective and search stages, and Fit-quality Metrics for the definitions of the PCS metrics.

docs.title: Tutorial: One-bond Conformer Search
docs.text: Use examples/conformer_search_demo/ from the source checkout or portable release. This nine-atom synthetic teaching fragment demonstrates structural search, not chemically optimized conformers or population fitting. Read the search overview first. Short paths below are relative to examples/conformer_search_demo/; see finding the example files.

docs.title: Inputs and fixed conditions
docs.text: demo.pcsp contains start.xyz geometry and three target H PCS observations at Refs 6–8. truth.xyz rotates the terminal fragment by +45° about Ref 3–4. The metal remains at the origin, Δχ_ax=12 and Δχ_rh=3 E-32 m³. Orientation is zero, and Sync Main preserves the same rotation in the search's ZYZ representation.

docs.title: Run the search
docs.text:
1. Use File → Open PCS Project... to open demo.pcsp, select Conformer Search → Run & Options, and choose Sync Main in the contextual Ribbon. Confirm three observations, zero orientation and tensor 12 / 3.
  2. In Fixed atoms, fix Refs 1 and 9, then apply the locks. Use dihedral search, Position constraints and Anchor mode off.
  3. In Rotatable bonds, select only Ref 3–4, clearing other detected bonds.
  4. In Run & Options, use global DE, max iterations 80, population 8, workers 1 and three candidates. Choose Run Search.
  5. Inspect candidate views, correlation and report. Expect about +45° change, RMSD below 0.0001 ppm, no detected clashes and unchanged fixed atoms.
  6. Export with Save XYZ or Save Report. Apply/Revert are explicit actions; running the search does not automatically replace main geometry.

To inspect locking, temporarily fix terminal H Ref 6 and reapply locks; the selected bond should become locked. Restore the original fixed set before running. Candidate count/order can vary after angular deduplication. A small residual does not establish chemical stability or a unique structure.

For Position constraints, verify Cartesian Max fixed-atom drift. Angular drift excludes zero-length metal-centred vectors because their direction is undefined. Cartesian and radial diagnostics still include those atoms. If no valid directions remain, the angular summary is zero; it does not establish a defined orientation for an atom at the metal.

For nonzero orientation, review the orientation conversion. Do not use the truth geometry as the search's starting input.

Actual reopened position-constrained search result: one free bond, three PCS observations, 45° change and negligible Cartesian and angular fixed-atom drift.

docs.title: Save and resume candidates
docs.text:
After searching, save a new .pcsp copy, close its document and reopen the copy. The latest candidate list, reports, displayed candidate and pending preview are restored with embedded geometry and PCS inputs. Temporary Sync Main files are not required. Reopening does not rerun optimization or apply a pending candidate.

Viewing a candidate report and queueing a candidate with Select are separate actions; both states are retained. Use Select to queue the intended candidate before Apply. An already applied structure remains applied after reopening, and Revert still returns to the stored original structure. Changing main structure, PCS, metal or tensor conditions, or changing the search's scientific controls/constraints/connectivity, disables Apply for the recorded search; results remain available for export. Current graph edits are retained separately from the graph used for the recorded run. Sync Main replaces search inputs and clears the previous candidate set/queued preview; save or export first. Then run deliberately for new inputs.

Only the latest search set is retained. Save separate project copies or exports to retain multiple searches. Older files with only RMSD/Q/clash summaries lack the coordinates needed to reconstruct candidates.

docs.title: Residual Analysis
docs.text: PCS Analyzer exposes residuals in several views. They do not all use the same sign, threshold, or model, so identify the workflow before comparing values.

docs.title: Residual definitions by workflow
docs.text:
View or report Residual definition Main table colouring active-model calculated PCS − δ_Exp Standard Fitting report and plot predicted PCS − δ_Exp Multi-Conformer ensemble predicted PCS − experimental PCS (ppm) Joint PCS+RDC: PCS predicted PCS − experimental PCS (ppm) Joint PCS+RDC: RDC predicted RDC − experimental RDC (Hz) PRE predicted Γ₂ − measured Γ₂ (s⁻¹); standardized plots divide by the fitted error scale Multi-Lanthanide: Tensor fitting predicted PCS − experimental PCS (ppm), separately for each dataset Multi-Lanthanide: Reilley predicted total paramagnetic shift − δ_para (ppm), in original shift space Rhombicity Table δ_Exp − calculated PCS Rhombicity Check δ_Exp − axial-only regression prediction NMR Analysis δ_nonPCS δ_para − calculated PCS VT observed-shift analysis measured − fitted in the selected y-coordinate units; Curie/Curie-Weiss model metrics use raw observed δ

The δ_nonPCS quantity compares a derived paramagnetic shift with the calculated PCS and is not the same as a δ_Exp fitting residual. See Observed and Diamagnetic Shifts. See VT Analysis for the separate temperature-fit residuals, coordinate transforms and model comparisons.

Normalized Reilley views show the recorded fit in transformed coordinates; the residual plot remains in original ppm. Other Multi-Lanthanide diagnostics have their own selected quantities, rather than one universal PCS residual. The Joint fitting objective scales residuals by their selected error scales; the configured RDC multiplier also affects that objective. Its plots retain raw ppm/Hz residuals. Keep the raw units distinct when reading standardized values or comparing weighted sums. See Advanced metrics.

docs.title: Main and Rhombicity table colouring
docs.text:
Enable Color below the main table or above the Rhombicity Table to apply the shared absolute-residual classification. Both views share the accepted cutoffs and Color state within the active document. The defaults are:

  • green: |residual| ≤ 0.10 ppm;
  • orange: 0.10 < |residual| ≤ 0.30 ppm;
  • red: |residual| > 0.30 ppm; and
  • gray: no residual is available.

With Color off, cutoffs appear as subdued values without input borders and cannot be edited. Each dot, comparison sign and value forms a compact group, with equal spacing between groups. Enable Color to turn the two cutoff values into editable fields; both views switch together without resizing the whole row. The legend stays right-aligned, keeping the ppm end fixed in both modes. Edit the fields beside ≤ and press Enter, or leave the field, to apply them. Values must be finite and satisfy 0 ≤ green cutoff < orange cutoff. Invalid input is marked and leaves the accepted values and colours unchanged; Escape restores the accepted values. The red label follows the orange cutoff automatically. Changing these controls retags existing rows without rerunning PCS calculations or fitting.
