Each document can have its own cutoffs. Changes mark the document as modified; save the .pcsp to preserve them. Older projects without these settings use 0.10/0.30 ppm with Color off. These display settings are outside scientific Undo/Redo history.

The Rhombicity Table colors the axial residual when Enable Δχ_rh is off and the axial-plus-rhombic residual when it is on. These thresholds are classification aids, not uncertainty estimates or universal acceptance criteria.

The Fitting tab's residual plot has its own fixed 0.05/0.15 ppm color thresholds; see Quality Metrics.

docs.title: Selecting observations
docs.text:
The G_ax vs PCS view supports individual point picking and lasso or box selection. Fit (Fit Selected) on its contextual Ribbon restricts that linear regression to the selected subset; Clear Selection returns to all points. Plot selections are reflected in the main table.

The standard nonlinear Fitting tab uses PCS observations instead, including grouped targets when structured observations are available. Each group contributes one residual. Its plot labels points by Ref ID but does not provide an interactive include/exclude selector. In Rhombicity Check, a current selection in the Fitting PCS observations list is used when present; otherwise the diagnostic uses all available δ_Exp Ref IDs. At least three valid assigned points are required.

docs.title: Reading the residual pattern
docs.text:
Review more than a single summary number. Useful checks include:

  • the largest absolute residuals and their Ref IDs;
  • whether residuals are concentrated in one atom class or region;
  • whether the sign changes systematically with orientation;
  • whether results change strongly when questionable points are excluded; and
  • whether an axial-only residual correlates with the rhombic geometrical factor.

A residual can reflect experimental error, assignment mismatch, a structure or centre error, an unsuitable tensor frame, averaging assumptions, or model terms not included in the calculation. Residual structure alone does not identify a unique cause.

docs.title: Exports
docs.text:
• G_ax vs PCS Ribbon → Export Plot writes the figure in the chosen image format and also creates a _summary.txt report and _points.csv data file.
  • Fitting Ribbon → Export Plot saves the correlation and residual figure as PNG or PDF.
  • File → Save table... exports the main table and, when populated, the Rhombicity Table. XLSX uses separate Table and Rhombicity sheets; CSV creates separate _table.csv and _rhombicity.csv files.

The textual Rhombicity Check report and its diagnostic figure do not have a dedicated export command in the current tab. Copying or exporting those items requires an external capture or a later implementation.

For the axial/rhombic comparison, see Rhombicity Diagnostics.

docs.title: Rhombicity Diagnostics
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer provides two related rhombicity views:

  • 📊 Rhombicity Check performs an axial-only regression and examines the remaining residuals; and
  • 📊 Rhombicity Table compares calculated axial and axial-plus-rhombic PCS point by point for user-supplied tensor values.

They are diagnostic tools with different purposes. A correlation or improved residual is evidence to investigate, not proof that rhombicity is the only missing contribution.

docs.title: Rhombicity Check
docs.text: Choose ⟳ Update Diagnostic after assigning δ_Exp and establishing the current structure, centre, and tensor-frame orientation. The diagnostic uses the selected Ref IDs in the Fitting PCS observations list when that list has a selection; otherwise it uses all δ_Exp assignments that match the current atom set. At least three valid points are required.

docs.title: Axial-only reference fit
docs.text:
The diagnostic first regresses δ_Exp against the current axial geometrical factor Gax. By default it fits both slope and intercept. Selecting Force b = 0 (through origin) fixes the intercept to zero.

The report provides:

  • number of points and axial residual RMSD;
  • fitted slope and intercept;
  • a Δχ_ax estimate converted from the slope; and
  • per-point δ_Exp, axial prediction, residual, φ, and Grh.

Here the residual is δ_Exp − axial prediction, unlike the standard Fitting tab's predicted-minus-experimental convention.

docs.title: Residual versus φ and Grh
docs.text:
The plot shows residual versus azimuth φ and residual versus Grh. The second panel fits a line with an intercept and reports its Pearson correlation r and R². The slope is converted to an approximate Δχ_rh value using the same PCS scaling convention. The report also lists the five largest absolute residuals.

A strong linear relationship between axial residual and Grh is consistent with an omitted rhombic component in the current tensor frame. It is not unique evidence: outliers, contact or other non-PCS shifts, incorrect assignments, averaging, centre errors, and an unsuitable frame can generate structured residuals. The converted Δχ_rh is therefore an interpretation aid, not a confidence-bounded full-tensor estimate.

The diagnostic respects active symmetry and torsional averaging when it builds Gax and Grh.

docs.title: Rhombicity Table
docs.text:
Enter Δχ_rh (E-32 m³), choose ⟳ Update, and use Enable Δχ_rh to select which model controls the residual colouring. The table contains:

  • Ref ID, atom, r, θ, and φ;
  • Gi_ax and Gi_rh;
  • δ_PCS(ax) and δ_PCS(ax+rh);
  • δ_Exp; and
  • res(ax) and res(ax+rh).

Both residual columns use δ_Exp minus calculated PCS. With rhombicity enabled, changing Rotate around Z-axis (°) changes φ and the rhombic prediction without changing the axial factor. The slider and entry cover −180° to +180°.

Residual colours use absolute values with editable cutoffs shared with the main table. Defaults are green through 0.10 ppm, orange through 0.30 ppm, and red above 0.30 ppm. See Residual Analysis for how these thresholds differ from the Fitting plot.

docs.title: Axial versus rhombic comparison
docs.text:
Compare res(ax) with res(ax+rh) across the full table rather than choosing Δχ_rh from one point. A systematic decrease in residual magnitude can support the rhombic model, but adding a component also increases model flexibility. The Rhombicity Table does not itself optimize Δχ_rh or calculate a model- selection statistic.

Gi_rh depends on both θ and φ. Its sign and magnitude are meaningful only in the current tensor frame, including the z-rotation that defines the x/y directions. For the canonical factor and tensor definitions, see Axial and Rhombic PCS and Tensor Conventions.

docs.title: Tensor reconstruction
docs.text:
🧮 Calc χ(xx,yy,zz) reconstructs the principal susceptibility components from the current Δχ values. When Enable Δχ_rh is off, reconstruction uses the axial case; when enabled, it includes the entered rhombic component. If a molar isotropic susceptibility is supplied, it is retained as χiso; otherwise the application constructs the traceless anisotropic tensor.

The exact definitions, units, and reconstruction formulas are documented in Tensor Conventions.

docs.title: Export limitations
docs.text: File → Save table... includes the populated Rhombicity Table in the table export. The Rhombicity Check text and plot currently have no dedicated export button, and the diagnostic does not report uncertainty intervals for its approximate Δχ estimates.

docs.title: Experimental PCS Data
docs.text: PCS Analyzer uses δ_Exp as the experimental PCS value supplied for a specific structure Ref ID. These values are the targets used by the main geometrical-factor regression, the Fitting tab, the rhombicity diagnostic, and PCS-based advanced fitting workflows.

docs.title: Meaning of δ_Exp
docs.text:
In the current application, δ_Exp means experimental PCS. It is stored separately from the observed and diamagnetic chemical-shift layers.

The related quantities are:

Quantity Meaning in PCS Analyzer δ_Exp User-supplied experimental PCS used as a regression or fitting target δ_PCS or calculated PCS PCS predicted from the current structure, metal centre, tensor, orientation, and active prediction model δ_obs Observed shift for the paramagnetic sample δ_dia Diamagnetic reference shift δ_para Paramagnetic shift contribution computed as δ_obs − δ_dia δ_nonPCS Diagnostic difference δ_para − calculated PCS

Although δ_para may be used as an experimental PCS estimate when other paramagnetic shift contributions are negligible, the two terms are not automatically interchangeable. PCS Analyzer does not automatically copy δ_para into δ_Exp. See Observed and Diamagnetic Shifts.

docs.title: Entering values in the main table
docs.text:
The main table contains a δ_Exp column. Double-click a cell in that column, enter a numeric value in ppm, and press Enter. Submitting an empty value clears the assignment. Other text is rejected as an invalid value.

For multiple assignments, use Ribbon → Data → Import PCS or Paste. Export Template creates a file containing the currently visible Ref IDs and atom labels. The complete import workflow is described in Import and Export.

Alternatively, NMR Workbench → PCS Preparation derives experimental PCS from paired observables and supplies reviewed single-atom or structured targets through an explicit handoff.

docs.title: Ref IDs are the assignment key
docs.text:
Each δ_Exp value is associated with an integer Ref ID, not merely with an atom or element label. A fit uses a value only when that Ref ID is also present in the current effective atom set and is selected in the relevant workflow.

Reloading or replacing a structure can change the meaning or availability of Ref IDs. After doing so, verify the assignments and re-import the data when necessary. A value attached to a numeric Ref ID that is absent from the current structure remains stored but cannot contribute to a fit.

docs.title: Experimental and calculated PCS
docs.text:
Calculated PCS values are refreshed from the current inputs and appear as δ_PCS in the main table. δ_Exp is an independent experimental layer; an update of the structure, tensor, centre, rotation, or averaging settings changes δ_PCS but does not change δ_Exp.

The main-table δ_PCS follows Prediction model: Axial excludes the rhombic term; Full tensor (Axial + Rhombic) includes it only when Enable Δχ_rh is on. Linked NMR predictions follow this policy too. Polar contours and G_ax vs PCS remain axial diagnostics. See Axial and Rhombic PCS.

docs.title: Structured observations and grouped targets
docs.text:
Experimental PCS prepared for a grouped NMR site, matching ligand sites, or a custom group is retained as one observation with one experimental value and, when supplied, one uncertainty. It contributes one residual to standard fitting, not one independent measurement for every member atom. Such grouped observations need not appear as individual δ_Exp cells in the main table.

The prediction is calculated at each member's geometry, then reduced according to the target's member/site hierarchy. The current grouped targets use arithmetic means: first within each site, then across sites. For example, sites containing two and three atoms give

\[ \delta_{\mathrm{pred}} =\frac{1}{2}\left[ \frac{\delta_1+\delta_2}{2} +\frac{\delta_3+\delta_4+\delta_5}{3} \right]. \]

This gives equal weight to the two sites, not to all five atoms. A singleton without reduction retains its own PCS. Predictions are not evaluated at a mean coordinate: PCS depends nonlinearly on distance and direction. Existing symmetry/torsional geometrical-factor averaging remains applicable to the member predictions; see Averaging.

When structured observations are present, PCS observations lists their assignments/identifiers; otherwise fitting uses the legacy proton Ref list. Review the selected targets and their members before fitting. Group membership does not justify treating members as additional independent observations.

docs.title: Residual sign
docs.text:
The main table uses the difference

\[ \delta_{\mathrm{PCS}}-\delta_{\mathrm{Exp}} \]

for residual colouring. The nonlinear fitting reports use the same predicted-minus-experimental sign. The axial-only rhombicity diagnostic uses the opposite sign, experimental minus prediction, as explained in Residual Analysis.

For the PCS equation and susceptibility conventions, see PCS Theory and Tensor Conventions.

docs.title: Observed and Diamagnetic Shifts
docs.text: PCS Analyzer keeps observed shifts, diamagnetic-reference shifts, derived paramagnetic shifts, and experimental PCS assignments as distinct data layers.

docs.title: Shift definitions
docs.text:
For a given Ref ID, the application uses

\[ \delta_{\mathrm{para}} = \delta_{\mathrm{obs}}-\delta_{\mathrm{dia}}. \]

Here:

  • δ_obs is the observed chemical shift in the paramagnetic sample;
  • δ_dia is the corresponding diamagnetic reference shift; and
  • δ_para is the shift difference computed by PCS Analyzer.

δ_para is calculated only when both δ_obs and δ_dia are present for the same Ref ID. Clearing or changing either input recomputes the derived layer.

docs.title: Paramagnetic shift is not necessarily PCS
docs.text:
The paramagnetic shift may contain PCS and contributions not represented by the current PCS model. PCS Analyzer therefore does not equate δ_para with δ_Exp automatically.

The NMR analysis workflow calculates the diagnostic quantity

\[ \delta_{\mathrm{nonPCS}} = \delta_{\mathrm{para}}-\delta_{\mathrm{PCS,calc}}, \]

where δ_PCS,calc follows the active Prediction model. Axial excludes the rhombic term; Full tensor (Axial + Rhombic) includes it only when Enable Δχ_rh is on. This value is a residual-like comparison, not a guaranteed physical separation of contact shift, referencing error, and every other non-PCS contribution.

Caution

A small δ_nonPCS is consistent with the compared PCS model accounting for most of δ_para. A large value can have several causes, including a genuine non-PCS contribution, an incorrect assignment, an unsuitable diamagnetic reference, or an inaccurate structure, centre, tensor, or orientation.

docs.title: Working with the shift layers
docs.text:
Open Modules → NMR Workbench, process and reference vendor spectra, and assign corresponding signals in NMR Data, or import/add prepared absolute observed shifts there without a spectrum. Set Paramagnetic / Diamagnetic dataset roles and choose Pair with. Inspector → Shift Analysis compares assignment-matched observables in Table, Overlay, Stacked, or Shift Diagnostics views. Existing project shift layers also appear as read-only shift lists; they are not measured intensity traces.

The project-layer equation above is keyed by structural Ref ID. Workbench pairing instead matches reviewed observable assignment labels; those labels do not accept structural targets automatically. See NMR Data and the FID/CSV tutorial.

Use PCS Preparation to choose a derivation method, map structural targets, and review a handoff to δ_Exp. δ_para is not transferred automatically. See Shift Analysis and PCS Preparation.

See Import and Export for accepted files, column matching, preview behavior, and Ref ID troubleshooting. To provide data to fitting, assign experimental PCS values explicitly as δ_Exp.

docs.title: Import and Export
docs.text: The experimental-data controls accept CSV and Excel tables and provide a preview before modifying the current assignments. δ_Exp is managed on Ribbon → Data → Experimental PCS. For observed/reference shifts, use assigned vendor spectra or prepared observed values in NMR Workbench. NMR Data → Import accepts observed-shift CSV/TSV or pasted tables without a spectrum. Existing project δ_obs/δ_dia layers remain readable as read-only projections.

docs.title: Supported input paths
docs.text:
Data File import Clipboard-style input Where δ_Exp CSV, XLSX, XLS Yes Data Ribbon → Experimental PCS NMR observed shifts Vendor 1D data; observed-shift CSV/TSV/text Paste or manual values; peak assignment editing NMR Workbench → NMR Data; see NMR Data PCS-project δ_obs / δ_dia CSV, XLSX, XLS Yes NMR Data → Import → PCS project observed/diamagnetic shifts; read-only Workbench projections

The table-import rules below describe the current δ_Exp importer and the legacy δ_obs/δ_dia table importers. Legacy import dialogs are not the current Workbench's acquisition/processing workflow. Recognized legacy headings are retained here for interpreting existing tables and projects. The general Observed shifts CSV / TSV… importer uses separate validation and identity rules described in NMR Data. In particular, do not apply the blank-cell clearing or structural Ref-matching rules below to that importer.

CSV reading first tries UTF-8 with a byte-order mark and then Windows cp1252. Excel reading uses the engines available to pandas. The standard dependency set includes support for XLSX. Although the file chooser also offers legacy XLS files, reading an XLS file can fail if no compatible legacy Excel engine is installed; the application reports the read error.

docs.title: Recognized columns
docs.text:
Column matching ignores capitalization and surrounding whitespace. Use a Ref ID column whenever possible.

Role Recognized headings Ref ID Ref, ID, ref_id, rid Atom label Atom, Element δ_Exp δ_exp, delta_exp, exp, delta values δ_obs δ_obs, delta_obs, obs, ppm, shift δ_dia δ_dia, delta_dia, dia, diamagnetic, delta_diamagnetic

If neither a Ref nor an Atom heading is recognized but the table has at least two columns, the importer treats the first two columns as Ref ID and value. For predictable results, include explicit headings rather than relying on this fallback.

docs.title: Ref ID matching
docs.text: With a recognized Ref column, the importer converts each value to an integer and assigns the data to that Ref ID. A numeric ID is accepted by the preview even if it is absent from the current structure; such an assignment remains stored but is ignored by structure-dependent fitting and diagnostics until a matching atom exists.

docs.title: Atom-label matching
docs.text:
If no Ref column is present but an Atom column is available, labels are matched exactly, including case, against the currently visible table. When a label occurs more than once, imported values are consumed in visible table order. This can be ambiguous for repeated labels such as multiple H atoms, so Ref IDs are strongly preferred.

If both Ref and Atom columns are present, Ref ID matching takes precedence.

docs.title: Preview and selective application
docs.text:
After reading a file or pasted block, PCS Analyzer opens an import preview. Each row shows its source identifier and value, mapped Ref ID, parsed value, and one of three actions:

  • set assigns a numeric value;
  • clear removes the existing value for a matched Ref ID; and
  • skip makes no change.

Blank cells, NaN, and non-numeric cells parse as clear, not as an automatic skip. Review these rows carefully before applying them. Unmapped rows cannot be selected.

Click the first preview column to toggle a row, or use All on, All off, and Invert. Apply changes only the selected rows. Undo last restores the data layer to its state before the most recent applied preview in the current session.

docs.title: Clipboard input
docs.text:
The Paste dialogs provide an editable text area rather than reading the system clipboard without review. Paste a block with a header, then choose Preview. Comma, tab, semicolon, and whitespace separators are detected from the first line.

Recommended two-column examples are:

Ref,δ_Exp
12,0.084
18,-0.137

Ref δ_obs
12  7.913
18  8.204

docs.title: Exporting experimental-data tables
docs.text:
Data → Export Template writes the currently visible main-table rows as Ref, Atom, and δ_Exp. Existing δ_Exp values are retained in the output. CSV is written as UTF-8 with a byte-order mark; XLSX is also available.

File → Save table... exports the current main table. An XLSX export also includes a Rhombicity worksheet when that table contains rows. A CSV export creates a _table.csv file and, when available, a separate _rhombicity.csv file.

For the wider file-format inventory, see File Formats. The detailed matching and preview behavior on this page remains the authoritative experimental-data reference.

docs.title: Common mismatch cases
docs.text:
• The imported Ref IDs belong to another structure or to an earlier atom order.
  • A Ref value contains non-integer text and is skipped.
  • An atom label differs in case or spelling from the visible table.
  • Repeated atom labels are assigned in an unintended order.
  • Filtering hides rows needed for atom-label matching or template export.
  • A blank or invalid numeric cell is selected in the preview and therefore clears an existing value.
  • δ_obs and δ_dia use different Ref IDs, so δ_para is not calculated.

When the fit cannot find expected points, compare the imported Ref IDs with the current main table, then use ⟳ Refresh in the Fitting tab.

docs.title: Fit History
docs.text:
Open Fit History from the contextual Fitting Ribbon. It manages standard Mode A/B/C runs for the active document. Each completed standard fit adds a run; inspecting an older run does not overwrite the other runs or apply its tensor. Advanced Fitting results are separate.

Mode B runs for Nd(iPr₂BA)₃ with fixed and fitted axial anisotropy.

docs.title: Inspect and compare
docs.text:
Select a run and choose Inspect, or double-click it, to show its saved parameters, metrics and predictions in the Fitting result area. With multiple runs selected, Inspect uses the focused run. Select exactly two runs and choose Compare for parameter and metric differences. Read the comparison warnings: different observations, weighting, modes or fitting inputs can make numerical rankings misleading. Compare residual patterns and scientific assumptions, not just the lowest RMSD.

Status Meaning and action Current Checked scientific fit inputs match those used for this run. This does not prove model validity or uniqueness. Stale Checked inputs have changed. The stored report remains inspectable, but Apply to Tensor and Preview Geometry are blocked; rerun for the changed analysis. Unknown Validity cannot be checked. Review provenance and inputs; do not treat it as Current merely because application/preview is available.

Status compares the run's recorded observation selection and configuration against current scientific inputs; it is not simply a check of which rows are currently highlighted. Changing geometry, data, averaging, weighting or a tensor value needed by the run can change status. Inspecting a run does not restore its original project or all its fitting controls.

After inspection, Apply Tensor and Preview obey the same mode-specific rules as a fresh fit. Mode A cannot apply a tensor. Mode B retains the current rhombic value. Mode C tensor application retains the assigned metal centre; the refined centre is available only through the temporary geometry preview. See Running and applying a fit.

docs.title: Manage and exchange runs
docs.text:
The More ▾ menu provides:

  • Label…: name one selected run, for example by subset or model assumption. There is no separate free-text notes editor; keep detailed analysis notes alongside the project.
  • Import Fit Run(s)…: import a PCS Analyzer fit-run JSON export. Import preserves reports without running the optimizer or applying the tensor; duplicates are skipped and rejected records are reported. Imported results are checked against the active project's inputs.
  • Export selected as JSON…: save one or several complete runs for later import, including labels, parameters, predictions and recorded fit provenance.
  • Export selected as CSV…: write <base>_summary.csv; selecting one run also writes <base>_observables.csv with its experimental/predicted values and residuals. Multiple-run CSV export contains summaries only. CSV is for analysis/reporting, not fit-run re-import.
  • Delete…: remove one selected run after confirmation. Export important results first, then save the project to retain the history changes.
  • Refresh: update the list and status indicators.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text:
Saving the .pcsp project retains complete standard runs, labels and the inspected/latest run references. Reopening restores the reports without rerunning the fit. Their predictions describe the original runs, while live project displays are recalculated. Older summary-only records cannot recover complete reports.

A fit-run JSON is evidence of a calculation, not a standalone reconstruction of the structure and acquisition. Keep it with the corresponding project, source data, application version and analysis notes. A plot export alone does not preserve the numerical report. See Projects and Persistence and File Formats.

docs.title: Full Tensor Fitting
docs.text: Mode C · Full tensor + metal jointly refines tensor-frame orientation and metal position against selected experimental PCS values. Depending on the tensor checkboxes, the actual parameter vector contains six, seven, or eight variables.

docs.title: Parameter combinations
docs.text:
The following parameters are always fitted:

  • three Cartesian Euler angles;
  • metal x, y, and z.

The tensor controls add parameters as follows:

Fit Δχ_ax Fit Δχ_rh Number of variables Tensor behavior Off Off 6 Both current tensor components remain fixed On Off 7 Δχ_ax fitted; current Δχ_rh fixed Off On 7 Current Δχ_ax fixed; Δχ_rh fitted On On 8 Both tensor components fitted

Count the variable parameters for the chosen checkbox settings rather than assuming that every full-tensor run fits eight parameters.

docs.title: Initialization and bounds
docs.text:
The Euler angles start at 0° unless Use current tensor as initial guess is selected, which uses the current orientation. The metal coordinates start at the currently assigned centre, and each coordinate is restricted to ±1 Å around that starting value. A tensor component starts from its current input value when it is fitted.

Euler angles are bounded from −180° to +180°. Tensor components are unbounded in the final refinement. Global search (DE) provides a preliminary search; see Initialization.

docs.title: Geometry evaluated during refinement
docs.text:
For each trial centre, the rigid structure is translated relative to that centre, rotated with the active extrinsic X → Y → Z convention, and evaluated in the tensor frame. The structure's internal coordinates do not deform. Selected experimental observations provide one residual each, including structured groups. Symmetry- and torsional-averaged geometry factors are used when those features are active.

See Coordinate Handling for the rotation convention and Tensor Conventions for Δχ definitions and units.

docs.title: Results and application
docs.text:
The result report shows the refined metal coordinates, Euler α/β/γ values, the fitted or fixed tensor values, quality metrics, and per-point residuals. The displayed Greek angle names correspond to the same three X/Y/Z rotation parameters reported as ax, ay, and az in Mode B.

Apply to Tensor copies Δχ_ax, Δχ_rh and orientation into the current tensor, clears an existing geometry override, and refreshes the views. It retains the assigned metal position, prediction model and rhombic enablement. It does not permanently adopt the refined centre. Main predictions after application can therefore differ from the fit report.

Preview Geometry temporarily uses the fitted orientation and refined metal position in the views. It also fills and confirms the fitted Δχ input values through an immediate redraw, retaining current tensor orientation, prediction policy and rhombic enablement. It does not reassign the metal atom. Clear Preview removes temporary geometry while keeping those current tensor settings. Undoing Preview restores the previous geometry and tensor values; Undoing Clear restores the preview. Neither action reruns the fit. Saving a current project retains this active preview, including its refined centre and orientation, separately from the assigned metal centre. Reopening restores the preview without refitting or applying the result to the canonical tensor. Older files that omitted those values disable the incomplete preview; recreate it from the saved Fit History run if its status allows. See Projects and Persistence.

docs.title: Interpretation and limitations
docs.text:
Metal position, orientation, axial anisotropy, and rhombicity can compensate for one another, especially with few observations or poor spatial coverage. Use more independent PCS points than fitted parameters, inspect the residuals, and compare repeated fits or constrained alternatives. The application does not currently report parameter covariance or nonlinear confidence intervals.

See Quality Metrics and Rhombicity Diagnostics for the available checks.

docs.title: Joint PCS+RDC tutorial
docs.text:
Use this workflow when PCS and RDC measurements describe the same structure and susceptibility-induced magnetic self-alignment. It fits Δχ_ax and Δχ_rh with the current metal position and tensor orientation fixed. RDCs from an external alignment medium do not satisfy this coupled model.

The examples below use synthetic labelled probes, not an optimized molecular structure or experimental dataset. Prepared projects and input files are in examples/joint_pcs_rdc_demo/. The known tensor is Δχ_ax=-18 and Δχ_rh=5 E-32 m³ per molecule, at 14.1 T and 298 K.

Short paths below are relative to examples/joint_pcs_rdc_demo/ from the release or source archive; see finding the examples.

docs.title: 1. Open the prepared project
docs.text:
Use File → Open PCS Project... to open examples/joint_pcs_rdc_demo/noisy/demo.pcsp, then select Advanced Fitting → Joint PCS+RDC. The project contains 24 PCS observations, 12 RDC bonds, supplied uncertainties and a recorded successful fit. Reopening restores it as Current without rerunning or applying it. No separate CSV import or structure loading is needed for this starting point.

The noiseless project verifies exact numerical recovery. The noisy project adds reproducible independent Gaussian noise: 0.02 ppm for PCS and 0.5 Hz for RDC. Use it to inspect realistic residuals rather than numerical rounding noise.

docs.title: 2. Review and select input data
docs.text:
Select PCS opens an observation selector in the Ribbon. Selection is local to this joint fit; it does not change main atom visibility or selection. Structured observation reductions use the existing PCS model.

Load RDC CSV reads explicit raw-atom ref1/ref2 pairs, or unambiguous legacy atom1/atom2 labels. Ref pairs are recommended. A minimal row is:

ref1,ref2,rdc_exp,rdc_err,nuc1,nuc2
1,2,4.96,0.5,15N,1H

RDC values and errors are in Hz; rdc_exp is required. Missing rdc_err defaults to 0.5 Hz and missing nuclei default to H/N. H/1H, N/15N and C/13C are supported. Unmatched pairs are shown as skipped rows. Unsupported nuclei, invalid values/errors and duplicate matched bonds are rejected. The loader does not infer atom correspondence from row order.

The input tables, report and plot region have vertical splitters. Input data can be collapsed; the summary retains data counts and live conditions. Short windows scroll the entire tab. Reports remain selectable and scroll both ways. With enough window height, plots fill the remaining vertical space while the chosen input/report heights are retained; collapsing inputs releases space to the plots. Smaller windows retain a usable plot height and scroll instead of compressing away the axis labels.

This preparation screenshot clears the example's saved result in the disposable capture session; the distributed noisy project itself includes that result.

docs.title: 3. Set conditions and weighting
docs.text:
Open Fit settings from the Ribbon. For this demo, keep B₀=14.1 T, temperature=298 K, RDC residual multiplier=1, and Use supplied PCS uncertainties enabled. Every selected PCS observation then needs positive σ.

The objective is the sum of squared PCS residuals divided by their σ, plus squared RDC residuals divided by max(rdc_err, 0.1 Hz) and multiplied by the RDC residual multiplier. Thus the multiplier is squared in the objective. When PCS uncertainty weighting is disabled, the legacy unit-ppm PCS residual scale is retained; it is not a statement about measurement uncertainty.

The current model fits both scalar components, retains the main metal and orientation, and does not support torsional averaging of RDC bonds. Use consistent signed RDC definitions when exchanging data with other software. The molecular susceptibility alignment factor contains no Avogadro divisor. See Method References for background and reporting scope.

docs.title: 4. Validate and run
docs.text:
Select Validate inputs to check mapping, errors and rank, then choose Run Fit. The fixed-frame linear fit runs in the background. Inspect the result before choosing Apply; neither validation nor running the fit changes the main tensor.

For the noisy example, expect approximately:

Quantity Value Δχ_ax −18.012246 E-32 m³ Δχ_rh 4.990465 E-32 m³ PCS RMSD 0.015990 ppm RDC RMSD 0.365648 Hz Rank 2 / 2

Small last-digit differences after reopening reflect eight-decimal coordinate tables, not a different optimization model. PCS and RDC RMSDs retain different units and are reported separately; no combined physical-unit RMSD is defined.

docs.title: 5. Inspect residuals and result state
docs.text:
Switch Diagnostics to Residuals. Both plots show predicted minus experimental values. The report records the original conditions and per-point values even when live inputs change. Check rank and condition number alongside RMSDs: rank 2 establishes independence in this two-scalar model, but neither rank nor a low RMSD establishes structural correctness or precise parameters.

Editing the selected observations, geometry, orientation, RDC inputs or fit conditions can make the report Stale, which disables Apply. Review the changes and rerun the fit with the intended inputs. Tiny representation-rounding differences and equivalent orientation representations do not alone make the result stale; changed scientific inputs require refitting.

The model currently estimates no confidence intervals or bootstrap/CV results. The noisy example is a reproducible calculation check, not a reliability study.

docs.title: 6. Inspect a failure case
docs.text:
Open ambiguous/demo.pcsp. All coordinates and RDC bonds lie along z, so the rhombic basis column vanishes. Run Fit reports rank below 2 instead of presenting an arbitrary rhombic value. No successful result is installed and Apply remains disabled.

The screenshot shows the actual workspace after rejection; it is not an error dialog mockup. Add independent geometry/observations or choose a different scientific model before fitting. Importing invalid-rdc.csv separately should reject its unsupported nucleus and retain the previous input collection.

docs.title: 7. Save, export and apply deliberately
docs.text:
Save Project retains the RDC inputs, selected PCS observations, fit settings and last recorded result. Reopening checks the saved result without refitting or applying its tensor. Older projects without joint-fit data open with empty joint inputs and defaults. For storage and compatibility details, see File Formats.

Export result writes recorded inputs, matching and numerical diagnostics as JSON, including stale results. It does not substitute live settings. Apply copies only the fitted Δχ_ax/Δχ_rh scalars from a Current successful result. It preserves metal, orientation, rhombic enablement and prediction policy; enabling a rhombic contribution in main predictions remains a separate choice. Joint reports stay separate from standard Fit History.

See Fitting overview, Projects and File formats.

docs.title: Tutorial: Multi-Conformer PCS Fitting and Reliability
docs.text:
This tutorial fits populations and shared tensor magnitudes from structure-specific PCS predictions, then evaluates uncertainty and held-out prediction error. It uses two reproducible synthetic projects: one with distinguishable PCS signatures and one where two conformers are indistinguishable.

The coordinates are labelled geometric probes around a metal, not an optimized chemical structure or experimental evidence for conformational exchange. The current model assumes fast exchange, a common fixed tensor orientation, and PCS averaging after prediction for each conformer. It does not average coordinates or fit independent tensors for different conformers.

Read Multi-Conformer fitting for the complete input and model contract. Standard Full Tensor Fitting is a different workflow; this tutorial does not optimize orientation or metal positions.

docs.title: 1. Get the demo projects
docs.text:
Use examples/multi_conformer_demo/ from the source checkout or portable release: short paths below are relative to this directory. See finding the example files.

Project Purpose informative/demo.pcsp Recover tensor magnitudes and two fitted populations from different PCS signatures. ambiguous/demo.pcsp See why a good PCS fit does not determine populations of identical conformers separately.

Each scenario also contains three XYZ files and pcs.csv for inspecting the inputs. The project embeds the structures, explicit Ref mapping, fit options and structured PCS observations including uncertainties. No CSV reimport or manual mapping is needed for these prepared projects.

The ground truth is:

Quantity Value Observations 24 H probes, Ref 2–25 Metal Ref 1, origin (0, 0, 0) Å True C1 / C2 / C3 populations 0.25 / 0.55 / 0.20 Δχ_ax / Δχ_rh 12 / 3 E-32 m³ Tensor orientation Zero Euler angles, fixed Measurement noise Independent Gaussian, σ = 0.03 ppm Initial C1 / C2 / C3 populations 0.40 / 0.40 / 0.20

C3 is fixed at 0.20; C1 and C2 share the remaining 0.80. In the ambiguous project, C1 and C2 have identical coordinates, so their combined population is the relevant quantity rather than the two individual weights.

docs.title: 2. Open and inspect the informative project
docs.text:
1. Choose File → Open PCS Project... and open informative/demo.pcsp.
  2. Select Advanced Fitting → Multi-Conformer in the Analysis area.
  3. Inspect the conformer table. All three rows are Included and Mapped / confirmed. The Population column shows Fit for C1/C2 and Fixed for C3.
  4. Double-click a row, or select it and press Enter, to inspect its mapping, metal/frame, inclusion and initial/fixed population. Cancel leaves it unchanged.
  5. In the contextual Ribbon, confirm Fit Δχ_ax and Fit Δχ_rh are checked.

The Fitting group and Run Fit appear first. Parameters contains Fit settings and native parameter checkboxes. Data → Select PCS selects observations independently of main atom selection; Validate inputs checks mapping, frame and population constraints. It does not certify the chemistry or the statistical model.

docs.title: Check the fit conditions
docs.text:
Open Fit settings and confirm:

Setting Demo value Fit target both Objective weighting experimental_uncertainty Alignment confirmed_common_frame Population initialization user Δχ_ax initial / fixed −5 E-32 m³ Δχ_rh initial / fixed 1 E-32 m³ Multi-start count 4 Random seed 11

Both scalar checkboxes are enabled, so −5 and 1 are starting values rather than fixed constraints. tensor fixes the supplied populations; populations fixes both specified scalars. Clearing a scalar checkbox holds its specified value fixed, including a nonzero rhombic value.

For your own structures, use Use Current or Load XYZ, then Map / frame. Confirm chemical Ref correspondence and each file's metal origin/frame explicitly. Equal atom counts do not establish chemical identity. Use metal-centered core alignment only with at least three corresponding noncollinear anchors; use Already tensor-oriented only when those are the actual coordinate axes.

docs.title: 3. Run the fit and read the results
docs.text:
Click Run Fit. The computation runs in the background. Completion records a result; it does not automatically apply it to the main structure.

With the bundled noise realization and settings, the result is approximately:

Quantity Recovered value C1 0.2484 C2 0.5516 C3 0.2000, fixed Δχ_ax 11.9977 E-32 m³ Δχ_rh 3.0015 E-32 m³ In-sample PCS RMSD 0.02646 ppm

Small last-digit differences can depend on numerical-library versions. Check the recorded conditions and solver status before interpreting a number. A converged multi-start solution is not proof of a global optimum or unique populations.

  • PCS correlation compares experimental and ensemble-predicted PCS against the identity line. It is not a second regression fitted to the display points.
  • PCS residuals are predicted minus experimental PCS in ppm.
  • Conformer populations shows the fitted weights, including fixed C3.
  • Result contains recorded conditions, per-conformer details, error metrics, ambiguity and per-observation results. Its text is selectable and scrollable.

Drag the two horizontal splitters to allocate height to the list, report and plots. The Conformers header can collapse the list. Very short windows use the whole-tab scrollbar; report text retains its own scrollbars.

docs.title: 4. Evaluate reliability
docs.text:
After reviewing a successful Current result, click Results → Reliability. The command is unavailable while a Multi-Conformer job is running or inputs require a refit. It also requires recorded/current uncertainties to match: changing σ can leave an unweighted fit Current while still requiring a refit before evaluation.

Use these first-review settings:

Control Value Interpretation Bootstrap method parametric Independent Gaussian perturbations using recorded positive σ. Bootstrap refits 100 A practical initial review; increase for endpoint stability. Grouped CV folds 5 Each observation group is held out once. Random seed 2026 Reproducible sampling and solver starts. Marginal confidence 0.95 Enter a fraction, not 95. Relative PCS similarity threshold 0.01 Suggestions from structure-specific PCS columns at the fitted tensor.

Click Evaluate. Progress appears in the Analysis header. Each replicate refits every selected free tensor/population field; joint uncertainty is not approximated by keeping the tensor fixed. Geometry, orientation and fixed values remain fixed. Larger counts can take several minutes.

docs.title: Choose the resampling method deliberately
docs.text:
parametric requires known positive uncertainty for every selected observation and assumes independent Gaussian errors. It is rejected for overlapping physical members or shared source observables without a covariance model.

cases samples independent, exchangeable observation groups with replacement. Overlapping member Ref IDs, pseudo-members or shared source observable IDs stay together. Unknown correlations between the remaining groups are not automatically modelled; selecting cases does not make correlated experimental data independent.

Grouped CV uses only training observations to fit the tensor and populations. It starts from the recorded user/uniform initialization, not the full-data fitted parameters. There must be enough independent groups for the selected fold count, and each fold must retain at least three training observations. This is evaluation of a preselected model, not nested validation of structure/model selection.

docs.title: 5. Interpret the reliability report
docs.text:
Collapse Conformers if useful and scroll the report to Reliability evaluation.

For the bundled example, 100/100 bootstrap refits and 5/5 CV folds succeeded. The held-out PCS RMSD is approximately 0.03081 ppm, compared with the in-sample 0.02646 ppm. Both are raw ppm errors; the weighted objective is a different quantity.

The displayed approximate marginal 95% intervals are:

Parameter Interval Δχ_ax [11.9948, 12.0009] E-32 m³ Δχ_rh [2.9784, 3.0195] E-32 m³ C1 [0.2474, 0.2495] C2 [0.5505, 0.5526] C3 Fixed / not estimated

Population interval marks appear on the plot only where an interval is available. These are percentile estimates, not normal/Hessian intervals. Fixed parameters do not receive a zero-width estimated interval.

In this particular noise realization, C1's known truth 0.25 is outside its displayed interval. A nominal 95% interval need not cover the truth in every realization; one plot cannot establish coverage or calibrate intervals for other datasets.

Important report states:

State Meaning Successful refit count Failed repetitions are retained, not silently replaced. Withheld interval Too few successful refits or deficient/ambiguous parameter diagnostics prevent an individual interval. Fixed / not estimated The parameter was not varied in the evaluation. Partial CV score Some folds failed; the pooled score covers successful folds only. Similar PCS group Inspect the combined population; this is a suggestion, not an automatic merge.

At least 20 and 80% of requested refits must succeed before intervals are considered. Population boundaries, nonlinear or multimodal solutions, too few tail samples and incorrect error assumptions limit interpretation. Multi-start spread measures optimizer sensitivity; it is not a confidence interval. Uncertainty in geometry, orientation, metal positions, assignments or the chosen model is not propagated.

docs.title: 6. Compare the ambiguous project
docs.text:
Open ambiguous/demo.pcsp, then repeat Run Fit → Reliability → Evaluate with the same settings. The fixture intentionally gives C1 and C2 identical PCS signatures.

The fit still predicts PCS well; the held-out RMSD is approximately 0.03772 ppm. The individual weights are not determined uniquely: a run can retain the initial 0.40/0.40 split or return another pair summing to 0.80. The screenshot's 0.0239/0.7761 is one such solver choice, not a numerical checkpoint to reproduce. None of these splits establishes recovery of the true 0.25/0.55 populations.

The report withholds individual parameter intervals when the joint diagnostics are rank deficient or ambiguous. It suggests C1, C2: combined population 0.8000 with a descriptive bootstrap range [0.8000, 0.8000]. C3 is fixed at 0.20, so the remaining sum 0.80 is itself fixed by the model; the zero-width aggregate range is not evidence of a precisely measured exchange population. No conformer is merged or removed.

docs.title: 7. Save, export and apply deliberately
docs.text:
• Export result saves the recorded inputs, all fit starts, contributions, bootstrap/fold runs, assumptions and diagnostics as JSON.
  • Save the PCS project to a new working path to retain the conformer inputs, fit and reliability result. Reopening restores the record; it does not recompute it. Keep the bundled example projects unchanged for repeatable comparisons.
  • Check Current/Stale/Unknown after changing inputs. A previous result retains its historical conditions rather than reading numbers from the live table.
  • Apply explicitly copies fitted scalar fields only. It preserves main orientation, metal, rhombic enablement and prediction policy. It does not install ensemble PCS in the main table or apply local fixed overrides. Population-only fitting has no newly fitted tensor fields to Apply.

Multi-Conformer results are separate from standard Fit History. See Projects and Persistence and Quality Metrics for the corresponding storage and metric scope.

The screenshots show the Light theme and 100-refit results described above. For statistical background and the limits of these estimates, see Method References.

docs.title: Multi-Lanthanide and Reilley tutorial
docs.text: Use Advanced Fitting → Multi-Lanthanide to compare independent tensor fits and analyse corresponding nuclei across a lanthanide series. Select the tool in the contextual Ribbon Analysis selector. Run Analysis executes the selected analysis; Validate inputs checks it without installing a result.

docs.title: 1. Open the synthetic example
docs.text:
Use File → Open PCS Project... to open examples/multi_lanthanide_demo/noisy/demo.pcsp. It contains eight synthetic probes, PCS and total paramagnetic-shift datasets for six Ln ions, supplied errors and a recorded result for each of the six analysis modes. Reopening restores them as Current. The coordinates are not a chemically optimized molecule. The inputs are supplied with the release; see finding the example files. Short paths below are relative to examples/multi_lanthanide_demo/.

noiseless/demo.pcsp verifies exact recovery. The noisy example perturbs total shifts with a fixed-seed 0.015 ppm Gaussian noise; recorded errors are 0.03 ppm. Its independently generated tensor PCS data remains noiseless.

For a first pass:

  1. Select Advanced Fitting → Multi-Lanthanide and choose Reilley separation in the contextual Ribbon's Analysis selector.
  2. Expand Input data. Keep Temperature = 300 K, Normalization = No normalization and Use supplied errors checked, with all six Ln datasets included.
  3. Choose Validate inputs, then Run Analysis. Inspect the Result for eight nuclei across Nd, Eu, Tb, Dy, Er and Yb. The total-shift observations and structural G values are already in the project; do not add the neighbouring paramagnetic.csv again, which would create duplicate Ln datasets.
  4. Continue with the sections below. For Nuclei diagnostics, choose H1 and H2 as the first two nuclei and leave the optional third nucleus empty initially.

docs.title: 2. Prepare and review input data
docs.text:
Reilley and series diagnostics use total paramagnetic shifts δ_para=δ_obs−δ_dia. Tensor fitting uses PCS. These quantities must not be interchanged. Nucleus labels identify corresponding assigned sites across Ln; matching numeric Ref IDs alone does not establish consistent assignments.

Add CSV accepts the historical wide Reilley matrix:

Nucleus,ref_id,G_common,Nd,Eu,Tb,Dy,Er,Yb,error
H1,1,-0.00196669,0.80,-0.87,12.59,14.91,-5.64,-3.55,0.03

Values are total paramagnetic shifts in ppm, not raw observed shifts. Blank cells remain missing; zero is a valid geometry value. Geometry may also use Ln_G_i columns. Errors may use Ln_err columns or the shared error column. Invalid numbers, nonpositive errors and duplicate nucleus labels are rejected. Geometry ratios/CFP checks need explicitly supplied structural G values.

Single-dataset CSVs use integer ref_id/ref/id, a site/Nucleus label, pcs_exp in Tensor fitting or delta_para in a series analysis, and optional pcs_err/error. Legacy delta_exp/d_exp/ppm aliases use the selected mode's input type. Reference / import Ln assigns the ion when importing a single dataset. Use Current copies main PCS into a local dataset, preserving single-atom observation errors. Grouped targets require explicit review and are not imported through this action.

Click an Ln heading to include/exclude that dataset. In Tensor fitting, Input view → Datasets provides a dataset summary; double-click its first column to change inclusion. Ref mapping shows assigned sites and shifts. Double-click Ref and press Enter to map the same site across local Ln datasets; Escape cancels the edit. It does not modify the main structure or PCS table. Duplicate included Ln datasets are rejected for Reilley/series analysis; choose one per Ln. Independent tensor fits can retain multiple datasets for the same ion.

For Reilley, a compact Coefficients table inside Fit conditions shows C_D and S(T) for included Ln ions, with short references to the coefficient sources. Settings use compact, font-aware control widths; coefficients take the remaining width. Settings and coefficients sit side by side when space permits and stack in narrow windows. Cell borders distinguish headings and numeric values. Temperature edits update S(T); Sm/Eu keep their marked 300 K values. Excluding an Ln removes it from this coefficient area. The input quantity is δ_para (ppm). The same coefficient area is available in nucleus/geometry diagnostics.

Input data collapses conditions, coefficients and its table together. Resize the vertical splitters to allocate input/report height; diagnostics fill the remaining height. Short windows scroll the whole workspace, while reports/tables retain native scrollbars for their contents.

docs.title: 3. Reilley separation
docs.text:
The selected coefficient convention fits each nucleus independently:

\[ \delta_{para}=G_{eff}C_D+F_{eff}\langle S_z\rangle. \]

The Normalization selector offers No normalization, Normalize by S(T) and Normalize by C_D. No normalization fits the original δ_para (ppm) values. The other objectives divide the equation by S(T) or C_D. With Use supplied errors, errors are divided by the absolute same denominator, preserving the original weighted objective. Without weighting, normalized regressions have different objectives and may yield different coefficients. Zero normalization denominators are rejected.

The Result report provides G_eff/F_eff, coefficient standard errors when estimated, rank, scaled-design condition number, residual degrees of freedom, original-space RMSD and per-Ln PCS/FCS predictions. Exactly two Ln points can provide an identifiable two-point estimate but no residual degrees of freedom; R² and residual-based standard errors are withheld. Insufficient/rank-deficient nuclei and missing supplied errors are reported as excluded, rather than omitted.

The plot selector displays δ/〈S_z〉, δ/C_D or PCS/FCS components. Normalized views display the recorded fit in the selected coordinates; changing a plot does not fit another objective. The right plot uses Pred−Exp in original ppm.

docs.title: Coefficients and assumptions
docs.text:
Coefficients shows the values used for the selected temperature. Parameter table shows the full supported relative C_D and RHF spin-factor set. Short references identify Bleaney (1972) and Pinkerton et al. (1985); coefficient identity remains recorded in project/export data.

The default temperature for new inputs is 300 K. Reopening a project preserves its recorded temperature, including existing 303 K analyses. The supplied demo datasets and recorded analyses are generated at 300 K.

The implemented temperature expression is S(T) = a + b × 10⁻⁴ T for Ce, Pr, Nd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm and Yb. Sm/Eu use fixed 300 K values even when a different temperature is selected. C_D is relative and remains constant; effective fitted coefficients absorb this convention at the selected temperature. This is a single-temperature separation model, not a general variable-temperature model. In particular, selecting 303 K does not convert the fixed Sm/Eu values into 303 K coefficients. Prepare each included series at a common measurement temperature; the CSV does not record separate temperatures for measurements.

Pinkerton Table 1 (p. 422) gives the RHF a/b coefficients and 300 K values. Its Sm/Eu values use the full equations (footnote d); Eu additionally uses g = 4.4 for the ground state (footnote e). The application's fixed Sm/Eu values at other temperatures are an approximation, not a linear expression supplied for these ions in that table.

For Reilley and total-shift diagnostics, supply the paramagnetic increment (δ_para = δ_obs − δ_dia, in ppm), rather than the absolute observed chemical shift. The importer does not subtract a diamagnetic reference automatically. The published application describes this subtraction and a dataset-specific Sm outlier; review such cases for your series rather than assuming all included ions are equally reliable.

Reilley separation assumes compatible structures, assignments and coefficient interpretation across the series. Linearity is a diagnostic, not proof of isostructurality. Crystal-field and contact-coupling changes can also affect the trend. See the published Reilley application and assumptions and Pinkerton's spin-polarization paper. Coefficient uncertainties and temperature uncertainty are not propagated; supplied measurement errors are treated as known for coefficient covariance calculations. For the distinction between original-method, coefficient and application sources, see Method References.

docs.title: 4. Retain independent Tensor fitting
docs.text:
Choose Tensor fitting to fit Δχ_ax and Δχ_rh independently for each included PCS dataset. Main geometry, metal and tensor frame stay fixed. Explicit Ref mapping replaces dependence on main visibility or atom selection. Zero-distance metal sites are excluded from the PCS design. Missing Refs are listed; singular designs and incomplete supplied errors are rejected for the affected dataset.

Tensor values use E-32 m³. The report and selected-dataset correlation/residual plots describe the recorded fit. Standardized residuals require supplied errors; otherwise raw ppm residuals remain displayed. This fits no shared metal position, orientation, tensor ratio or cross-ion crystal-field model, and has no Apply-to-Main action. Geometry overrides and torsional averaging are unsupported.

docs.title: 5. Use series diagnostics
docs.text:
• Ln scaling: correlations across matching nuclei against the chosen reference ion, with per-Ln slope/intercept/rank. These diagnostic regressions are unweighted; both-axis measurement uncertainty is not modelled. Total-shift slopes may contain contact contributions and are not certified Bleaney constants.
  • Nuclei diagnostics: choose two distinct nuclei to inspect δ_i/〈S_z〉 versus δ_j/〈S_z〉 and the geometry-subtracted contact difference. An optional distinct third nucleus gives Q_A/Q_B diagnostics. Missing/zero geometry and unmatched denominators are recorded as exclusions. This does not independently determine absolute PCS or supply an anchor contact estimate.
  • Geometry / CFP: compare total-shift ratios with explicit geometry ratios. Relative CFP compares Reilley G_eff against common nonzero G_struct through origin/free-intercept regressions. Ln-varying or near-zero structural factors are excluded from that comparison. Values are relative coefficients under the selected coefficient convention, not absolute energy-unit crystal-field parameters. Ratio checks do not assume that contact contributions vanish automatically.

Empirical absolute separation, anchor-corrected PCS, nonlinear geometry fitting and general uncertainty propagation remain outside this implementation.

docs.title: 6. Transfer deliberately, save and export
docs.text:
From a Current Reilley result, choose PCS transfer quantity:

  • Model PCS: fitted G_eff C_D.
  • Measured − contact: δ_para−F_eff〈S_z〉; it differs from model PCS by the residual.

Review PCS transfer creates local typed PCS datasets and opens Tensor fitting in Ref mapping view. Review their mapping and inclusion before fitting. Existing datasets remain present; avoid including unintended duplicates. Derived values share fitted-coefficient uncertainty and are correlated. Their errors are not silently treated as independent measured errors; transfer leaves supplied-error weighting off. Any subsequent tensor covariance is descriptive, not a calibrated uncertainty propagation from the Reilley analysis. The main PCS table and tensor are not overwritten.

Export result writes the selected recorded analysis as JSON, including stale results. Export Template produces a wide paramagnetic matrix. Projects retain typed inputs, mapping, inclusion, conditions, coefficient convention and a result for each analysis in an optional [multi_lanthanide] section. Loading verifies recorded outputs by deterministic linear replay; it neither launches an analysis worker, replaces those outputs nor applies a tensor. Older projects default to empty Multi-Lanthanide state. These results remain separate from standard Fit History.

docs.title: Orientation Fitting
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer provides two fixed-centre orientation models in the 🔍 Fitting tab. Mode A defines an orientation from selected ligand donors; Mode B applies a general rigid-body Cartesian Euler rotation. Both fit the selected δ_Exp points while leaving the assigned metal position fixed.

The canonical rotation and tensor-frame definitions are given in Coordinate Handling and Tensor Conventions.

docs.title: Mode A: ligand-donor fit
docs.text:
Select Mode A · Ligand-donor, one or more donor Ref IDs, an Axis vector mode, and the PCS observations to fit.

The implementation first constructs a unit donor axis from the assigned metal to the selected donor coordinates. It then fits:

  • θ, the target angle between that donor axis and the positive tensor z-axis; and
  • α, a twist of the rigid structure around the donor axis after the θ alignment.

Both angles start at 0° and are bounded from −180° to +180°. The mathematical polar angle between two vectors is 0–180°, but the optimizer permits a signed −180° to +180° θ parameter because it is used as a rotation target. Do not interpret the fitted θ as an unrestricted conventional spherical polar angle without considering this parameterization.

docs.title: Donor-axis construction
docs.text:
Axis vector mode Construction used by the implementation first Metal-to-first-donor unit vector bisector Normalized sum of the metal-to-donor unit vectors average Same normalized unit-vector sum as bisector centroid Vector from the metal to the arithmetic centroid of donor coordinates normal Normal to the donor plane (two donors define a cross-product normal) pca Principal direction of the donor unit vectors

With one donor, normal and pca reduce to the first donor direction. A degenerate axis construction also falls back to the first donor direction. Plane-normal and PCA directions have an inherent sign ambiguity, so equivalent orientations or different angle signs can occur.

When Δχ_rh is nonzero or fitted, Mode A also applies the current Rotate around Z-axis (°) value from the Rhombicity Table as the in-plane azimuth reference. Changing that control changes the rhombic frame used by the fit while leaving the axial z direction unchanged.

docs.title: Mode B: Euler fit
docs.text:
Select Mode B · Euler and the PCS observations to fit. No donor selection is required. The mode fits a rigid-body rotation about the fixed metal centre using three angles shown in the result as ax, ay, and az.

These are active, extrinsic rotations about fixed Cartesian axes in X → Y → Z order. Angles start at 0° unless Use current tensor as initial guess is selected, and are bounded from −180° to +180°. The Tensor Euler ZYZ controls express the same orientation with different angle values; do not substitute their triplet directly for XYZ.

The fitted az establishes the in-plane reference for a rhombic calculation. For a purely axial tensor, rotation about the tensor z-axis does not change the axial PCS term and may therefore be weakly or non-identifiable.

docs.title: Atom and tensor behavior
docs.text:
The structure is treated as a rigid coordinate set; the selected PCS observations define the residuals, not a set of independently moved atoms. The application uses its current effective geometry, including the averaging-aware geometry factors when symmetry or torsional averaging is enabled.

Use Refresh after changing visibility or assignments. Visibility filters the available observations; it does not make a separately deformable rigid group.

For either mode, Δχ_ax and Δχ_rh may be fitted or held at their current values. Mode A supports Preview Geometry only. Mode B Apply to Tensor copies Δχ_ax and orientation, retaining the existing Δχ_rh and rhombic enablement; its preview changes only the geometry override. See Fitting Overview for initialization and application and Quality Metrics for the report fields.

docs.title: Fitting Overview
docs.text:
The 🔍 Fitting tab optimizes PCS predictions against selected δ_Exp assignments. It provides three orientation/centre models and a common result report. The separate 🔍 Advanced Fitting tab contains several fixed- geometry workflows described at the end of this page.

Standard Mode B/C Apply to Tensor is recorded in the active document's Undo/Redo history. Undo restores the previous tensor and any geometry preview removed by Apply; recorded Fit History remains available. Redo restores the applied values without rerunning fitting. Mode A's geometry-preview workflow is unchanged.

docs.title: Inputs shared by the standard fitting modes
docs.text:
Before fitting, provide:

  1. a loaded structure with a valid metal-centre assignment;
  2. experimental PCS values as δ_Exp or structured observations;
  3. a current Δχ_ax value and, when used, Δχ_rh; and
  4. enough independent selected PCS observations to constrain the parameters.

Selecting Fitting exposes its contextual Ribbon: Run Fit, initialization options, Refresh (the Refresh Inputs command), Apply Tensor (Apply to Tensor), Preview (Preview Geometry), Clear Preview, Fit History, and Export Plot (Export Fit Plot). Model and observation choices remain in the analysis area. These commands act on the active document.

Choose Refresh after changing the structure, filter, or assignments. PCS observations lists structured assignments when available; otherwise it lists visible proton Ref IDs with legacy δ_Exp data. Select at least three valid observations and substantially more when fitting several parameters. A grouped target contributes one residual, regardless of its atom count; see Structured observations.

Mode C rejects a run with fewer than three matched PCS observations. Modes A and B currently enforce only that the selections are nonempty; they can therefore start an underdetermined fit with fewer than three matched points. Avoid using that permissive behavior as evidence that the data are sufficient.

Mode A also requires one or more non-hydrogen Ref IDs from its donor list.

docs.title: Standard fitting modes
docs.text:
UI mode Always fitted Optionally fitted Fixed in this mode Mode A · Ligand-donor donor-axis θ and axial twist α Δχ_ax, Δχ_rh metal position Mode B · Euler global ax, ay, az orientation Δχ_ax, Δχ_rh metal position Mode C · Full tensor + metal three Euler angles and metal x, y, z Δχ_ax, Δχ_rh unchecked tensor components

Mode C has six, seven, or eight variable parameters depending on the Fit Δχ_ax and Fit Δχ_rh checkboxes. See Full Tensor Fitting.

docs.title: Fitted and fixed tensor components
docs.text:
Fit Δχ_ax and Fit Δχ_rh determine whether each component is included in the parameter vector. An unchecked component is read from the current main-window value and held fixed. Tensor inputs and results use units of \(10^{-32}\,\mathrm{m^3}\) per molecule.

Rhombic fits require a defined in-plane frame because the rhombic term depends on azimuth. See Orientation Fitting and Tensor Conventions.

docs.title: Initialization, bounds, and optimization
docs.text:
By default, orientation angles start at 0° and tensor parameters start from the current Δχ values. Use current tensor as initial guess initializes Mode B/C from the current tensor orientation and components; it is unavailable for Mode A. Mode C still starts at the assigned metal position.

Orientation angles are restricted to −180° to +180°. Mode C restricts each metal coordinate to ±1 Å around the assigned starting centre. Tensor components are not bounded in the final refinement.

Global search (DE) searches for an initial solution before local refinement; it can help with starting-point sensitivity but does not establish uniqueness. Its preliminary search restricts tensor components to the current value ±50 in the application's Δχ units. Compare runs from different initial assumptions.

docs.title: Weighting
docs.text: Weighting: Unweighted minimizes the sum of squared residuals in ppm. Experimental uncertainty divides each residual by that observation's uncertainty σ in ppm before optimization. Every selected observation must have a finite, strictly positive σ; missing, zero, negative, or non-finite values reject the run. Uncertainty belongs to the experimental observation, including when its target contains several atoms. See Quality Metrics.

docs.title: Running and applying a fit
docs.text:
1. Select a mode and the required observations/donors.
  2. Choose fitted tensor components, initialization, and weighting.
  3. Select Run Fit and inspect the parameters, metrics and per-observation residuals.
  4. Choose Apply to Tensor to change the current tensor, or Preview Geometry to inspect the fitted geometry using a temporary override.
Mode Apply to Tensor Preview Geometry A Unavailable: the donor-dependent orientation is not applied to the current tensor Previews donor-axis orientation; does not copy fitted Δχ inputs B Applies fitted Δχ_ax and orientation; retains the current Δχ_rh and its enablement Previews XYZ orientation; does not copy fitted Δχ inputs C Applies Δχ_ax, Δχ_rh and orientation; retains rhombic enablement and the assigned metal position Previews orientation and refined metal position; also fills the Δχ input fields

Tensor application clears an existing geometry override and refreshes the views. It does not change Prediction model or enable rhombicity automatically. Check both controls when comparing the main prediction with a fit that used a rhombic term. Mode B application retains the existing rhombic value even if that component was fitted.

Preview Geometry uses the existing visualization override and redraws immediately. Mode C also uses its fitted Δχ input values in that redraw; it does not apply fitted orientation to the canonical tensor. Clear Preview removes the geometry override while retaining current tensor settings. Both actions support document Undo/Redo. Undoing Preview restores the previous geometry and tensor values; Undoing Clear restores the removed preview. The refined metal position is temporary and is not adopted as the project's assigned centre. Consequently, Mode C's post-application main predictions can differ from its fit report, which used the refined centre.

Fit History retains runs for inspection and comparison. Results marked Stale cannot be applied or previewed because fit inputs changed. Unknown means validity could not be established, not that the result is current; review its inputs. Restoring or inspecting a run does not automatically apply it. Export Fit Plot saves the standard figure as PNG or PDF.

Note

A completed optimization is not evidence that the model is unique or scientifically appropriate. Compare parameter count with the number and spatial distribution of observations, inspect residuals, and test sensitivity to initialization and fixed assumptions.

The result header shows the mode, observation count, RMSD, R² and validity. The report distinguishes fitted and fixed values and lists residuals; the figure shows predicted versus experimental PCS and signed residual bars. RMSD remains in ppm even for weighted fits; χ²/N is uncertainty-normalized chi-square per datum, not reduced chi-square. See Quality Metrics.

Mode B fitting result for Nd(iPr₂BA)₃.

This example fits Δχ_ax to the phenyl assignments with unweighted residuals; the iPr assignments are excluded. Its 15 selected Ref assignments span symmetry-related ligands and do not represent 15 independent experimental resonances.

docs.title: Current advanced fitting workflows
docs.text: The following workflows are implemented under 🔍 Advanced Fitting. They do not replace the standard orientation and metal-position fit. Multi-Conformer uses its own structure collection and observation selection; the other workflows use the current selected atom set and geometry.

docs.title: Multi-Conformer
docs.text:
For a worked example with current screenshots, see the Multi-Conformer fitting and reliability tutorial.

Use at least two included conformers and three matched PCS observations. The model averages structure-specific PCS, assuming fast exchange and a shared tensor with fixed orientation. It does not predict PCS from averaged coordinates.

Use the contextual Ribbon Use Current or Load XYZ commands (XYZ, OUT and LOG are supported). The current structure is copied in full; main visibility filters do not determine its atom mapping. Imported files require Map / frame or a row double-click/Enter to confirm chemical Ref correspondence, the file's own metal origin and its frame. Equal atom counts or element sequences do not confirm identity. Different file row orders are supported through explicit Ref mappings.

In Fit settings, choose a confirmed common frame or metal-centered core alignment with at least three noncollinear corresponding anchors. Core alignment uses proper rotations without shifting the metal origin; inspect the recorded alignment RMSD. For exported coordinates already in the tensor axes, explicitly choose Already tensor-oriented in the row editor to prevent a second rotation; do not combine those inputs with core alignment. An active main geometry override is unsupported by this fixed-frame workflow and must be cleared before fitting.

Use Select PCS for observation selection, independently of main atom selection. Structured observations take precedence over legacy δ_Exp inputs. Member/site and pseudo/torsion reductions occur within each conformer before population averaging.

Fit settings offers tensor, populations or both. Edit inclusion, initial population and Fixed population in each Analysis row. Fixed populations retain their values; only the remaining mass is fitted, with nonnegative populations summing to one. Fixed totals greater than one are rejected. Fit Δχ_ax and Fit Δχ_rh enable scalar variables; clearing either holds its specified local value fixed, including a nonzero fixed rhombic value. populations holds both specified scalars fixed. Unweighted fitting is the default; uncertainty weighting requires a positive supplied uncertainty for every selected observation.

For both, seeded multi-start combines user/uniform and random feasible starts (default eight, maximum twenty). Results retain starts, failures, fixed/fitted conditions, raw PCS RMSD, objective, predictions and predicted-minus-experimental residuals. Rank deficiencies and similar-quality population alternatives warn about ambiguity; convergence does not establish unique populations or a global optimum. After a successful current fit, Reliability in the Ribbon Results group opens bootstrap and grouped cross-validation settings. Parametric bootstrap requires independent PCS observations with known positive uncertainties; cases resamples independent observation groups with replacement. Every replicate refits the selected free tensor/population variables. Fixed values, orientation and geometry are retained. Overlapping physical members/shared source observables stay together in cases resampling and CV; parametric evaluation rejects them without a covariance model.

The report records refit counts/failures, approximate marginal percentile intervals, training-only out-of-sample PCS RMSD and similar-PCS conformer groups. Insufficient successful refits or ambiguous/rank-deficient individual estimates withhold intervals. Fixed parameters have no estimated interval. Failed CV folds remain visible and a partial pooled score is labelled accordingly. Similarity groups are suggestions at the fitted tensor, not automatic merges or guarantees of structural equivalence; their aggregate ranges are descriptive. Population boundaries, unmodelled errors and correlated measurements limit interpretation. Multi-start variation is not a confidence interval. Evaluation runs in the background and neither Applies the tensor nor changes the original fit. JSON exports/projects retain its assumptions and runs. Evaluation uses recorded uncertainties; after editing σ, refit before evaluating again, including when an unweighted fit's objective still remains Current.

The Multi-Conformer tutorial provides ready-to-open informative and ambiguous-conformer projects. Their coordinates are synthetic labelled probes, not a chemically optimized molecule or experimental validation.

The report uses recorded conditions even after live inputs change. Apply is enabled only for a current successful result with fitted scalar fields, and applies only those fields. It preserves main orientation, metal, rhombic enablement and prediction policy. It neither applies local fixed overrides nor installs ensemble predictions in the main table. Results are separate from standard Fit History. Export result saves recorded inputs, runs and conformer contributions as JSON; the dedicated .pcsp section retains source coordinates without requiring the original files on reopen. Use the whole-tab scrollbar and report/plot splitters for shorter windows.

docs.title: Joint PCS+RDC
docs.text:
This workflow fits Δχ_ax and Δχ_rh with the main metal position and tensor orientation fixed. Select Joint PCS+RDC within Advanced Fitting. The contextual Ribbon provides Run Fit, Fit settings, Select PCS, Load RDC CSV, Validate inputs, Apply, Export result and Export Template. Controls are separate from the Analysis data/results area.

RDC CSVs accept explicit raw-atom ref1/ref2 columns (recommended), or unambiguous atom1/atom2 labels matching the structure. Required rdc_exp values are in Hz. rdc_err defaults to 0.5 Hz when omitted; nuc1/nuc2 default to H/N. Explicit nuclear types H/1H, N/15N and C/13C are supported. Unknown labels/Refs are listed as skipped rows. Duplicate matched bonds, unsupported nuclei and invalid measured values/errors are rejected.

Fit settings provides field \(B_0\), temperature, an RDC residual multiplier and optional PCS uncertainty weighting. RDC residuals are divided by max(rdc_err, 0.1 Hz) and multiplied by the RDC multiplier, so its square scales their contribution to the objective. Without PCS uncertainty weighting, PCS residuals retain the legacy unit-ppm scale. With it enabled, every selected PCS observation must have a positive supplied uncertainty. Structured PCS target reductions use the existing PCS model. This joint model requires magnetic self-alignment; RDCs from external alignment media must not be treated as susceptibility-coupled data. Torsional averaging is not supported by its fixed-bond RDC model.

Input data can be collapsed; vertical splitters resize the data, selectable report and two-plot region. A whole-tab scrollbar provides access in short windows. Correlation and Residuals show separate PCS/RDC diagnostics with ppm/Hz units; residuals are predicted minus experimental. The report records execution conditions, PCS/RDC RMSDs, per-observation values, matching diagnostics, rank and condition number. Input changes mark the recorded result Stale. Apply requires a Current successful result and copies only the two fitted scalar fields, preserving orientation, metal and main prediction settings. Export result writes the recorded inputs and diagnostics as JSON, including stale results; it does not export live controls.

The fixed-frame solver uses linear least squares and rejects data that cannot independently determine both tensor components. Unknown nuclear types and nonpositive RDC uncertainties are rejected rather than silently substituted. RDC prediction uses molecular susceptibility in E-32 m³ with \(A=B_0^2\Delta\chi/(15\mu_0 k_B T)\), without a molar Avogadro conversion. This corrects an earlier RDC scale error; previously obtained joint-fit results should be recomputed. The existing signed RDC convention is retained. The numerical example in the Joint PCS+RDC tutorial checks known parameter recovery against independent Cartesian equations. Its coordinates are synthetic probes, not an experimentally validated molecular model.

The optional [joint_pcs_rdc] project section retains inputs, settings and the last verified result. Older projects receive defaults; reopening does not fit or apply automatically.
