No confidence intervals are estimated by this fit. See the Joint PCS+RDC tutorial for prepared noiseless/noisy/rank-deficient projects and illustrated workflows.

docs.title: PRE
docs.text:
The PRE tab fits one effective correlation time from proton increments Γ₂=R₂,para−R₂,dia at fixed raw geometry, metal position, field and moment. Fit conditions sits above the Input data table and collapses with it. The Ribbon provides Run Fit, Load PRE CSV, Validate inputs, Export result and Export Template. There is no PRE Fit settings popup.

Select supplied-error weighting or the legacy assumed-error rule; set positive τ_c bounds (default 0.001–1000 ns). The report records execution conditions, matching, time, boundary status, RMSD and weighted residual sum of squares. Distance profile, correlation, standardized residuals and a recorded-data τ_c objective scan support inspection. Confidence intervals are not estimated. The fixed-field amplitude fit uses a bounded monotonic inverse. This simplified proton Γ₂ model does not include full SBM/Curie relaxation, R₁ fitting or ensemble-distance averaging. A preset fills μ_eff; it does not validate the relaxation model for that ion.

PRE inputs, options and a verified result round-trip in projects without refitting or changing the main tensor. See the PRE tutorial for canonical/paired-rate CSVs, legacy alias warnings, synthetic examples and actual screenshots.

docs.title: Multi-Lanthanide
docs.text:
The contextual Ribbon Analysis selector retains independent Tensor fitting and adds Reilley separation, Ln scaling, Nuclei diagnostics, Geometry / CFP and Parameter table. Input conditions and tables collapse together; Result and selected-target diagnostic plots share adjustable sashes.

Tensor fitting uses PCS and explicit main Ref mapping, with the main metal/frame fixed and independent axial/rhombic scalars per dataset. Reilley uses total paramagnetic shifts, δ_para (ppm) = δ_obs−δ_dia, for matching nuclei across Ln. Direct and two normalized objectives (Normalization: No normalization / Normalize by S(T) / Normalize by C_D) support supplied errors with corresponding error scaling, rank/conditioning checks, two-point diagnostics and explicit exclusions.

The compact Coefficients table inside Fit conditions displays included Ln values, C_D and S(T), with short Bleaney/Pinkerton references. Temperature and coefficient identity are recorded; new inputs default to 300 K and saved temperatures are preserved. Sm/Eu retain fixed 300 K values. This is a single-temperature separation model. Ln scaling/nucleus/geometry checks are conditional diagnostics, not proof of a shared structure or independent absolute PCS separation. CFP comparisons are relative, not absolute energy-unit estimates.

Review PCS transfer creates local typed datasets from a Current Reilley result; it does not overwrite main PCS or Apply a tensor. Separated values share coefficient uncertainty. Projects retain typed inputs/conditions and verified results per analysis; JSON export retains recorded inputs and diagnostics. See the Multi-Lanthanide and Reilley tutorial for formats, assumptions, synthetic examples and actual screenshots.

docs.title: PRE tutorial
docs.text: Use Advanced Fitting → PRE to estimate one effective correlation time from proton transverse PRE increments, Γ₂=R₂,para−R₂,dia. Structure, metal position, magnetic field and effective moment remain fixed. This is a simplified proton Γ₂ model; the fitted time is not necessarily pure rotational tumbling.

docs.title: 1. Open the example
docs.text:
Use the example inputs supplied with the release; see finding the files. Open examples/pre_demo/noisy/demo.pcsp using File → Open PCS Project.... Select Advanced Fitting → PRE. The project contains six synthetic proton probes, supplied errors and a recorded successful result, restored as Current. These coordinates are not a chemically optimized molecular structure. The project already contains the geometry, PRE observations and fit conditions; do not import pre.csv again for this exercise. Short paths such as noiseless/demo.pcsp are relative to examples/pre_demo/.

The exact generating time is 3 ns at 14.1 T and μ_eff=3.68 μB. Fixed small perturbations give a fitted time of approximately 3.01264 ns. The separate noiseless/demo.pcsp verifies recovery of 3 ns to numerical precision.

docs.title: 2. Review inputs and conditions
docs.text:
Expand Input data. Fit conditions sits above the matching table. The top row contains B₀ (T), Ln preset, μ_eff (μB) and Weighting; the second row pairs the τ_c range (ns) with the model description. Shorter widths reflow the fields. Collapsing Input data hides the conditions and table together; no settings popup is needed.

Ln preset supplies a moment; the equation uses the displayed moment. Changing it manually selects Custom. The default positive bounds are 0.001–1000 ns. Keep supplied-error weighting selected for this demo. Every matched observation then needs a positive uncertainty. With weighting unchecked, the existing assumed-error rule is used: σ=max(0.05 Γ₂,Exp, 0.1 s⁻¹). The report identifies this assumption.

Load PRE CSV in the Ribbon reads integer raw-atom Ref IDs. For example:

ref_id,gamma2,gamma2_err,nucleus
1,3862.897755468303,188.43403685211234,1H

Rates and errors are in s⁻¹. ref/id and g2 are accepted aliases. Alternatively, provide r2_para,r2_dia; their difference is used. If both r2_para_err,r2_dia_err are supplied, their root-sum-square gives σ under an independent-error assumption. Single r2_para or r2 columns remain legacy increment aliases and trigger an interpretation warning: they must already contain the PRE difference, not raw R₂.

Only raw hydrogen atoms are supported. Missing Refs are listed as unmatched; duplicates, non-finite values, invalid errors, unsupported nuclei and protons at the metal centre are rejected. Signed noisy increments are accepted; nonpositive measured values use linear diagnostic axes. Main visibility and atom selection do not silently remove PRE observations. Geometry overrides and torsional averaging are unsupported in this fixed-distance model.

docs.title: 3. Fit and inspect
docs.text:
Use Validate inputs, then Run Fit in the Ribbon. The fit runs in the background and does not Apply a susceptibility tensor. The selectable report records conditions, errors, matching, effective time, boundary status, Γ₂ RMSD, weighted residual sum of squares and per-proton predictions.

Distance profile shows measured Γ₂ with errors and the fitted distance dependence, alongside standardized residuals (Pred−Exp)/σ. Correlation shows measured versus predicted rates with an identity line. Legends use automatic placement. Splitters resize input, report and plots; plots fill remaining height. A whole-tab scrollbar keeps the content accessible in short windows.

Select τ_c scan to replace the residual plot with the actual weighted objective evaluated against the recorded observations and errors. The vertical line marks the fitted time; this curve is not a confidence interval.

For the noisy example, Γ₂ RMSD is approximately 39.4181 s⁻¹ and the weighted sum of squares is approximately 2.14833. The latter is not reduced chi-square or a likelihood-based confidence statement. Confidence intervals are not estimated.

docs.title: 4. Recognize a boundary solution
docs.text:
Open examples/pre_demo/boundary/demo.pcsp. Its same observations require approximately 3 ns, but the allowed upper bound is 1 ns. The fit reaches that bound and the report explicitly identifies a boundary solution and poor residuals.

Review bounds and model assumptions rather than interpreting a bounded optimum as a precise physical estimate. A changed live field, moment, geometry, data or objective marks a recorded result Stale; plots and report still use its recorded execution inputs. Main tensor orientation does not enter this isotropic distance model.

docs.title: 5. Save and export
docs.text: Export result saves recorded inputs, predictions and diagnostics as JSON, including stale results. Export Template produces canonical Γ₂ columns. Saving the project retains PRE data, conditions and the last verified result in an optional section. Reopening verifies it without refitting. PRE results remain separate from standard Fit History and do not alter the main susceptibility tensor.

docs.title: Model and limits
docs.text:
The existing simplified proton forward equation is retained:

\[ \Gamma_2(r)=\frac{1}{15}\left(\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\right)^2 \gamma_H^2(\mu_{eff}\mu_B)^2 r^{-6} \left(4\tau_c+\frac{3\tau_c}{1+(\gamma_H B_0\tau_c)^2}\right). \]

The implementation converts Å to metres and ns to seconds. At fixed field, moment and distances, all rates share a single amplitude. Weighted amplitude fitting followed by a bounded monotonic inverse finds the one-parameter optimum. Moment and time are not fitted together from one field.

This omits additional electron-frequency terms and Curie relaxation; presets alone do not validate that simplification for a given ion. There is no R₁ fit, multi-field fit, ensemble-distance averaging or general-nucleus model. See the Xplor-NIH PRE model description and the relaxation-model discussion, equations 12–14 for assumptions behind simplified transverse PRE expressions.

docs.title: Quality Metrics
docs.text:
The standard Mode A, B, and C reports calculate their metrics from the same per-point values. Let

\[ e_i=\delta_{\mathrm{pred},i}-\delta_{\mathrm{Exp},i} \]

be the fitting residual and let \(N\) be the number of matched, selected experimental observations. A grouped target counts once, not once per member atom. RMSD, R², Q and Raw SSE/N below use raw ppm residuals even in a weighted fit.

docs.title: RMSD
docs.text:
\[ \mathrm{RMSD} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{N}\sum_i e_i^2}. \]

RMSD is reported in ppm. It describes the typical residual magnitude but does not account for the number of fitted parameters.

docs.title: R²
docs.text:
\[ R^2 = 1- \frac{\sum_i e_i^2} {\sum_i(\delta_{\mathrm{Exp},i}-\overline{\delta}_{\mathrm{Exp}})^2}. \]

R² is omitted when the experimental values have essentially zero variance. It can be negative when the predictions are worse than using the experimental mean as a constant prediction.

docs.title: Q-factor
docs.text:
\[ Q = \sqrt{ \frac{\sum_i e_i^2} {\sum_i\delta_{\mathrm{Exp},i}^2} }. \]

The Q-factor is omitted when the squared experimental values sum to essentially zero.

docs.title: Raw SSE/N
docs.text:
The report's Raw SSE/N is

\[ \frac{1}{N}\sum_i e_i^2=\mathrm{RMSD}^2. \]

It is an unweighted mean squared residual in ppm², not a chi-square statistic.

docs.title: Experimental-uncertainty weighting
docs.text:
With Weighting: Experimental uncertainty, the optimizer minimizes

\[ \chi^2=\sum_i\left(\frac{e_i}{\sigma_i}\right)^2, \]

where each \(\sigma_i\) is the supplied uncertainty of one experimental observation in ppm. All selected uncertainties must be finite and strictly positive. The report adds χ² = Σ(resid/σ)² and χ²/N (weighted), both dimensionless. These are separate from the raw ppm metrics above.

The denominator N is the observation count, not N minus the number of fitted parameters. χ²/N (weighted) is chi-square per datum, not reduced chi-square. Its statistical interpretation depends on whether the uncertainties and error model are appropriate; grouping does not supply extra independent data.

docs.title: Residual displays
docs.text:
The standard fitting report lists the five largest absolute residuals and a complete per-point table. Its correlation plot compares δ_Exp with predicted PCS, colors points by absolute residual, and labels each point with its Ref ID. The residual bars use fixed display thresholds:

  • green: |residual| ≤ 0.05 ppm;
  • orange: 0.05 < |residual| ≤ 0.15 ppm;
  • red: |residual| > 0.15 ppm.

These fixed plot thresholds are distinct from the editable cutoffs shared by the main and Rhombicity tables. Those tables default to 0.10 and 0.30 ppm; changing their cutoffs does not change the Fitting plot. See Residual Analysis for table controls and persistence.

docs.title: Metrics in other workflows
docs.text:
Workflow Metrics shown by the current UI Main G_ax vs PCS linear regression R², residual SD, RMSE, slope/intercept standard errors and 95% confidence intervals, and a converted Δχ_ax 95% confidence interval Rhombicity Check axial-only residual RMSD; Pearson r and R² for residual versus Grh Advanced Multi-Conformer PCS RMSD, recorded objective, fitted/fixed populations and tensor components, and attempted starts. Optional reliability evaluation adds conditional bootstrap intervals, held-out RMSD and ambiguity warnings; detailed sensitivity/rank records are retained in result JSON. Advanced Joint PCS+RDC Separate PCS RMSD (ppm) and RDC RMSD (Hz), rank, condition number and weighted residual sum of squares. There is no combined raw-unit RMSD. Advanced PRE Γ₂ RMSD (s⁻¹), weighted residual sum of squares, effective τ_c and whether the solution reaches a selected bound. Advanced Multi-Lanthanide Independent tensor RMSD per dataset; Reilley G_eff/F_eff with conditional standard errors, rank, condition, residual degrees of freedom and original-space RMSD (ppm). Other modes provide their own diagnostic regression metrics.

Standard nonlinear Mode A/B/C fits do not report parameter covariance or nonlinear confidence intervals. Joint PCS+RDC and PRE do not estimate confidence intervals either. The 95% intervals from the main G_ax regression belong to that linear model and must not be transferred to another workflow.

Multi-Conformer bootstrap intervals and held-out errors are conditional on its recorded geometry, assignments, model and resampling assumptions. Ambiguous individual populations can have their intervals withheld; a reported group interval is not proof of unique individual populations. See the reliability tutorial.

Reilley coefficient errors use supplied measurement uncertainties as known when weighting is enabled, or estimated residual variance otherwise. Exactly two points have no residual degrees of freedom and no reported coefficient errors or R². Coefficient-table and temperature uncertainty are not propagated. See Reilley coefficients and assumptions.

Compare weighted objectives only when inputs, error scales and residual definitions are compatible. Joint PCS+RDC includes its configured RDC multiplier/error floor; PRE can use assumed errors instead of supplied uncertainties. These sums are not automatically reduced chi-square. Workflow details are in the Joint PCS+RDC and PRE tutorials.

docs.title: Comparing residual signs
docs.text:
Standard fitting and advanced fitting store residuals as predicted minus experimental. The main table's residual colouring also uses calculated minus δ_Exp. In contrast, Rhombicity Check and the Rhombicity Table display experimental minus predicted. Always check the workflow before interpreting the sign; absolute-value rankings and RMSD are unchanged.

See Residual Analysis for selection, colouring, and export behavior.

docs.title: Tutorial: Standard fitting and rhombicity
docs.text: Use examples/standard_fitting_demo/ from the source checkout or portable release. The conditions and known values are listed below. These synthetic geometrical probes are not a chemically optimized molecule or experimental data. Short paths below are relative to examples/standard_fitting_demo/; see finding the example files.

docs.title: Choose the exercise
docs.text:
Each project has 32 H observations, Nd Ref 1 and donor N Ref 2. Coordinates are Å; PCS is ppm; tensor scalars are E-32 m³. The noiseless input uses 0.02 ppm as an objective scale. This is not measured precision or added random noise.

Project Mode Known answer mode_a/demo.pcsp A, first donor Ref 2 Axial 12, rhombic 0; θ=20°, α=25° mode_b/demo.pcsp B Axial 12, rhombic 3; extrinsic XYZ 12°, −8°, 18° mode_c/demo.pcsp C Same tensor; centre (0.20, −0.15, 0.10) Å axial/demo.pcsp Diagnostic reference Axial 12, rhombic 0; zero orientation rhombic/demo.pcsp Diagnostic comparison Axial 12, rhombic 3; zero orientation

docs.title: Fit and review
docs.text:
Open a project and select Fitting. Expand Fit settings, verify the restored mode and its Mode details, select all 32 PCS observations and verify the count. Project loading does not restore row selection. For A, select donor Ref 2 and Axis vector mode: first, fitting only Δχ_ax. For B/C, fit both tensor components. Keep the saved uncertainty weighting and disable global search for this reproducible exercise.

Choose Run Fit in the Ribbon. Expect RMSD below 0.00001 ppm after coordinate rounding, recovered axial 12 and rhombic 3 in B/C. C recovers the centre listed above. Equivalent angular representations can describe the same predictions; this exercise does not establish global uniqueness or statistical precision.

Repeat a fit and compare recorded conditions in Fit History. The supplied projects contain inputs only. Apply/preview behavior matters:

  • A previews donor-axis geometry; Apply to Tensor is unavailable.
  • B applies orientation/axial values while retaining the existing rhombic value.
  • C applies tensor/orientation while preserving the assigned metal position; Preview Geometry uses the refined centre temporarily.

See standard fitting behavior. Reopen the source project between exercises to reset all working values, or use Clear Preview to remove only temporary geometry; save practice results to a separate project.

To practice Mode C persistence, run the fit, choose Preview Geometry, and save to a new .pcsp path. Preview redraws immediately. Close that document and reopen the saved copy. The preview centre, orientation and displayed PCS should match; the assigned metal centre stays unchanged and Fit History retains the run. Opening the supplied input-only project instead starts with no preview.

Mode A: selected donor Ref 2, fitted θ/α and axial tensor. Settings are collapsed and the selectable report is scrolled to the fitted parameters.

Mode C: the refined centre and tensor are recorded in the result. The main metal assignment and main tensor have not been replaced by running the fit.

docs.title: Compare rhombicity diagnostics
docs.text:
Open axial/demo.pcsp, select Rhombicity Check, and choose Update Diagnostic with structure and δ_Exp ready. Repeat with rhombic/demo.pcsp, all observations and zero orientation. The first dataset has negligible axial-only residuals. The second leaves structured residuals that the rhombic term explains.

Inspect residual against φ/G_rh, reconstructed tensor and Rhombicity Table. A two-column G_ax/G_rh fit recovers 12 / 3 for the rhombic case. The diagnostic residual is δ_Exp−δ_Pred; standard fit reports use the opposite sign. Preserve the frame when comparing the two projects. This controlled comparison excludes contact shifts and structural uncertainty; it is not an experimental acceptance criterion. See rhombicity definitions.

docs.title: Batch Processing
docs.text: Use VT Series → Batch Processing…, Processing → Batch Processing… in the Workbench panel, or VT stacked → Batch to review processing for multiple experiments. The panel action can also use selected experiments without a VT series. Settings describe an ordered recipe; each dataset retains its own committed history and provenance.

docs.title: Choose targets and the starting spectrum
docs.text:
Select a series and check the experiments to process. The All header selects/clears targets. Row selection browses a spectrum; it is not the batch target selection. Included members are initially checked. Checking an excluded member authorizes this batch only and does not change series inclusion.

Starting point Behavior Current spectrum Continue from committed processing. Untouched raw FIDs can receive default vendor preprocessing/FT automatically. Original FID Restart from available raw data. Review the visible Fourier Transform step and operation order. A processed-only dataset cannot recover an absent FID.

Resolve any single-spectrum preview with Apply or Cancel before including that experiment in a batch. Repeating a phase correction on an already corrected current spectrum applies another correction.

docs.title: Build and review the recipe
docs.text:
1. Set each operation On/Off. Drag operation rows to change their order.
  2. Select an operation and enter parameters. Set common stores its batch-wide settings; it does not process spectra.
  3. For an experiment-specific setting, select that experiment and choose Set for selected. Clear selected overrides clears its operation overrides so common settings apply again.
  4. Choose Preview checked. Inspect member results/warnings and the Committed, Preview or Overlay spectrum view.
  5. Choose Apply reviewed previews and confirm explicitly. Failed/skipped experiments remain unchanged; changed source inputs require fresh review.

Five synthetic members are ready; no batch result has been committed in this capture. The experiment list and long result messages can be scrolled. The blue input trace includes deliberate phase, baseline and reference errors.

The usual tutorial sequence is Phase → Baseline → Reference → Peak Picking. Apodization/zero filling and FT have different input requirements; enable them only as intended for your starting data. Cancel discards pending previews. Preview does not replace peaks or write committed processing history.

docs.title: Reference each experiment independently
docs.text:
Choose Reference type, compound/signal and Target position (ppm). A common Search region is evaluated separately in every experiment and must contain exactly one detected candidate per member. Missing/multiple candidates are reported rather than assigned silently. A manual observed position is a per-experiment override, not one shared observed peak position.

Reference presets do not establish peak identity or correct condition-dependent shifts automatically. Inspect their nucleus and temperature applicability. Phase pivot is the origin of a phase ramp, not a chemical-shift reference.

Batch picker thresholds are fractions: 0.01 means 1%, unlike the percentage fields in the single-spectrum picker. Minimum separation is in spectral points, not ppm. Automatic replacement preserves manual peaks but can remove old automatic IDs and invalidate track links. Processing/referencing changes can also stale links; review tracking again.

docs.title: Reuse settings
docs.text:
Use Preset, Name, Save and Delete to manage reusable recipes. Series presets retain configured targets/overrides. A preset saved from a selected-experiment batch is a Workbench common preset without member IDs or individual overrides; loading it keeps current checked targets and clears individual overrides. Save the NMR session to retain presets.

For known settings and expected results, follow the VT tutorial.

docs.title: NMR Data and Observed-Shift Tables
docs.text: Open Inspector → NMR Data in NMR Workbench. This table combines picked spectral peaks and prepared observed shifts. You can start with a spectrum, import a shift table, paste values, or add observations manually. Prepared values do not require an FID or manufacture spectral peaks.

docs.title: Read and filter the table
docs.text:
Choose Experiment (Active experiment, All experiments, or a named experiment) and Show (All, Assigned, or Unassigned). Click a column heading to sort; use the horizontal scrollbar for additional columns.

Column Meaning Use Include this assigned observation in single-pair shift comparison/PCS preparation. Click to toggle; unassigned peaks must first be assigned. Assignment Correspondence label used for pairing, not an inferred structural target. Shift / ppm Absolute observed chemical shift, not Δshift or experimental PCS. Source Spectrum-linked, manually entered/imported, or read-only PCS-project data. Status Readiness or diagnostics, including unassigned/duplicate labels, changed source shifts and missing conditions. Experiment, Role, Nucleus, T / K Dataset identity and conditions. σ / ppm Provided shift uncertainty; leave blank if unknown. Intensity, Picking Peak height and manual/automatic picking source when a spectral peak exists.

Use does not change VT series member inclusion or a VT analysis fit mask. Display filtering does not remove data. Check diagnostics even when a row is included; a check mark alone does not establish scientific suitability.

For spectrum-linked rows, double-click Assignment or press Enter; Tab advances and Shift+Tab goes back. See Peaks and Assignments.

docs.title: Add or edit prepared values
docs.text:
1. Choose Add and select New experiment or an existing editable experiment.
  2. For a new experiment, enter its name, nucleus, role and temperature in Kelvin where known. Existing experiment conditions remain those of that experiment.
  3. Enter Assignment, Shift / ppm, and optional Uncertainty / ppm.
  4. Set Use in shift comparison, then choose Save.

Use More → Edit details… for an existing observation. Independent shifts can be edited. A spectrum-linked shift stays owned by its source peak and is read-only in this dialog; change spectral processing/referencing instead of overwriting its measurement. Uncertainty, if supplied, must be finite and positive.

More → Remove selected… asks before removing a value. For a spectrum row it removes the source peak and linked observation, which can stale track links. More → Clear picked peaks in active experiment… concerns peaks, not all independent observations. Review the confirmation before clearing.

docs.title: Import CSV or TSV
docs.text:
The synthetic FID/CSV tutorial supplies this four-row table. The screenshot shows Preview only; nothing has been applied.

  1. Choose Import → Observed shifts CSV / TSV…, or Paste observed shifts….
  2. Review the text and fallback Name, Nucleus, and Role. File metadata can supply these conditions instead. Temperature values are in Kelvin.
  3. Use Read columns after changing headings. Map Assignment and Shift to distinct columns; inspect the automatic mapping before accepting it.
  4. Choose Preview and check experiment, assignment, shift and role.
  5. Choose Apply explicitly. Import does not pair experiments or transfer PCS.

Use UTF-8 (a BOM is accepted) and a header row. The chooser accepts .csv, .tsv, and .txt; comma, tab and semicolon delimiters are supported. For example:

assignment,shift_ppm,experiment,role,nucleus,temperature_k
H1,2.0,Paramagnetic,paramagnetic,1H,298.15
H2,5.0,Paramagnetic,paramagnetic,1H,298.15

assignment and shift_ppm are the recommended headings. Common aliases such as Ref/Label and Shift/ppm can be mapped, but a Ref-looking label does not automatically accept a structural target. The import accepts absolute observed shifts; do not map δ_para, Δshift, PCS or δ_Exp as an observed shift.

A legacy wide table with both δ_obs and δ_dia can create separate paramagnetic and diamagnetic observations. Blank entries in those two columns are omitted and numeric zero is retained. In a regular single-shift table, a missing or invalid shift is an error. These are not the set/clear rules of the PCS-project importers.

Repeated assignments are retained and diagnosed; they are not automatically averaged. Changing import settings/text invalidates the review: Preview again before Apply. Then choose the experiments explicitly in Shift Analysis.

docs.title: Export, identities and project projections
docs.text:
Export → All observations CSV… exports observations from all loaded datasets, including excluded values and source identities/provenance, rather than just the filtered rows. Unassigned picked peaks without observables are not exported. Read-only PCS-project projections can also appear in this CSV; exporting them does not make the original project records editable or session-owned.

The export includes experiment/observable IDs, peak links where present, spectral revision, conditions, uncertainty and inclusion. For round trips:

  • Update exact loaded IDs explicitly enables updates to existing identities; source links and experiment conditions must still match.
  • Reopening a vendor FID creates new identities. Open the original NMR session to recover peak-linked records.
  • Import detached values (new identities) creates independent values with retained source evidence. It does not restore an authoritative spectrum link.

This observed-shift export is distinct from the peak-linked assignment-review CSV in Assignments / Analysis. Use that window's reviewed import for its assignment table; do not substitute nearest-ppm matching or a general shift import.

When bound to PCS Analyzer, the Import menu also exposes PCS project observed shifts… / PCS project diamagnetic shifts… and their paste counterparts. These update the existing project layers through their own review dialogs. Their Workbench projections remain read-only. More → Copy experiment values… opens a detached-copy review for independent session data; choose the actual nucleus explicitly if the old project did not specify one.

Use More → Show in Chemical Map and target-preview actions to inspect a reviewed mapping. Use reviewed target in PCS Preparation accepts a mapping explicitly; selection alone does not transfer PCS or establish an assignment.

docs.title: Shift Analysis and PCS Preparation
docs.text: Use the Shift Analysis and PCS Preparation Inspector tabs in NMR Workbench, after processing, referencing, and assigning corresponding paramagnetic and diamagnetic signals. Alternatively, start from prepared absolute observed shifts in NMR Data; no measured spectrum is required for that route.

docs.title: Pair and compare
docs.text:
In Experiments, set one dataset's Role to Paramagnetic and the other to Diamagnetic, then choose Pair with. Both must have the same nucleus. Pairing matches observable assignments after trimming whitespace and ignoring case. Missing partners and duplicate assignments are flagged; duplicate observations are not silently averaged.

You can also choose Observed / Para and Reference / Dia directly in Shift Analysis, then Compare. Role changes require confirmation. Review NMR Data Use flags and assignment diagnostics before comparing.

All shifts are in ppm:

\[ \delta_\mathrm{para}=\delta_\mathrm{obs}-\delta_\mathrm{dia}, \qquad \delta_\mathrm{nonPCS}=\delta_\mathrm{para}-\delta_\mathrm{PCS,calc}. \]

δ_obs is the observed paramagnetic-sample chemical shift, δ_dia its diamagnetic reference, and δ_para their difference. δ_Exp is the experimental PCS supplied to fitting after choosing a derivation method. These quantities are not interchangeable.

Shift Analysis → View offers Table, Overlay, Stacked, and Shift Diagnostics. Spectrum comparisons use absolute chemical-shift positions; diagnostics compare differences. A predicted absolute position is δ_dia + calculated PCS + any supplied fixed correction, not δ_para. Expand Display for plot-layer options. Normalize changes display scale. Broaden sticks creates a visual envelope for shift lists, not experimental lineshape fitting.

Calculated PCS follows the bound document's Prediction model: Axial excludes the rhombic term; Full tensor (Axial + Rhombic) adds it only when Enable Δχ_rh is on. δ_nonPCS is a diagnostic, not a uniquely resolved contact shift. Large discrepancies can also reflect assignment, referencing, conditions, structure, tensor, metal-position, or averaging errors. Its sign differs from some fitting residuals.

docs.title: Derive and map experimental PCS
docs.text:
Nd(iPr₂BA)₃ / La(iPr₂BA)₃ shift comparison in PCS Preparation.

  1. Choose a Derivation method explicitly.
  2. Select an assignment and enter its correction or manual PCS if required, and experimental uncertainty σ in ppm where known.
  3. Choose Target scope and its structural target; click Update selected.
  4. Review Use, PCS, Target, and Status. Double-click Use to include/exclude a row; resolve missing, ambiguous, or conflicting targets.
  5. Choose Review & Apply…. Check additions, replacements, and δ_Exp overwrites in Review Experimental PCS Handoff, then explicitly apply to PCS Analyzer. Check the bound document first.
Method Meaning and requirement Direct from Δshift PCS = δ_para. Use only when non-PCS contributions are negligible or already accounted for. FCS-corrected PCS = δ_para − manually supplied FCS/contact correction. This is not an automatic contact-shift fit. Manual / Imported PCS Use a supplied PCS rather than δ_para; a matched assignment pair is still required as provenance. The label does not imply a dedicated CSV-import button.

Targets include Single atom, NMR site, Matching ligand sites, and Custom refs. A grouped target is one experimental observation. Prediction averages member PCS values within each site and then reduces across sites; it does not evaluate PCS at a mean coordinate or create independent measurements for each member. See structured observations.

Selecting atoms or an NMR site previews a target. Use Use in PCS Preparation to accept it explicitly; highlighting alone does not change the mapping. Use Chemical Map to inspect membership and matching ligand instances before applying grouped observations.

docs.title: Existing shift lists and limitations
docs.text:
Existing PCS-project δ_obs/δ_dia layers appear as read-only shift-list datasets and can be paired without a measured trace. To bring in your own prepared absolute shifts, use NMR Data → Import → Observed shifts CSV / TSV…. The Nd/La documentation example also supplies observed-shift lists separately from its PCS project. See the FID/CSV tutorial for spectrum-based and prepared-data workflows.

Prepared values and read-only project projections are not measured intensity traces. A broadened stick display does not recover experimental line shapes.

Pairing checks role and nucleus, not chemical equivalence, solvent, temperature, or assignment correctness. Review those experimentally. Finite positive σ supports uncertainty-weighted fitting; see Quality Metrics. Handoff does not establish that a correction or averaging model is scientifically valid.

For temperature-specific series evidence and reference matching, use the separate VT PCS Pairing and Reviewed Transfer workflow. Its exact temperature checks are distinct from this single-pair comparison.

docs.title: Peaks and Assignments
docs.text: Process and reference the spectrum before interpreting peak positions. In Processing → Peak Picking, use Start Picking to select peaks on the spectrum and Stop to leave picking mode, or use Auto Pick. Advanced controls specify Min height (% max), Prominence (% range), and Min distance (points). Automatic picking detects positive peaks of the real processed spectrum; inspect negative, missed, overlapped, and baseline-distorted signals yourself.

docs.title: Inspect and assign
docs.text:
Open Inspector → NMR Data, choose Active experiment and Show = All. The unified table shows assigned observations and unassigned picked peaks. Inspect Shift / ppm, Source, Status, Intensity, and Picking (scroll horizontally for additional columns). Select a spectrum row to highlight its peak. Prepared independent shifts have no measured peak marker. Double-click Assignment, or press Enter, to edit. Tab advances to the next assignment; Shift+Tab goes back. Use More → Remove selected… or Delete to request removal of the selected source peak and its linked observation; review the confirmation. Processing → Peak Picking → Clear Auto Peaks retains manual picks; re-running automatic picking replaces previous automatic picks.

Use the same chemically meaningful assignment in the paramagnetic and diamagnetic datasets. Peak number and intensity order are not reliable cross-sample identifiers. Assignment text alone does not establish a structural atom mapping or chemical equivalence.

A peak assignment creates or updates an observable when required metadata is valid; review Status and the Use column. Observables carry chemical shift and assignment for downstream pairing. An annotation can remain a draft if missing metadata prevents observable creation; inspect warnings instead of assuming every label has become usable analysis data.

Click Use to include/exclude an assigned observation from shift comparison. Leave reference-standard peaks such as TMS unassigned or explicitly excluded when they are not sample observations. Clearing a spectrum assignment removes its observable linkage without deleting the peak. Reprocessing or replacing peaks can invalidate tracking evidence; do not assume links are repaired by nearest ppm. See NMR Data for independent values and CSV input.

docs.title: Link to the structure
docs.text:
Use NMR Data → More or the row context menu to Show in Chemical Map, Preview NMR site, Preview matching ligand sites, and explicitly Use reviewed target in PCS Preparation. A selection preview does not accept a target automatically. Check Ref IDs and all group members, especially methyl sites and equivalent ligand instances.

Once assignments are reviewed, set dataset roles and pair them in Shift Analysis and PCS Preparation. Duplicate labels within a dataset produce ambiguous pairs, not independent replicate measurements or an automatic average. Molecular assignments and interpretation of overlapping signals still require experimental judgment.

docs.title: Peak Tracking and Assignment Review
docs.text:
A track records reviewed correspondence between peaks in different series members. Its label is not a molecular assignment, an atom mapping or an automatically created observable. Process, reference and pick each spectrum before establishing links.

Open VT Series → Peak Tracking…, or VT stacked → Tracks.

docs.title: Link existing peaks explicitly
docs.text:
1. Choose a series, enter a track Label, then New.
  2. Select a member in the points table and inspect its spectrum.
  3. Choose an Existing peak, then Link peak.
  4. Repeat for the intended members. Inspect linked ppm and review diagnostics.

These H1 links use the tutorial's explicitly supplied correspondence. They do not prove a molecular assignment. The table is shown in temperature order; the original acquisition order is retained.

Use Save to update the label. Point state offers missing, ambiguous, unlinking and removal. Workflow links to assignment review, analysis and PCS preparation.

State Interpretation Unreviewed / unlinked Correspondence has not been confirmed. Confirmed Explicitly linked existing peak; source validity and member inclusion still matter. Missing No accepted observation for this member. Ambiguous Correspondence is uncertain; do not treat a candidate as a fit point. Stale Linked source/revision changed and requires review/reconfirmation.

Only valid confirmed observations from included members can enter fitting. Reprocessing, referencing or replacing peaks can stale links. Reinspect the actual source and Link peak again when justified; the Workbench does not silently recover links by nearest ppm.

docs.title: Use suggestions as review aids
docs.text:
After linking an anchor, set Candidate window / ppm and choose Suggest. Inspect candidate shift, score and reasons, select the intended candidate and choose Accept candidate explicitly. Suggestions do not create links until accepted and must be refreshed if inputs change. Manual linking remains available when no suitable candidate exists.

The current scoring uses acquisition-order continuity. Changing displayed order to temperature order does not change that scoring. A score is not an assignment probability or evidence of chemical equivalence. Inspect overlap, crossings, line-shape changes and potential species changes independently.

docs.title: Convert correspondence into reviewed assignments
docs.text:
Open Workflow → Assignment review… from tracking, or the corresponding VT analysis Workflow action. For the selected track:

  1. Enter Assignment, Nucleus and a Review note.
  2. Choose Associate to record reviewed assignment intent.
  3. Inspect member actions, existing observable IDs and diagnostics.
  4. Select intended members with Ctrl/Shift and choose Confirm selected.

Associate alone does not propagate labels into every dataset. Confirmation acts only on selected safe proposals; existing conflicts are not silently overwritten. Use selected copies a member's existing assignment into the review form; Associate and member confirmation are still explicit steps.

Inspect the resulting dataset-local observations in NMR Data. Structural targets remain a separate reviewed mapping. An NMR assignment does not become experimental PCS without pairing/derivation. Save an NMR session to preserve identities and reviewed evidence.

docs.title: Raw Data and Processing
docs.text:
In NMR Workbench, choose Open Dataset Folder… or Open FID File…. Keep acquisition data and metadata together.

Vendor input Select Bruker raw 1D Experiment folder containing fid and acqus, or its fid. Bruker processed 1D Processed-data folder containing 1r and procs. Varian/Agilent raw 1D .fid directory containing fid and procpar, or its fid.

The loader handles supported 1D datasets, not arbitrary vendor folders or multidimensional ser data. In a Bruker folder containing both raw and processed markers, automatic loading prefers raw data. Loading raw data initializes a default Fourier-transformed spectrum; this is a starting point, not a guarantee of correct phase, baseline, or referencing.

Raw FID shows the acquired time-domain data. Spectrum shows the processed frequency-domain trace, normally in ppm when metadata permits. Start Reprocessing starts again from available raw data. A processed-only dataset cannot recover the original FID or acquire missing resolution. Applicable Bruker digital-filter correction uses acquisition metadata.

docs.title: Processing sequence
docs.text:
Expand the numbered Processing sections as needed. Preview displays pending changes, Apply commits them, and Cancel discards the preview. Check the committed/preview indicator and History before picking signals.

  1. Apodization: select a window and parameter. Exponential line broadening and Gaussian broadening use Hz. Broadening trades resolution for noise suppression; it is not a fitted linewidth.
  2. Zero Filling: choose the transform size. Added points improve digital sampling, not intrinsic acquisition resolution.
  3. Fourier Transform: use Create Spectrum when processing from the time domain. Reprocessing preserves the original acquisition.
  4. Phase: expand Manual adjustment to adjust P0/P1, or select Peak minima / ACME under Auto and choose Run. Pivot → Pick… selects the origin of the phase ramp; Strongest uses the strongest magnitude signal. Pivot is not a chemical-shift reference. Preview changes and choose Apply. Inspect positive and negative regions before applying. Automatic phasing can fail for broad, overlapped, or unusual spectra.
  5. Baseline: preview correction and inspect weak/broad signals before applying. Auto Baseline uses arPLS; advanced alternatives expose their parameters. Optional processing dependencies may be needed.
  6. Reference: select an observed signal, choose Residual solvent, Reference standard, or Custom, and check observed/target ppm and offset. Preview and apply. Presets require a suitable nucleus and selected signal; choosing a solvent does not prove a peak's identity.
  7. Peak Picking: continue with Peaks and Assignments.

Applying a reference changes peak positions and associated observable shifts. Use a chemically justified reference for each sample before calculating shift differences. Retain vendor metadata and record processing choices; inspect Metadata for nucleus, frequency, solvent, temperature, and acquisition information when available.

The supplied Yb example opens from examples/documentation_demo/Yb_iPr2BA3_demo/PROTON_01.fid. The canonical image retains its vendor ppm axis; it does not assert an independently verified solvent calibration or completed quantitative analysis.

For a reproducible introductory exercise with known phase errors, baseline artifacts and separate TMS offsets, follow the FID/CSV tutorial. Save committed processing in an NMR session, rather than relying on a figure export. Batch Processing also supports reviewed processing of multiple experiments; its settings and previews do not commit until explicitly applied.

docs.title: NMR Sessions and Data Exchange
docs.text: Save NMR work separately from a PCS project. A .pcsp retains PCS analysis inputs and handed-off observations; it does not replace a recoverable NMR session.

docs.title: Save and reopen committed work
docs.text:
Open VT Series → Manage VT Series… (also available from the VT Series toolbar button), then choose Files → Save NMR session…. You can save a single-temperature experiment or prepared shift data without creating a series.

A .nmrsession preserves session-owned datasets, conditions, identities, embedded raw data when available, committed spectra, processing history, peaks and observables. It also retains series/tracks, reviewed associations, saved preparations/handoff evidence, retained analysis evidence and processing presets where present. Pending processing previews, render caches and transient UI selections are not saved. Apply a reviewed preview before saving if you intend to preserve its processing result.

Use Files → Open NMR session… in a fresh Workbench to resume. Check recovery diagnostics before continuing. Missing, moved or changed vendor sources are reported; embedded committed data remains available. Files → Rebind loaded source… lets you locate a vendor folder and check its source fingerprint. Rebinding a path does not silently reconfirm stale tracking links.

Keep original vendor directories for independent reproducibility. Reimporting the same FID is not equivalent to reopening its session: the new import has new dataset and peak IDs.

Read-only PCS-project projections are omitted from NMR session ownership and reported when applicable. Save the corresponding .pcsp separately, or use a reviewed detached copy for independent NMR data. Opening a session in the integrated Workbench does not restore or choose its PCS-document binding; check PCS: and rebind explicitly before structural operations or handoff.

docs.title: Choose the right file
docs.text:
File Purpose Limit .nmrsession Resume committed NMR work with stable identities. Does not preserve a live UI layout or pending previews. .nmrseries Export/import series membership and track definitions against loaded datasets. Does not embed spectra or replace a session; links can need review. Observed-shift CSV Exchange prepared/spectrum-linked observables with conditions and provenance via NMR Data. Does not recreate FIDs, peaks or tracks. Linked values need their matching session or explicit detachment. Assignment-review CSV Review assignment/uncertainty edits for existing peak-linked observables. Requires matching identities; reopening FIDs does not recreate them. Analysis CSV Report extracted coordinates, inclusion, predictions and residuals. Not a recoverable session or an observed-shift import template. Analysis results JSON Retain/import historical fit configuration, source snapshots, results and diagnostics. Import does not recalculate or change live fits. Use Keep in session to retain evidence before saving. Plot PNG/PDF/SVG Share a figure. Does not preserve scientific input identities or processing state.

Series definition commands are Files → Export series definitions… and Import series definitions… in the series manager. Assignment CSV and saved results JSON use Assignments / Analysis (File menu: Assignments / Saved Analysis…). Analysis tables/figures are exported from the VT analysis window.

For a practical save/reopen exercise, see the FID/CSV tutorial. For recovery of a multi-temperature series and its tracks, see the VT tutorial. For PCS-project/workspace storage, see Projects and Persistence.

docs.title: NMR Workbench
docs.text:
The former NMR Shift Viewer functionality, available through v1.3.4, is now part of NMR Workbench.

Open Modules → NMR Workbench or Ribbon → Tools → NMR Workbench. Choose the input route appropriate to your data:

Vendor data → processing → referencing → peak picking → assignments → observables → Shift Analysis → PCS Preparation.

Prepared observed-shift CSV / paste / manual values → NMR Data → Shift Analysis → PCS Preparation. A spectrum is not required for prepared observations. See NMR Data and the FID/CSV tutorial for both routes.

For multiple temperatures, VT Series provides series management, batch processing, stacked spectra, peak tracking and VT analysis. Tracking establishes reviewed correspondence; it does not automatically assign a resonance or map it to an atom. Save committed work as an NMR session. Follow the VT tutorial with the supplied synthetic FIDs; VT PCS preparation is a separate reviewed derivation step.

A broadened shift-list display is not a measured intensity trace; use the vendor-data route above for processing measured spectra.

Yb(iPr₂BA)₃ spectrum after processing and peak picking, with all 17 picked peaks displayed in NMR Data. Demo A/B are the two assigned observations.

Demo A/B are illustrative peak annotations, not molecular assignments. Inspect phase, baseline, referencing and peak picks before accepting a result; automatic processing is only a starting point. See Raw Data and Processing for the example input and processing workflow.

docs.title: Workspace
docs.text:
Area Use Experiments Select a dataset, inspect conditions, assign Paramagnetic or Diamagnetic role, and choose Pair with. Processing Apodization, Zero Filling, Fourier Transform, Phase, Baseline, Reference, and Peak Picking. Spectrum Measured trace, peak markers, and Matplotlib toolbar. View switches Spectrum and Raw FID when available. Inspector History, Metadata, NMR Data, Shift Analysis, and PCS Preparation tabs. NMR Data combines picked peaks and prepared observations, with assignment editing and import/export controls.

Use Open Dataset Folder… or Open FID File… to load vendor data. Reset View restores the plot view; Auto Scale fits the intensity range. See Raw Data and Processing and Peaks and Assignments for the practical sequence.

The spectrum area also has Single spectrum and VT stacked tabs. Assignments / Analysis opens assignment CSV and saved-analysis exchange; Guide opens the workflow, terms and file-purpose help. The same workflows are available from the Workbench's File, VT Series and Help menus.

For standalone practice from the source repository, run python tools/nmr_workbench.py with the application's dependencies installed. Standalone mode supports NMR work but has no PCS document or structural targets.

docs.title: PCS-document binding
docs.text:
The Workbench binds to the PCS document active when it opens. Switching the main document tab does not redirect structural selections or PCS handoff. Check the PCS: indicator before mapping targets or applying results. Rebind to Active PCS Document explicitly changes the binding. If the bound document is closed, rebind before continuing those operations.

Loading a spectrum does not populate fitting data automatically. Only an explicit, reviewed PCS preparation handoff supplies experimental PCS observations to the bound document. Retain original vendor data for reproducibility; a processed display or figure cannot replace it.

docs.title: Tutorial: FID or CSV to Shift Comparison
Tutorial: From FID or CSV to Shift Comparison
docs.text: This synthetic teaching example provides four resonances through two input paths. It exercises processing, assignments, shift comparison and optional structure mapping. It is not measured data or a validated model of PCS.

docs.title: Get the example files
docs.text:
Use examples/nmr_workflow_demo/ from the portable release or source archive. All short paths below are relative to this directory. See finding the example files.

  • Example input directory
  • Paramagnetic CSV
  • Diamagnetic CSV
  • Toy structure

For FID practice, retain the complete FID/Paramagnetic.fid/ and FID/Diamagnetic.fid/ directories, including fid and procpar. For CSV-only practice, download the raw CSV files from their GitHub file pages. Do not save an HTML preview as a CSV.

Open NMR Workbench from PCS Analyzer's Tools Ribbon. Start each input route in a fresh Workbench. Using both routes together creates separate datasets for the same teaching observations.

Both experiments are 1H, 298.15 K. Expected referenced values are:

Assignment Dia / ppm Para / ppm Para − Dia / ppm H1 1.20 2.00 0.80 H2 3.40 5.00 1.60 H3 5.60 8.00 2.40 H4 7.80 11.00 3.20

H1–H4 are correspondence labels. The role names do not establish molecular assignments, contact-shift separation or physical PCS.

docs.title: Route A: Process the FIDs
docs.text:
1. Use File → Open Dataset Folder… to load both .fid directories. The initial default FT creates a starting spectrum; do not run FT again. Leave apodization and zero filling off for this exercise.
  2. Select Paramagnetic. In Processing → Phase → Manual adjustment, enter P0 = −25°, P1 = 0°, then Apply once. Repeat for Diamagnetic. This undoes the synthetic +25° phase error; a second application adds another correction. Pivot does not affect this P1 = 0 example.
  3. In Baseline, choose Auto Baseline (arPLS), inspect the fitted baseline/original-spectrum preview, then Apply. Repeat for both datasets. The default lambda is 1e5. Alternatively use manual arPLS with lambda 1e5 and Preview → Apply, rather than applying both methods consecutively.
  4. In Reference, choose Reference standard, TMS, target 0 ppm. Zoom near zero and Pick… the small TMS signal: approximately +0.179688 ppm in Para and −0.120117 ppm in Dia. Preview the offset (about −0.18 / +0.12 ppm) and Apply separately. Check TMS now lies at zero.
  5. Choose Peak Picking → Auto Pick for each dataset. Defaults of 1% height, 0.5% prominence and 3 points separation should yield five peaks: four sample peaks and TMS. Restore defaults if a custom threshold misses the small TMS peak.
  6. In NMR Data, choose Active experiment, Show = All, and sort Shift / ppm ascending. Leave TMS near zero unassigned. Assign the four remaining peaks H1–H4 using double-click/Enter and Tab. Repeat in both datasets and check Use for all four sample observations. If you label TMS for convenience, exclude its Use in both datasets.
  7. Choose Compare shifts →, select Observed / Para = Paramagnetic and Reference / Dia = Diamagnetic, then Compare. Confirm roles if asked.

Expect four matched rows. Peak-grid sampling gives differences approximately 0.799805, 1.599609, 2.399414, 3.200195 ppm. Compare with the table above within ±0.005 ppm; this teaching tolerance is not measured uncertainty. Try Overlay or Stacked and expand Display for plot options.

The smooth baseline, global phase error and reference offsets are deliberate. Skipping both reference corrections biases Para − Dia by about +0.30 ppm. Phase pivot selection is separate from chemical-shift referencing. No random noise is added. Automatic phase methods can be explored on a fresh input, but compare them with the known manual correction before accepting results.

docs.title: Route B: Import prepared CSV values
docs.text:
1. In a fresh Workbench, choose NMR Data → Import → Observed shifts CSV / TSV… and open CSV/Paramagnetic.csv.
  2. Check Assignment = assignment, Shift = shift_ppm. Choose Preview, review four rows, then Apply. The file supplies experiment, role, nucleus and temperature; ID-update/detached-copy options are unnecessary.
  3. Repeat with CSV/Diamagnetic.csv. Use All experiments to inspect both.
  4. Open Shift Analysis, choose Paramagnetic and Diamagnetic explicitly, then Compare. Expect four matches and differences 0.8, 1.6, 2.4, 3.2 ppm. Roles are already supplied by the files.

These values are already referenced. This route has no raw trace or picked peaks and needs no FT, phase or baseline correction. An overlay of prepared shifts is a stick/display representation, not measured lineshape data. TMS is not present in these CSVs. See NMR Data for the import preview and identity rules.

docs.title: Optional: Review structure mappings
docs.text:
This exercise requires the main PCS Analyzer, rather than standalone Workbench.

  1. In a fresh PCS document, use File → Load XYZ… to load structure.xyz. Choose Nd as centre and leave averaging disabled.
  2. Open Workbench from that document and follow one route above. Alternatively, save standalone work as .nmrsession and open it in a fresh integrated Workbench. Check PCS:; switching main document tabs does not rebind it.
  3. In PCS Preparation, choose each H1–H4 assignment and Single atom target scope. Explicitly select targets and use Update selected:
Assignment Structure Ref Element H1 6 H H2 7 H H3 8 H H4 9 H
  1. In NMR Data, select the corresponding row and More → Show in Chemical Map. Inspect Ref IDs and hydrogens; navigation does not transfer PCS.
  2. If practising Review & Apply…, explicitly declare Direct from Δshift as a teaching assumption, review targets/conflicts and inspect the destination. You can cancel the review and finish the mapping exercise without transfer.

The XYZ is a nine-atom toy Nd/O/H cluster, not an optimized molecule or the physical source of these shifts. Ref 1 is Nd, Refs 2–5 are O and Refs 6–9 are H. XYZ comments do not establish H1–H4 assignments. TMS is a separate reference species and has no target here. Do not use this example to assess tensor recovery or PCS fitting accuracy.

docs.title: Save and check your work
docs.text:
Choose VT Series → Manage VT Series… → Files → Save NMR session…; no VT series is required. Reopen the session in a fresh Workbench and check the committed data and assignments. NMR Data → Export → All observations CSV… exports observations/provenance, not the unassigned TMS peak or a full session. See Sessions and Data Exchange.

The supplied files are ready to import; no Python scripts are needed.

For measured-spectrum processing see Raw Data and Processing. For the scientific derivation and reviewed handoff see Shift Analysis and PCS Preparation. Continue with the separate VT tutorial to practise batch processing, tracking and observed-shift temperature fitting on five FIDs.

docs.title: Tutorial: Observed Shifts to PCS Fitting
Tutorial: Observed shifts to PCS fitting
docs.text:
Use examples/nmr_pcs_fitting_demo/ for a CSV-only exercise linking NMR Workbench to the main PCS fitting workflow. The supplied CSV files contain the mappings and known values described below. Unlike the simulated FID/VT teaching examples, these shifts are generated from a known tensor with explicit contact assumptions. They remain synthetic probes, not measured assignments.

Use the files supplied with the application; see finding the examples. Paths below are relative to examples/nmr_pcs_fitting_demo/. Import both shift CSVs from the same scenario as the open start.pcsp.

File in each scenario Use start.pcsp Open first; structure ready for the NMR-to-PCS exercise. paramagnetic.csv, diamagnetic.csv Import into the fresh NMR Workbench. mapping_and_truth.csv Read the supplied Ref mapping and contact corrections; do not import it as a third shift dataset. prepared.pcsp Open separately to start at the completed PCS-transfer checkpoint.

docs.title: Generating assumptions
docs.text:
Twelve H observations at 300 K map H1–H12 to Refs 3–14. The known tensor is Δχ_ax=12, Δχ_rh=3 E-32 m³ with zero orientation at the origin.

Folder Observed shifts Appropriate provider direct/ δ_obs = δ_dia + PCS; contact is exactly zero Direct from Δshift contact_corrected/ δ_obs = δ_dia + PCS + known contact FCS-corrected

mapping_and_truth.csv supplies assignment/Ref, both absolute shifts, contact and PCS. No uncertainty or random noise is supplied; use unweighted fitting.

docs.title: Import, derive and transfer
docs.text:
1. Choose File → Open PCS Project..., open direct/start.pcsp, then launch a fresh NMR Workbench from the Tools Ribbon.
  2. Import paramagnetic.csv and diamagnetic.csv through NMR Data Preview/Apply. Check roles, 1H, 300 K and twelve records per dataset.
  3. Pair the datasets in Shift Analysis. Review twelve matched assignments and δ_para = δ_obs − δ_dia.
  4. In PCS Preparation, choose Direct from Δshift and explicitly map Single atom targets H1–H12 to Refs 3–14. Labels alone do not establish targets.
  5. Use Review & Apply… for the selected rows. Inspect the destination and conflicts before transferring twelve PCS observations to the main document.
  6. In Fitting, choose Mode B, select all twelve observations, fit both tensor components, use Unweighted and disable global search/current-tensor initialization. Run Fit. Expect 12 / 3 and RMSD below 0.000001 ppm.

Repeat in a fresh session with contact_corrected/start.pcsp. Choose FCS-corrected and enter the listed contact correction for each assignment. Subtracting that known contact term recovers the same PCS and tensor. Direct subtraction would include contact in this case and is not the correct PCS.

The correction values are supplied assumptions, not inferred by this application. This exercise does not show that an unknown contact term can be identified from one experimental shift pair. See PCS preparation.

After transferring, the main Undo arrow beside Help restores the PCS destination's previous values, observations and provenance. Redo reinstalls the same recorded data without repeating preparation. The NMR source session and historical transfer receipts remain intact. See document Undo/Redo for supported edits and scope.

docs.title: Checkpoints and reproducibility
docs.text:
Each prepared.pcsp contains the expected data after PCS transfer. It includes PCS provenance/targets, but no NMR session or fitted result. Use it to practice fitting separately. Save your practice .nmrsession and .pcsp independently; reopening a PCS file does not reconstruct the underlying NMR datasets.

Actual Mode B fit of contact_corrected/prepared.pcsp: twelve observations, unweighted residuals and recovered 12 / 3 tensor. This is the transferred PCS checkpoint, not a screenshot of the observed-shift import dialog.

docs.title: Tutorial: Process and Analyse a VT Series
docs.text: Use examples/nmr_vt_demo/ for a five-temperature workflow: import → batch processing → stacked spectra → manual tracking → VT analysis → optional assignment/PCS review. These are simulated teaching signals, not measurements or a physical model of the supplied structure.

docs.title: Files and expected behavior
docs.text:
Get the example input directory. The same inputs are included in the portable release; see finding the example files. Short paths below are relative to examples/nmr_vt_demo/. Keep each experiment's fid and procpar together.

Input Use FID/Paramagnetic/ Five members, acquisition order 298, 278, 318, 288, 308 K. FID/Reference/Diamagnetic_298K.fid/ Separate reference for the optional 298 K comparison; not a sixth VT member. CSV/Expected_shifts.csv 24 ideal corrected observed shifts, including the reference values. structure.xyz Toy nine-atom Nd/O/H cluster for optional target review.

Open a fresh NMR Workbench from PCS Analyzer's Tools Ribbon. Use the main app for structural operations. All provided temperatures are nominal; no calibration or member override is supplied.

Importing Expected_shifts.csv through NMR Data creates independent values. It does not recreate FIDs, picked peaks, series or tracks. Keep that prepared-data exercise separate from this FID practice session.

docs.title: 1. Create and import the series
docs.text:
1. Open VT Series → Manage VT Series…, choose New, name it Synthetic VT.
  2. Use Import → Folder group… on FID/Paramagnetic, or select the five .fid directories through FID experiments….
  3. Check five included members with valid temperatures and no import failures.
  4. Compare Acquisition, Temperature ↑, and Temperature ↓. Ascending temperature order is 278, 288, 298, 308, 318 K.

Keep the reference outside the series. If practising Override / K, clear it again before fitting. See Series and Stacked Spectra.

docs.title: 2. Preview and apply processing
docs.text:
Open VT Series → Batch Processing…, select the series and check all five experiments. Use Current spectrum; untouched FIDs receive default FT. Leave apodization/zero filling off. Enable and order these operations, storing each operation's parameters with Set common before moving to the next:

Order Operation Settings 1 Phase Manual, P0 −25°, P1 0°, strongest-peak pivot. 2 Baseline arPLS, lambda 100000. 3 Reference Reference standard → TMS, proton signal, 0 ppm; search region −0.30 to +0.30 ppm. 4 Peak Picking Height fraction 0.01, prominence fraction 0.005, distance 3 points.

The search region independently finds the small TMS peak in each member. Initial TMS offsets in acquisition order are +0.18, −0.14, +0.22, +0.07, −0.09 ppm. Do not share one observed reference position across members.

Choose Preview checked, inspect the member results and Overlay, then Apply reviewed previews explicitly. Expect five successful members, each with four sample peaks plus TMS near zero. Use the batch preview image as a layout guide. Preview itself does not commit history or peaks.

Do not apply −25° again to an already corrected current spectrum. Start a fresh import/session, or review an Original FID recipe with the correct FT order to repeat from scratch. Phase pivot and TMS chemical-shift reference are separate settings.

docs.title: 3. Inspect spectra in temperature order
docs.text: Choose VT stacked, Temperature ↑, and adjust spacing/normalization. Select a trace to activate its experiment. Temporarily exclude a member in the series manager and inspect its trace disappearing; restore all five members before continuing. These display changes do not change peak measurements.

docs.title: 4. Establish four tracks
docs.text:
Open Tracks / Peak Tracking…. Create H1–H4. For each track, visit all five members, select the corresponding Existing peak, then Link peak. Use the four sample resonances in ascending ppm order; leave TMS untracked and unassigned. At 298 K they are approximately 2, 5, 8, 11 ppm. Expect four tracks with five confirmed links each.

Optional assisted practice: link an anchor, set Candidate window / ppm = 0.5, then Suggest. Inspect reasons before Accept candidate. This window is appropriate for these separated teaching signals, not a general experimental default. Scoring uses acquisition order even when display uses temperature order.

Try marking a point missing/ambiguous and then restore its correct link. These states should not enter the fit. Reprocessing/re-picking can stale links and requires explicit review. Track labels do not create dataset observables or infer molecular/structural assignments. See Peak Tracking.

docs.title: 5. Fit observed-shift temperature dependence
docs.text:
Open VT Analysis…, select a track, choose δ vs 1/T, and first inspect Linear (coordinate). Then choose Curie, unweighted. The generator uses:

\[ \delta(T)=a+C/T. \] Track a / ppm C / ppm·K δ at 298 K / ppm H1 1.2 238.4 2.0 H2 3.4 476.8 5.0 H3 5.6 715.2 8.0 H4 7.8 953.6 11.0

Expect five fit points per track and R² close to one. Grid sampling, processing and reference picking affect the measured shifts, so fitted coefficients need not equal generator constants exactly. No measured uncertainty is supplied; do not invent σ or use measured_sigma for this exercise.

Also inspect δ vs T, δT vs 1/T, residuals and Compare models (raw δ / ppm). Curie fits raw observed δ and transforms its curve for display. The nonzero offset means δT vs 1/T is not generally linear. Five points alone do not establish Curie-Weiss parameter precision or physical meaning.

Exclude one valid row using Exclude from fit: n should decrease to four while member inclusion and the confirmed track link remain unchanged. Restore it, select a plotted point and navigate back with Show spectrum. Export the analysis CSV/plot/results JSON. Exported results are extracted/fitted values; Expected_shifts.csv is the ideal generator table. See VT Analysis.

docs.title: 6. Review assignments and optional structure targets
docs.text:
From tracking/analysis Workflow → Assignment review…, select each track, enter its H1–H4 teaching assignment, 1H, and a synthetic-example review note. Choose Associate, inspect the member proposals, select all intended members and Confirm selected. Expect four dataset-local observations per experiment. TMS remains outside the assignments. Resolve existing conflicts explicitly.

For structure review in the main app, load structure.xyz, choose Nd as centre, keep averaging disabled, and check the Workbench's PCS: binding. Explicitly review single-atom targets H1 → Ref 6, H2 → Ref 7, H3 → Ref 8, H4 → Ref 9 using the existing PCS Preparation/structural-target controls and Chemical Map. Labels do not infer these targets. The toy XYZ is not optimized, is not the physical source of the shifts and contains no TMS atom.

docs.title: 7. Optional: Compare with the 298 K reference
docs.text:
Import FID/Reference/Diamagnetic_298K.fid separately. Correct phase/baseline/ TMS reference and pick peaks with the same parameters, individually or in a separate temporary batch series. Its initial TMS is −0.12 ppm. Set its role diamagnetic and assign its four sample peaks H1–H4; set the five VT datasets paramagnetic.

Open Workflow → VT PCS preparation… (tracking labels the action PCS preparation…). Choose a reviewed observation, compatible reference and structural target explicitly. Only 298 K has a matching reference here; other temperatures remain unresolved. Expected 298 K differences are 0.8, 1.6, 2.4, 3.2 ppm, approximately subject to spectral sampling.

Use shift_difference_only to inspect provenance. These differences are not independently established PCS. The example supplies no scientific basis for direct PCS, contact separation or tensor recovery. If practising transfer under an explicitly declared teaching assumption, review destination conflicts and keep it separate from real scientific work. See VT PCS Preparation.

docs.title: Save and resume
docs.text:
Choose Export → Keep results in session in VT Analysis when retaining fit evidence, then save Files → Save NMR session… in the series manager. Reopen in a fresh Workbench and inspect identities, five members, four tracks and associations. .nmrseries definitions alone do not preserve the full session. Previews/caches/transient selections are not saved. See Sessions.

The supplied FIDs are ready to import. Peak/track identities are established during this exercise; start with fresh imports rather than previously embedded session spectra.

docs.title: VT Analysis of Observed Shifts
docs.text: Open VT Series → VT Analysis…, or VT stacked → Analysis. Select a series and one or more tracks (Ctrl/Shift overlays tracks). The input is observed chemical shift δ in ppm, with effective temperature T in Kelvin. It is not automatically PCS, contact shift or a para-minus-dia difference.

docs.title: Coordinates and fitted models
docs.text:
Coordinate x y δ vs T T / K δ / ppm δ vs 1/T 1/T / K⁻¹ δ / ppm δT vs 1/T 1/T / K⁻¹ δT / ppm·K

Linear (coordinate) fits an unweighted straight line in the selected coordinates. Its slope/intercept units therefore depend on those coordinates.

Curie and Curie-Weiss fit raw observed shifts against temperature:

\[ \delta(T)=a+\frac{C}{T},\qquad \delta(T)=a+\frac{C}{T-\theta}. \]

Here a is in ppm, C in ppm·K and θ in K. Changing coordinates transforms the displayed curve rather than changing the raw-shift fit objective. With a nonzero offset, δT vs 1/T is not generally a straight line. Curie and a linear δ vs 1/T fit are mathematically equivalent for unweighted fitting of the same points, but a linear fit in the other coordinate views has a different meaning.

Five processed synthetic H1 observations, unweighted Curie fit, displayed as δ vs 1/T. Processing and grid sampling make parameters differ slightly from the generator's a = 1.2 ppm and C = 238.4 ppm·K.

docs.title: Choose fit points and weights
docs.text:
Valid fit points require a confirmed live peak link, an included series member, finite observed shift and finite positive effective temperature. Missing, ambiguous, stale and invalid points remain diagnostic evidence, not usable measurements.

Use Fit range / K to limit temperatures and Include in fit / Exclude from fit for selected rows in Observations / fit mask. These masks are local to the analysis; they do not change member inclusion or track decisions. Selecting a plotted point/row navigates to its member and peak. Show spectrum returns to the series spectrum view.

The model selector supports unweighted and measured_sigma for Curie/ Curie-Weiss. Measured-sigma fitting requires a finite positive provided shift uncertainty for every included point, synchronized with its linked observable. Missing uncertainties are not invented or replaced silently. Coordinate linear fits remain unweighted.

Curie needs at least two distinct temperatures; Curie-Weiss needs at least three, and additional points are needed to estimate residual variance reliably. The implemented Curie-Weiss branch requires T > θ. Use θ bounds / K to enter finite increasing bounds below the minimum fitted temperature. Blank bounds use guarded defaults; inspect the reported bound/conditioning diagnostics and do not interpret these defaults as scientifically established limits.

docs.title: Interpret residuals and comparisons
docs.text:
Residuals are measured minus fitted. Plot/table residuals use the selected y-coordinate units; raw-shift model metrics are in the observed-shift domain. Inspect diagnostics and covariance/parameter correlation, not only R². The models assume one unchanged resonance/species and a temperature-independent offset; exchange/population changes and temperature uncertainty are not modeled. C is a phenomenological coefficient, not a fitted susceptibility tensor.

Compare models (raw δ / ppm) compares empirical linear-in-T, Curie and Curie-Weiss models using the same points and weighting. Review RSS, RMSE, R², AIC/AICc, point count and status in that common domain. AICc may be unavailable with too few points; near-equal scores do not distinguish models. Good fit quality or extra parameters alone do not establish physical meaning.

docs.title: Export and retain evidence
docs.text:
Export provides Analysis table CSV…, Plot image / PDF…, Results JSON… and Keep results in session. CSV reports extracted/fitted values, identities, inclusion and residuals. JSON retains historical source snapshots, configuration, results and diagnostics. Keep results in session, then save the .nmrsession, to retain that evidence alongside the sources. Imported saved results do not recalculate the live fit. See Sessions and Data Exchange.

Follow the VT tutorial for known observed-shift curves, and VT PCS Preparation for the separate derivation workflow.

docs.title: VT PCS Pairing and Reviewed Transfer
docs.text: Open Peak Tracking → Workflow → PCS preparation…, or VT Analysis → Workflow → VT PCS preparation…. This workflow starts from reviewed track/observable associations. It does not fit a tensor or silently reinterpret an observed-shift trend as PCS.

docs.title: Review temperature-specific references
docs.text:
1. Choose a reviewed VT observation in Prepare / pair.
  2. Inspect Reference dataset, observable, T / K, δ / ppm and pairing diagnostics. Select a reference explicitly.
  3. Choose a Reviewed structural target and inspect its membership in the bound PCS document.

Paramagnetic/diamagnetic role, nucleus, assignment, source validity and temperature must be compatible. The current implementation requires exact effective Kelvin equality: it does not interpolate or choose the nearest reference temperature. Assignment matching trims whitespace but retains case in this VT route, unlike the case-insensitive single-pair comparison. Duplicate/repeated candidates need review, not averaging or automatic selection. A separate reference dataset still needs a live peak and synchronized assignment; general prepared CSV values alone do not supply that spectral provenance for this VT reference route.

docs.title: Keep quantities and scientific basis explicit
docs.text:
The provider selector exposes these current choices:

Choice Meaning shift_difference_only Retain the reviewed para-minus-dia difference and provenance; it is not transfer-ready experimental PCS. direct_delta_shift Treat Δshift as PCS only under an explicitly justified basis. manual_fcs Subtract a supplied Manual contact / ppm correction from Δshift. manual_pcs Use supplied Imported PCS / ppm for the reviewed pair.

For a PCS provider, supply the required finite correction/manual value and a Scientific basis / review note. A note records an explicit decision; it does not prove the approximation. These are not automatic contact separation or temperature-dependent susceptibility fits.

Choose Prepare reviewed pair to save the reviewed evidence. Preparation lets you inspect provenance or remove a saved preparation. Changes to source peaks, assignments, conditions or targets can make saved evidence stale; inspect readiness and prepare/review again rather than assuming automatic validity.

docs.title: Transfer only reviewed PCS observations
docs.text:
The main PCS Analyzer is required for a destination and structure. In Reviewed transfer:

  1. Check Destination and use Choose document when needed. A main tab switch alone does not redirect a bound Workbench.
  2. Select intended preparations with Ctrl/Shift, or Select temperature. Nothing is initially selected or transferred automatically.
  3. Choose Preview transfer. Review readiness, single/grouped targets, additions, replacements and destination conflicts.
  4. Approve only the explicitly listed replacements if appropriate, then choose Transfer reviewed and confirm. Changed selection/sources/destination invalidate the preview and require another review.

Transfer produces a receipt and updates the destination's PCS observations; it runs no fitting. Unrelated destination data remains intact. Later NMR source changes do not rewrite transferred PCS values automatically. Save both the NMR session and the PCS project.

In the synthetic VT tutorial, the only reference is at 298 K. Other temperatures remain unresolved. The known differences at 298 K are a workflow check, not an independently established PCS or contact-shift model.

docs.title: VT Series and Stacked Spectra
docs.text:
A variable-temperature (VT) series groups loaded experiments while retaining each dataset's own spectrum, processing history, peaks and identity. It does not average spectra or infer which resonances correspond across temperatures.

Open VT Series → Manage VT Series…, or the VT Series toolbar button. For a guided exercise with five synthetic FIDs, see the VT tutorial.

docs.title: Create and inspect a series
docs.text:
1. Choose New and enter a series name.
  2. Use Add loaded for an existing experiment, Import → FID experiments… for experiment directories, or Import → Folder group… for a group folder.
  3. Review the imported members and any loading failures/skipped inputs.
  4. Check T / K, T source, Label, Use and Diagnostic.

Keep vendor metadata beside its FID. A series member references an existing dataset; removing a member does not delete that loaded dataset. Read-only PCS-project shift projections are not acquired experiments and cannot be added through this series workflow.
