docs.title: File Formats
docs.text: PCS Analyzer uses different formats for structures, experimental values, projects, numerical exports, figures, and viewer presets. Support is workflow-specific: an extension accepted by one tool is not necessarily accepted by another.

docs.title: Format summary
docs.text: Format Read Write Principal use .xyz Yes Yes Main structures, conformers, and optimized structures ORCA .out, .log Yes No Main geometry input; PCS Workbench geometry and susceptibility-tensor input .csv Yes Yes Experimental values, advanced fitting inputs/templates, tables, and numerical results .xlsx Yes Yes Experimental shifts, templates, PCS plot data, and table exports legacy .xls Offered for experimental-shift input No Older spreadsheet input when a compatible pandas engine is installed .pcsp Yes Yes PCS Analyzer project persistence, including structured observations and standard fit history .pcsw Yes Yes Ordered references to saved .pcsp projects; no embedded project data .nmrsession NMR Workbench NMR Workbench Recoverable committed NMR spectra, observations and series/tracking state .nmrseries NMR Workbench NMR Workbench Series/track definitions referencing loaded datasets; no embedded spectra .png No Yes Raster figure and viewer export .pdf, .svg No Selected views only Vector/document figure export .json Yes Yes Fit-run import/export; molecular visualization settings and other workflow-specific viewer presets; plugin manifests .3d PCS Workbench No ORCA simple-grid spin-density input .npy, .npz No PCS Workbench Selected volume array; NPZ also includes associated data .cube, .cub, .vti, .vtk, .dx, .mrc, .ccp4, .map, .nrrd No PCS Workbench PCS or density volumes .vtp, .ply, .stl, .obj No PCS Workbench A selected isosurface .gif No PCS Workbench Temperature-dependent tensor-spheroid animation .txt No Selected workflows Regression companion summary and conformer-search report plugin .py, folder, .zip Module Manager No Local external-plugin installation

docs.title: Main structure loader
docs.text:
File → Load XYZ... accepts .xyz, .out, and .log. The extension selects the parser.

  • XYZ may use the standard atom-count/comment header or supported headerless coordinate rows.
  • ORCA input uses the last recognized Cartesian-coordinate block.
  • ORCA coordinates in Bohr are converted to Å.

See Structure Files and Parsing for accepted XYZ row layouts and ORCA block detection.

The Multi-Conformer fitting loader accepts the same three extensions through the common structure loader. The standalone Conformer Search file chooser is stricter: it accepts conventional XYZ with an atom-count line, comment line, and the declared number of coordinate rows.

docs.title: PCS Workbench inputs
docs.text:
PCS Workbench accepts ORCA .out/.log and ORCA simple-grid spin-density .3d files. In this context, the ORCA loader also looks for susceptibility tensors associated with TEMPERATURE/K and Tensor in molecular frame records. When multiple susceptibility sections are found, the Workbench asks which to use. This tensor parsing is additional to the main structure loader's geometry-only use.

The .3d reader expects a title, grid dimensions, origin, grid spacing, and exactly the declared number of scalar values. Its parser rejects non-positive dimensions or spacing and a mismatched data count.

docs.title: PCS Analyzer projects
docs.text:
.pcsp embeds the structure, principal analysis inputs and complete standard Fit History. It is intended for reopening analyses, and is not interchangeable with XYZ or a spreadsheet.

See Projects and Persistence for save/load behavior, compatibility handling, recalculated state, fit-history restoration and the Mode C preview persistence.

The existing [visibility] fields residual_thr_ok, residual_thr_warn, and residual_color_enabled retain the shared main/Rhombicity Table display classification. Cutoffs must be finite with 0 ≤ green < orange; invalid or missing pairs use 0.10/0.30 ppm. Missing Color defaults to off. Ribbon module order is an application preference and is not embedded here.

Current files also embed the latest Conformer Search candidate set in a versioned JSON record within [conformer_search]. It includes the original search geometry (Å), PCS observations (ppm), fixed/bond selections, recorded conditions, reports and candidate coordinates. Current manual graph edits are separate from the immutable run graph. Undefined R²/Q metrics use JSON null and remain undefined on restoration. Search inputs do not depend on temporary file paths. Older scalar-only summaries contain insufficient data to reconstruct candidates.

An applied Workbench tensor can also retain its ORCA source information in the Analyzer project. This does not embed the Workbench density or result session. See Tensor Transfer.

docs.title: Workspace references
docs.text: .pcsw is a workspace containing paths to saved .pcsp projects, their order and the active project reference. It does not store unsaved project changes or embed the projects. Save the project documents separately and keep referenced files available when moving or sharing a workspace. See Workspaces.

docs.title: Experimental-data spreadsheets and pasted text
docs.text:
The main δ_Exp and PCS-project δ_obs/δ_dia importers accept CSV, XLSX, and—when a compatible engine is available—legacy XLS. Clipboard dialogs accept comma-, tab-, semicolon-, or whitespace-separated text.

The separate NMR Data → Observed shifts CSV / TSV… importer accepts UTF-8 CSV/TSV/text and mapped absolute observed shifts, with its own identity rules. Its paste input supports comma, tab and semicolon delimiters. XLSX and the structural Ref-matching rules below belong to the PCS-project importers, not this general NMR input route. See NMR Data.

The preferred structure is:

Ref,δ_Exp
12,0.084
18,-0.137

Ref is the recommended identifier and must contain integer Ref IDs matching the current structure. An atom/element column can be used instead, but exact label matching and repeated-label ordering make it less reliable. A third Atom column is optional when Ref IDs are present.

The value heading depends on the data layer. Common forms include δ_Exp or delta_exp, δ_obs or delta_obs, and δ_dia or delta_dia. The importer also supports documented aliases and a preview with selective set, clear, and skip actions.

See Import and Export for the full recognized-heading table, fallback behavior, preview semantics, encodings, and mismatch troubleshooting. Those rules are the authoritative reference for the main experimental-data importers.

docs.title: Specialized CSV inputs
docs.text:
These files belong to specific workflows and do not use the general experimental-shift preview.

Workflow Required identifiers and values Optional/defaulted fields Conformer Search PCS First column: one-based Ref/ID; second value column, or third column when an element column is present Header row may be present; comma, tab, semicolon, or whitespace dialect is detected Joint PCS+RDC ref1, ref2, rdc_exp, or unambiguous atom1, atom2, rdc_exp Explicit raw Ref pairs recommended. rdc_err defaults to 0.5 Hz; nuc1/nuc2 default to H/N. d is accepted for rdc_exp; h/n are not label-column aliases. PRE Integer ref_id, ref or id; gamma2/g2, or paired r2_para,r2_dia Proton Γ₂ increments in s⁻¹. gamma2_err/sigma optional; paired rate errors combine by RSS. Single r2_para/r2 are legacy increment aliases with a warning. Optional nucleus supports H/1H only. Multi-Lanthanide Wide Nucleus,Ln... matrix for total paramagnetic shifts, or single-dataset ref_id/ref/id with pcs_exp (Tensor fitting) or delta_para (series tools) Ln_err/error uncertainties, G_common/Ln_G_i geometry, nucleus/Ref mapping. Legacy delta_exp/d_exp/ppm aliases use the selected input type. Missing cells remain missing; invalid numbers and duplicate labels are rejected.

The Advanced Fitting tab can export UTF-8-with-BOM CSV templates for RDC and PRE. The optional versioned [joint_pcs_rdc] project section retains RDC inputs, selected PCS observation IDs, conditions and the last recorded joint result. The main structure/PCS observations remain in their normal sections. Loading checks recorded predictions against recorded inputs without refitting or applying the tensor. Corrupt joint sections reject project loading; older files without the section use empty joint inputs and defaults.

PRE rejects malformed/duplicate observations; it does not silently skip them. Its optional versioned [pre_fitting] section retains observations, fit conditions and a verified recorded result without rerunning. See the PRE tutorial. Multi-Lanthanide adds an optional versioned [multi_lanthanide] JSON section for typed datasets, conditions and verified results per analysis. See its tutorial for coefficient and transfer limits. See Fitting Overview for current workflow limitations.

docs.title: PCS plot data
docs.text:
File → Save plot data... behaves according to the chosen extension:

Choice Output XLSX One workbook with PCS Data and Atom Coordinates sheets CSV Two UTF-8-with-BOM files: <base>_pcs.csv and <base>_atoms.csv PNG The currently open 2D PCS polar plot at the configured export DPI

The PCS-data output contains θ samples plus PCS level, radius, and Cartesian plot coordinates for each contour. The atom-coordinate output contains the visible atom labels, radius, θ, and geometrical factor. The exported Theta values in these data files are radians. PNG export requires the 2D PCS Plot window to be open. An absent or unrecognized extension falls back to XLSX.

docs.title: Main and rhombicity tables
docs.text:
File → Save table... exports the rows currently displayed in the main table.

  • XLSX creates a Table sheet and, when populated, a Rhombicity sheet.
  • CSV creates <base>_table.csv and, when populated, <base>_rhombicity.csv.

The main table columns are Ref, Atom, X, Y, Z, G_i, δ_PCS, and δ_Exp. The rhombicity export includes its displayed angular, Gi_ax, Gi_rh, axial/rhombic PCS, and residual columns.

The main-table δ_PCS column follows the active Axial/Full tensor prediction model; the rhombic term contributes only when enabled. Axial-plus-rhombic predictions, when enabled, remain separate columns in the rhombicity export.

docs.title: Experimental template
docs.text: Export δ_Exp Template writes visible main-table rows as Ref, Atom, and δ_Exp in CSV or XLSX. It preserves existing δ_Exp cells so the file can be edited and re-imported. See Experimental-data Import and Export.

docs.title: Visible XYZ
docs.text: File → Save current XYZ... writes a standard XYZ atom-count line, a PCS Analyzer comment line, and coordinate rows. It exports only currently visible elements from the effective structure. Coordinates include an applied fit orientation/centre override when supported, are centred on the active metal, and include the current X/Y/Z rotations. This is therefore a transformed analysis view, not necessarily the untouched input coordinates.

docs.title: Plot and viewer exports
docs.text:
Export capabilities differ by view.

View Explicit file export G_ax vs PCS PNG, SVG, or PDF figure, plus <base>_summary.txt and <base>_points.csv companion files Standard Fitting PNG or PDF correlation/residual figure Projection PNG, PDF, or SVG figure 3D Structure → Figure output PNG, or PDF/SVG containing an embedded image 3D Structure → Viewport capture PNG; experimental PDF/SVG that may contain raster content Retained Matplotlib structure viewer PNG/PDF/SVG from its own camera Main 3D PCS Plot PNG only; either live-view resolution or an off-screen DPI/width render Conformer Search PNG/PDF/SVG structure plot, multi-model XYZ for selected candidates, and TXT report NMR Workbench Spectrum figures through the Matplotlib toolbar; NMR Data observed-shift CSV; assignment CSV and analysis tables/JSON/figures through their respective windows. Save .nmrsession for recovery.

Figure PDF/SVG from the molecular viewer do not contain editable vector atoms, bonds or labels. See the 3D Structure Viewer for output choices.

The Gᵢ companion CSV contains Ref, Atom, G_i, δ_Exp, δ_PCS, and Residual. The standard Fitting export saves the plot only; the textual fit report and numeric result are not written by that button. Use Fit History JSON/CSV export to retain numerical results.

Viewer-specific details are documented under Visualization and in the NMR Workbench. See Raw Data and Processing for vendor dataset inputs.

docs.title: PCS Workbench outputs
docs.text:
Use File → Export 3D data… for PCS or density volumes and selected isosurfaces. Choose the full grid, input region or custom bounds. Every data export writes a JSON sidecar with units, grid information and calculation conditions; keep the pair together. NPY stores the array alone; NPZ includes associated data, with additional solver/tensor arrays for a full unsmoothed PCS export. Cropped, smoothed and density exports have different contents.

Other outputs include atom-comparison CSV (UTF-8 with BOM), PCS-viewer PNG, tensor PNG/GIF, and slice PNG/PDF/SVG. They are workflow-specific, rather than formats supported by every Analyzer viewer. See 3D Data Export for available formats, precision and options.

docs.title: Fit-run exports
docs.text: In Fit History → More ▾, Export selected as JSON… saves complete standard runs for Import Fit Run(s)…. Export selected as CSV… writes <base>_summary.csv; for one selected run it also writes <base>_observables.csv. Multiple selected runs produce only the summary CSV. CSV and figure files cannot be imported as complete fit runs. Importing a JSON run does not restore the source project or apply its tensor. See Fit History.

docs.title: Reproducing an analysis
docs.text:
Keep the following together:

  1. The .pcsp project containing the structure, centre, prediction policy, tensor/orientation, experimental targets/uncertainties and averaging settings.
  2. Original structures and experimental source data, with assignments and processing/referencing notes; retain raw FIDs for NMR-derived shifts.
  3. Complete fit-run JSON and, when useful, observation/residual CSVs. Label runs by subset, fitted/fixed parameters and model assumptions; record excluded observations and reasons. A plot or screenshot alone is insufficient.
  4. Application version and analysis notes, including initialization, weighting, averaging ranges/sample counts, and any temporary geometry preview.
  5. Optional .pcsw plus all referenced projects when reproducing a multi-document session. Keep their folder layout; the workspace does not embed data.

After reopening, check inputs and fit status, then verify live predictions. Stored fit predictions describe the original run. In particular, a temporary Mode C preview is retained separately from the assigned metal centre in current files. Older files without its complete preview values require recreating it from the recorded run. Retain that run and its reported coordinates. A visible XYZ export may contain transformed/averaged geometry and filtered atoms, so preserve the original structure separately.

docs.title: JSON viewer presets
docs.text:
The 3D Structure viewer saves appearance, background, PCS colors, axes and Figure options through File → Visualization settings → Save… / Load…. These files use format pcs-analyzer-visualization, version 1. They exclude coordinates, calculated PCS/tensors, camera, selection and shared main-application controls; keep the .pcsp project separately. See Save and reuse visualization settings.

The main 3D PCS Plot can save and load a JSON preset containing its level styles, grid/surface/atom display controls, colors, camera preset/projection, and PNG export options. PCS Workbench also saves and loads JSON parameter presets for its own control panel.

Preset files store controls, not structures, experimental data, or calculated fields. These workflows use separate presets; keep them with their corresponding project or source data.

docs.title: Plugin files
docs.text:
At a high level, the Module Manager accepts a single Python file (.py), a selected plugin folder, or a ZIP package (.zip). Folder and ZIP packages use manifest.json and a Python entry file; a .py installation generates that installed layout. JSON viewer presets and plugin manifests serve unrelated purposes even though both use .json.

See Distribution and Installation for the accepted layouts and current security limitations, and Plugin Manifest for fields that are operational, descriptive, or not enforced.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
These terms describe PCS Analyzer's controls and results. For numerical definitions and units, see Mathematical Conventions and Units.

Term Meaning PCS Pseudocontact shift: the contribution modeled from geometry and magnetic susceptibility anisotropy. It is not every paramagnetic shift contribution. δ_obs / δ_dia Observed paramagnetic-sample shift and its diamagnetic reference shift, in ppm. δ_para δ_obs − δ_dia. It can include contact and other contributions in addition to PCS. δ_Exp Experimental PCS supplied as a fitting/diagnostic target. Treating δ_para as δ_Exp requires a scientific assumption or correction. δ_PCS Calculated PCS under the active structure, tensor, orientation and averaging model. δ_nonPCS δ_para minus calculated PCS: a diagnostic difference, not a unique physical separation of contact shift. Ref / Ref ID One-based atom identifier assigned in structure-file order. An element label alone is not a unique assignment. PCS observation / target An experimental value and the structural atom or group to which it is assigned. A grouped target contributes one observation, not one per member. NMR site A structural grouping used for assignment/averaging. A grouping or suggested match does not establish experimental equivalence. Assigned centre The metal/PCS origin chosen for the working structure. Refined centre A centre estimated by fitting. Mode C Preview can use it temporarily without replacing the assigned centre. G_ax / G_rh Axial and rhombic geometrical factors in Å⁻³, calculated in the tensor frame. Δχ_ax / Δχ_rh Axial and rhombic susceptibility anisotropies, entered as numerical multiples of 10⁻³² m³ per molecule. Structure XYZ / Tensor Euler ZYZ Different rotation representations. Equivalent orientations can have different angle numbers; do not copy the three numbers between conventions. Residual Difference between prediction and experiment. Its sign depends on the workflow; see Residual Analysis. Current / Stale / Unknown Result-validity states: matching working inputs, changed inputs, or insufficient evidence to establish a match. Current does not certify scientific correctness. Preview / Apply Preview temporarily displays supported fitted geometry; Apply transfers the fields supported by that workflow. Neither is performed just by running a fit. Project / workspace / NMR session .pcsp analysis data, .pcsw references to saved projects, and .nmrsession recoverable NMR work. Their scopes differ.

For derivation and structural mapping, see Experimental PCS Data. For result state and application, see Fitting Overview and Projects and Persistence.

docs.title: Current Limitations
docs.text: This page describes limits relevant to the current source workflows. A successful fit, saved report or visualization does not establish a unique scientific model. See each workflow's manual for inputs, equations and interpretation.

docs.title: Fitting and confidence
docs.text:
• Standard Modes A/B accept nonempty matched selections without enforcing three independent points. Select enough independent observations for the parameters; the ability to run does not establish identifiability. Mode C rejects fewer than three matched observations but can still be underdetermined.
  • Standard nonlinear fits, Joint PCS+RDC and PRE do not estimate parameter confidence intervals. Multi-Conformer reliability intervals and Reilley standard errors are conditional on their documented assumptions.
  • Mode A provides geometry preview only. Mode B Apply Tensor copies axial anisotropy/orientation and retains the main rhombic value/enablement. Mode C tensor application retains the assigned metal centre; its refined centre is available in temporary geometry preview.
  • Multi-Lanthanide separates PCS and total paramagnetic-shift inputs. Reilley assumes a compatible Ln series; its Sm/Eu coefficients remain fixed at 300 K even when another temperature is selected. Derived PCS values share fitted coefficient uncertainty and are not independent measured observations.

Details: Fitting Overview, Quality Metrics, Multi-Conformer reliability, and Multi-Lanthanide/Reilley.

docs.title: Saving and reproducibility
docs.text:
Document Undo/Redo covers standard Mode B/C tensor Apply, Conformer Apply/Revert, main-table δ_Exp editing, shift-import Apply/Clear, the existing Undo import action, NMR Workbench PCS transfers, confirmed tensor/XYZ/ZYZ orientation edits, rhombic enablement, explicit raw-Ref metal-centre assignment and main-window XYZ/ORCA structure replacement with its coupled Ref-based inputs. Control Panel Reset also records its cleared working data and standard Fit History. Axial/Full tensor prediction-model selection is recorded without changing the stored tensor parameters or rhombic enablement. Fitting Preview Geometry and Clear Preview are recorded, including Mode C's fitted Δχ input values imported by its immediate redraw. It is separate from recorded fit/search results and is limited to the latest 100 session edits; project files do not persist its stack. Input imports outside these workflows and project/workspace opening are not recorded as standalone actions. Reset can restore the policy and temporary geometry it cleared. NMR source sessions and transfer receipts are not undone.

Projects preserve complete standard fit runs and supported advanced results, not an exact restoration of all windows and interaction state. Current files retain active Mode C previews. Older files missing their centre/orientation cannot restore that preview; use the retained fit run to recreate it. Current projects retain the latest Conformer Search candidate set and its inputs; older scalar summaries cannot reconstruct it. Search results remain viewable and exportable when inputs change, but Apply requires matching recorded host and search scientific inputs. Only completed search sets are persisted; replacement input files without a completed search are not separate saved sessions. Row selections, zoom/hover and import undo are transient. Residual-colour cutoffs and Color state are restored for the main and Rhombicity tables; changes to these display settings are outside scientific Undo/Redo. Export-DPI values recorded in a project are not reapplied by the loader.

A workspace contains paths to saved projects rather than unsaved scientific changes. NMR sessions must be saved separately. Older supported sections have defaults and compatibility handling, but cross-version loading is not a guarantee of identical behavior. Keep source data and exported run records.

See Projects and Persistence, File Formats, and NMR Sessions.

docs.title: Structure search and distributed PCS
docs.text:
Earlier source versions passed main-window XYZ angle numbers directly to the Conformer Search's ZYZ calculator. Current Sync Main preserves the rotation matrix through conversion; rerun nonzero-orientation searches made with older versions. See Conformer Search.

PCS Workbench treats .3d origin/spacing as Å and uses absolute density values for calculation; original signed samples are retained separately for export. It chooses a metal automatically, falling back to the first atom when needed. Check these assumptions against the source calculation. Grid extent, resolution and FFT padding can require substantial memory. See Workbench interpretation limits.

The padding convergence check measures numerical padding sensitivity, not experimental accuracy. Tensor transfer requires the same ordered structure and assigned centre; automatic atom matching and different conformations are not supported. Exported surfaces are individual levels, not complete viewer scenes, and external-reader support varies.

docs.title: Viewers and data import
docs.text: Viewer availability depends on installed/bundled PyVista, VTK and Qt dependencies. Matplotlib export formats depend on the active backend. Legacy .xls reading requires a compatible pandas Excel engine; use XLSX or CSV where appropriate. See Installation and Import and Export.

docs.title: Modules and plugins
docs.text:
Plugins execute Python in the host process and are not sandboxed. Catalog SHA-256 checks establish integrity against metadata, not safety or scientific correctness. New package installation validates paths, manifests and compatibility bounds; replacement uses backups and attempts rollback. Filesystem failures or locked files can still require restart and leave recovery paths.

Restart after update/replacement to execute new code. Disabling/removing a plugin does not undo its side effects or close its windows. Legacy manifest loading is more permissive and can report compatibility warnings. PluginApp remains an unversioned helper rather than a stable isolated extension API.

See Module Manager, Distribution, and Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Validation boundaries
docs.text:
Source checks and worked examples do not certify every platform, packaged build, external module or experimental dataset. Platform/runtime dependencies, large volumetric calculations and Windows file locks need environment-specific checks. Current PCS Workbench UI captures use illustrative data. Earlier field, slice, comparison and spheroid images remain scientific illustrations of their recorded workflow; they are not newly recalculated 0.1.1 validation results.

Historical development findings are kept in the repository's development records; this page is a current user guide, not a complete bug tracker or release guarantee.

docs.title: Mathematical Conventions
docs.text: This reference collects conventions that affect how project and exported data should be interpreted. It links to the canonical scientific pages rather than repeating their full derivations.

docs.title: Shift notation
docs.text:
Mathematical notation UI label Meaning \(\delta_{\mathrm{obs}}\) δ_obs Observed chemical shift in the paramagnetic sample \(\delta_{\mathrm{dia}}\) δ_dia Corresponding diamagnetic-reference shift \(\delta_{\mathrm{para}}=\delta_{\mathrm{obs}}-\delta_{\mathrm{dia}}\) δ_para Total paramagnetic shift contribution derived from those two layers \(\delta_{\mathrm{Exp}}\) δ_Exp User-assigned experimental PCS target used by the main regression and fitting workflows \(\delta_{\mathrm{PCS,calc}}\) δ_PCS Calculated PCS under the active Axial or Full tensor prediction policy; Full tensor includes rhombicity only when enabled \(\delta_{\mathrm{nonPCS}}=\delta_{\mathrm{para}}-\delta_{\mathrm{PCS,calc}}\) δ_nonPCS Residual-like NMR diagnostic; not a uniquely assigned physical contribution

UI and exported column labels retain their implemented capitalization and underscores. In equations, the same quantities are typeset as mathematical subscripts. Paramagnetic shift and experimental PCS are not automatically interchangeable; see Experimental PCS Data and Observed and Diamagnetic Shifts.

docs.title: Atom identifiers
docs.text:
Main-workflow Ref IDs are integers assigned from structure order, starting at 1. Experimental values, project data, table exports, conformer-search CSV, and many advanced inputs use these IDs as their join key.

The exact table and preferred file-column label is Ref. This documentation uses Ref ID as the short prose form and reference ID when the expanded term reads more clearly; both refer to the same identifier.

Filtering atoms does not renumber them. A Ref ID from a reordered or different structure must not be assumed to identify the same nucleus. See Experimental-data Import and Export.

docs.title: Coordinate frame and rotations
docs.text:
The main PCS workflow retains absolute input coordinates but evaluates PCS in a metal-centred tensor frame. Rotations are active, extrinsic rotations about fixed Cartesian axes in X → Y → Z order in the Structure controls. Tensor Euler (ZYZ) expresses the same molecular-to-tensor rotation using active intrinsic ZYZ angles. The same numeric triplet generally represents different rotations in XYZ and ZYZ. UI and project angles are degrees; projects retain the equivalent XYZ representation.

See Coordinate Handling for matrices, row-vector application, and the coordinate flow.

docs.title: Tensor and angular conventions
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer defines Δχ_ax, Δχ_rh, tensor principal components, θ, and φ as documented in Tensor Conventions. The axial term is invariant to z-axis rotation; a rhombic term depends on the in-plane x/y reference through φ.

The implemented definitions are

\[ \Delta\chi_{\mathrm{ax}} =\chi_{zz}-\frac{\chi_{xx}+\chi_{yy}}{2}, \qquad \Delta\chi_{\mathrm{rh}}=\chi_{xx}-\chi_{yy}. \]

The Half/Quarter plot toggle names display domains, not fractions of a stored tensor or sampling interval. Half view displays \(0^\circ\leq\theta\leq180^\circ\); Quarter view displays \(0^\circ\leq\theta\leq90^\circ\) and folds atom positions from the other hemisphere. See PCS Contour Plots.

Some exported angle columns use radians while UI/table columns use degrees. The exact file-level distinction is listed in Units.

docs.title: Residual signs
docs.text:
Residual sign is workflow-specific:

  • standard and advanced nonlinear fits use predicted minus experimental;
  • the main table colours calculated PCS minus δ_Exp;
  • Rhombicity Check and the Rhombicity Table display experimental minus predicted; and
  • NMR δ_nonPCS is δ_para minus calculated PCS.

See Residual Analysis before comparing signed residual columns from different exports. RMSD and absolute-residual rankings are unaffected by reversing the sign.

docs.title: Numeric text and missing values
docs.text:
Project files use a period as the decimal separator and UTF-8 text. Their fixed-column structure/delta rows are parsed strictly. Spreadsheet import has its own header matching, preview, and clear/skip rules; do not apply .pcsp editing assumptions to CSV or Excel data.

See Projects and Persistence and File Formats for format-specific behavior.

docs.title: Method References and Reporting
docs.text: Use these references for the scientific background of an analysis. The linked workflow pages define the model and options implemented in PCS Analyzer; a reference to a general method is not evidence that every variant is supported.

docs.title: PCS and susceptibility conventions
docs.text:
The point-dipole PCS expression and its extension to distributed spin density are discussed in A partial differential equation for pseudocontact shift. For broader context, see Magnetic susceptibility and paramagnetism-based NMR.

For calculations in this application, use the definitions in PCS Theory and Tensor Conventions: coordinates in Å, anisotropies in 10⁻³² m³ per molecule and output shifts in ppm. Check axial/rhombic definitions and frame conventions before comparing published tensors. The PCS Workbench describes the separate point/distributed-field comparison and its grid assumptions.

docs.title: Lanthanide series and Reilley separation
docs.text:
• Bleaney's Nuclear magnetic resonance shifts in solution due to lanthanide ions provides the historical lanthanide-shift framework.
  • Separation of contact and dipolar lanthanide induced nuclear magnetic resonance shifts: evaluation and application of some structure independent methods is an original-method reference for contact/dipolar separation.
  • Pinkerton et al. (1985), Table 1, is the source identified for the RHF spin-factor coefficients.
  • The DTMA fluoride-binding study is an application example, not the original source of the separation method.

The Multi-Lanthanide tutorial states the application's relative C_D convention, temperature expression, fixed Sm/Eu approximation and common-temperature requirements. Report those choices when interpreting separated components. A linear trend alone does not establish unchanged geometry or contact coupling across the series.

docs.title: Joint PCS and RDC
docs.text: The general relationship between susceptibility anisotropy and paramagnetic NMR observables, including RDC, is covered by the susceptibility review. The Joint PCS+RDC tutorial specifies the narrower implemented model: magnetic self-alignment, a fixed structure/frame, two fitted tensor scalars and the stated residual weighting. RDC from a separate alignment medium is outside that model.

docs.title: PRE
docs.text: The PRE tutorial gives the actual proton Γ₂ equation and omitted terms. Compare it with the Xplor-NIH PRE model description and the relaxation-model discussion, equations 12–14. Report the magnetic field, moment, correlation-time bounds and errors, and explain why the simplified model is appropriate for the sample. An ion preset or a fitted effective time alone does not establish that appropriateness.

docs.title: Reliability evaluation
docs.text:
SciPy's bootstrap documentation explains percentile resampling intervals. The grouped cross-validation documentation and data-leakage guidance provide statistical background for keeping related observations together and withheld data out of training. These are method explanations, not additional PCS Analyzer dependencies or a claim that its evaluator calls those APIs.

The Multi-Conformer tutorial defines the implemented parametric/cases bootstrap, grouping, failed-refit handling and held-out score. Its intervals are conditional on the supplied geometry, mapping, orientation and model; they do not propagate uncertainty in those inputs.

docs.title: Report a reproducible analysis
docs.text:
Alongside the software version and archived-release citation, retain:

  • original structure and experimental data, acquisition/reference conditions, assignments and any excluded observations with reasons;
  • tensor units/frame, averaging assumptions and fitted versus fixed parameters;
  • initialization, bounds, objective weights and diagnostic results;
  • a saved project and numerical result exports; NMR work also needs its session;
  • for reliability evaluation, resampling method, group definition, seed, requested and successful refit counts, and failed/partial evaluation status.

Use the file-format reproducibility checklist for the supported exports. A screenshot alone does not retain a complete fit.
