docs.title: VT observed-shift coordinates
docs.text: NMR Workbench uses effective temperature T in K, inverse temperature 1/T in K⁻¹, observed shift δ in ppm and δT in ppm·K. Curie/ Curie-Weiss parameters use offset in ppm, C in ppm·K and θ in K. θ is a temperature-model parameter, not an orientation angle. Coordinate-linear fit units depend on the selected axes; raw-shift model metrics and transformed plot residuals have different domains. See VT Analysis.

docs.title: Coordinate and angle exports
docs.text:
XYZ output always contains Cartesian coordinates in Å. The main Save current XYZ... command writes the transformed, metal-centred view rather than the original absolute input coordinates; see File Formats.

Do not infer an angle's unit from the word Theta alone. Main PCS plot-data exports use radians, while Rhombicity Table headings explicitly use degrees. Application rotation entries and fitted-angle reports are degrees.

The distinction between δ_Exp, calculated PCS, observed/diamagnetic shifts, and δ_nonPCS is summarized in Mathematical Conventions.

docs.title: Susceptibility units
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer's Δχ inputs use \(10^{-32}\,\mathrm{m^3}\) per molecule. Tensor reconstruction may also display SI molar susceptibility in \(\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}\). These are not numerically interchangeable without the documented scaling and Avogadro conversion.

See Tensor Conventions for the complete definitions and the cgs-to-SI warning. See PCS Theory for the PCS prefactor used with the geometry factors. PCS Workbench's separate ORCA conversion and grid assumptions are documented under PCS Workbench Inputs.

docs.title: PCS Workbench exports
docs.text: PCS values remain in ppm. CUBE/CUB uses Bohr for atom coordinates, grid origin and spacing; the other implemented volume/mesh exports use Å. Normalized solver density uses Å⁻³ internally and Bohr⁻³ in CUBE. Original signed density retains its source values, marked source_units; the loader does not establish their physical unit. The JSON sidecar records the units of each export. See 3D Data Export.

docs.title: Coordinate Handling
docs.text:
PCS calculations depend on the position of each observed nucleus relative to the magnetic-susceptibility tensor frame.

PCS Analyzer therefore keeps the input structure and the PCS working coordinate frame conceptually separate. The original structure remains stored in its input coordinate system, while centre translation and rotations are applied to working coordinates as required.

docs.title: Coordinate representations
docs.text: The structure workflow uses several related coordinate representations.

docs.title: Original coordinates
docs.text:
The coordinates parsed from the input structure are stored as the original structure. These coordinates are expressed in Å and retain the coordinate frame of the source file.

The original representation is retained so that the initially loaded geometry can be restored after operations such as conformer manipulation.

docs.title: Raw coordinates
docs.text:
The raw structure is the current unaveraged molecular geometry used by the application.

Immediately after structure loading, the raw and original coordinates are identical. Operations that intentionally modify the current geometry may update the raw coordinates while leaving the initially stored original geometry available for restoration.

docs.title: Effective coordinates
docs.text:
When symmetry averaging is enabled, PCS Analyzer generates a separate effective coordinate representation for the averaging-aware analysis path.

When symmetry averaging is disabled,

\[ \mathbf r_i^{\mathrm{eff}} = \mathbf r_i^{\mathrm{raw}}. \]

The raw structure is retained independently so that the original atomic geometry remains available to viewers and other tools that require explicit atoms.

See Symmetry Averaging.

docs.title: PCS origin
docs.text:
Let the selected paramagnetic-centre coordinate in the input frame be

\[ \mathbf r_\mathrm{M} = (x_\mathrm{M},y_\mathrm{M},z_\mathrm{M}). \]

For PCS geometrical analysis, working coordinates are translated to the centre:

\[ \mathbf r_i^{\,0} = \mathbf r_i-\mathbf r_\mathrm{M}. \]

Thus,

\[ \mathbf r_\mathrm{M}^{\,0} = (0,0,0). \]

This translation is performed on the working coordinates. The raw atom list remains stored in the absolute coordinate frame of the imported structure.

This distinction is important for modules that explicitly require the original absolute geometry.

docs.title: Coordinate-frame rotation
docs.text:
After translation to the PCS origin, coordinates can be rotated relative to the tensor frame.

PCS Analyzer uses active, extrinsic rotations about fixed Cartesian axes. The default Euler order is

XYZ

meaning that the rotations are applied in the order:

X → Y → Z

For column-vector notation, the corresponding combined rotation matrix is

\[ \mathbf R = \mathbf R_z \mathbf R_y \mathbf R_x. \]

PCS Analyzer stores coordinate arrays as row vectors and therefore applies the transformation as

\[ \mathbf r_i' = \mathbf r_i^{\,0}\mathbf R^{\mathrm T}. \]

docs.title: Rotation matrices
docs.text:
For an angle \(\alpha\) about the \(x\)-axis,

\[ \mathbf R_x(\alpha) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & \cos\alpha & -\sin\alpha\\ 0 & \sin\alpha & \cos\alpha \end{pmatrix}. \]

For an angle \(\beta\) about the \(y\)-axis,

\[ \mathbf R_y(\beta) = \begin{pmatrix} \cos\beta & 0 & \sin\beta\\ 0 & 1 & 0\\ -\sin\beta & 0 & \cos\beta \end{pmatrix}. \]

For an angle \(\gamma\) about the \(z\)-axis,

\[ \mathbf R_z(\gamma) = \begin{pmatrix} \cos\gamma & -\sin\gamma & 0\\ \sin\gamma & \cos\gamma & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}. \]

Angles entered through the application are interpreted in degrees and converted internally to radians for the trigonometric operations.

docs.title: Structure XYZ and Tensor Euler ZYZ
docs.text:
Structure uses the extrinsic XYZ controls described above. Tensor Euler (ZYZ) expresses the same active molecular-to-tensor rotation with intrinsic ZYZ angles:

\[ \mathbf R=\mathbf R_z(\alpha)\mathbf R_y(\beta)\mathbf R_z(\gamma). \]

Both use degrees. Switching representations preserves the physical rotation; the displayed angle values may change. The same numeric XYZ and ZYZ triplets are generally not equivalent. At an Euler singularity, different triplets can represent the same rotation, so compare the orientation rather than angle values alone. For an axial tensor, rotation about its principal z-axis is unobservable in PCS; the ZYZ α control is disabled while rhombicity is disabled. Standard Mode B/C fit angles are XYZ even when the panel shows Tensor Euler ZYZ.

Conformer Search handoff

Sync Main converts the main Structure XYZ orientation to the search calculator's ZYZ representation while preserving the rotation matrix. The displayed angle numbers can differ while describing the same direction. Older implementations passed the numbers without conversion; searches made with that behavior at nonzero orientation should be rerun. See Conformer Search.

docs.title: Rotation about an arbitrary centre
docs.text:
The general coordinate-rotation helper can rotate a structure about any specified point \(\mathbf c\).

The transformation is

\[ \mathbf r_i' = \mathbf c + \mathbf R \left( \mathbf r_i-\mathbf c \right) \]

in column-vector notation.

For the main PCS geometrical calculation, the structure has already been translated relative to the paramagnetic centre, so the rotation centre is

\[ \mathbf c=(0,0,0). \]

Other viewers may instead rotate coordinates around an explicitly supplied molecular centre.

docs.title: Geometrical coordinates
docs.text:
After translation and rotation, a nucleus is represented relative to the PCS tensor frame by

\[ \mathbf r_i' = (x_i,y_i,z_i). \]

The radial distance is

\[ r_i = \sqrt{x_i^2+y_i^2+z_i^2}. \]

The polar angle is

\[ \theta_i = \cos^{-1} \left( \frac{z_i}{r_i} \right). \]

For rhombic PCS calculations, the azimuthal angle is defined by the orientation of the coordinate in the \(xy\)-plane and enters through the rhombic geometrical factor.

The axial term is invariant to rotation around the principal \(z\)-axis, whereas a rhombic term distinguishes the \(x\) and \(y\) directions.

docs.title: X-, Y-, and Z-axis roles
docs.text:
For the default axial PCS model, the \(z\)-axis defines the principal axial direction.

Changing the X- and Y-axis rotations changes the orientation of the molecular geometry relative to this axis and therefore changes \(r,\theta\)-dependent PCS geometry.

When rhombicity is included, the orientation of the \(x\)- and \(y\)-axes also becomes physically relevant. Rotation around the \(z\)-axis changes the azimuthal relationship between the structure and the rhombic tensor component without changing the axial \(G_{\mathrm{ax}}\) term.

docs.title: Vector alignment helper
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer also contains a vector-alignment operation based on Rodrigues' rotation formula.

Given two vectors,

\[ \mathbf v_1 \quad\text{and}\quad \mathbf v_2, \]

the operation constructs a rotation that aligns \(\mathbf v_1\) with \(\mathbf v_2\).

The alignment helper first translates the coordinate set so that its first atom is at the origin and then applies the rotation.

Parallel vectors require no rotation. For antiparallel vectors, the current helper returns the inverted translated coordinate set.

This operation is separate from the standard X/Y/Z coordinate controls and is used by command-based alignment functionality.

docs.title: Coordinate flow
docs.text:
The standard PCS coordinate path can be summarized as

Parsed absolute coordinates
        ↓
Raw/effective structure selection
        ↓
Subtract paramagnetic-centre coordinate
        ↓
Centre-relative coordinates
        ↓
Apply active XYZ rotation
        ↓
Tensor-frame coordinates
        ↓
r, θ and azimuthal geometry
        ↓
PCS geometrical factors

Absolute versus centre-relative coordinates

PCS Analyzer deliberately retains absolute raw coordinates while generating centre-relative coordinates for PCS calculations.

This prevents coordinate-frame ambiguity in modules that operate directly on the molecular geometry while allowing the PCS analysis to use the selected paramagnetic centre as its origin.

docs.title: Structure Files & Parsing
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer converts supported structure files into a common internal atom representation,

(element, x, y, z)

where the Cartesian coordinates are stored in Å.

This page describes the file syntax accepted by the structure loader and the internal processing performed before PCS analysis.

docs.title: Replacing a working structure
docs.text:
Main-window Load XYZ also accepts ORCA .out/.log. The file is parsed before any working data are replaced; the centre is the first atom matching the entered element. Cancel, a missing centre or an unusable file leaves the document unchanged.

An accepted load is one Undo/Redo action. New Ref IDs start at 1. Old PCS, observed/diamagnetic shifts, structured observations and their transfer/import metadata are cleared to prevent old mappings from being applied to the new atom numbering. Structure-specific rotational groups and temporary geometry are also reset. Undo restores the prior structure, centre, coupled data, visibility and rotational enablement. The tensor/orientation and recorded fit or search reports remain; check their Current/Stale state before applying a result. Redo restores the accepted data without rereading the file or asking for a centre. Opening a project/workspace or replacing inputs inside a standalone tool is outside this structure-load history scope.

docs.title: Changing the assigned centre
docs.text: After loading, right-click an existing raw atom row in the main table and choose Set Ref … as metal center (clear preview). This explicitly assigns the Ref's absolute raw coordinates as the centre without moving atoms or renumbering Refs. The action clears a temporary geometry preview and participates in document Undo/Redo; recorded fit/search results remain. Pseudo-atoms without a raw Ref cannot be assigned through this command.

docs.title: Supported structure formats
docs.text:
The structure loader accepts:

  • XYZ files (.xyz)
  • ORCA output files (.out)
  • ORCA log files (.log)

The file extension determines which parser is used.

docs.title: Standard XYZ syntax
docs.text:
A conventional XYZ file contains an atom count, one comment line, and one coordinate line for each atom:

5
example structure
U   0.000000   0.000000   0.000000
N   2.350000   0.000000   0.000000
N  -1.175000   2.035160   0.000000
N  -1.175000  -2.035160   0.000000
H   0.000000   0.000000   3.000000

If the first non-empty line is an integer, PCS Analyzer interprets it as the atom-count header and skips exactly two lines: the atom-count line and the following comment line. The comment line may be blank.

Headerless XYZ-like coordinate files are also accepted.

docs.title: Accepted coordinate-line forms
docs.text: The XYZ parser accepts several common whitespace-separated formats.

docs.title: Element and coordinates
docs.text:
U  0.000000  0.000000  0.000000

interpreted as

Element  X  Y  Z

docs.title: Atom index, element, and coordinates
docs.text:
1  U  0.000000  0.000000  0.000000

interpreted as

Index  Element  X  Y  Z

docs.title: Element, atomic number, and coordinates
docs.text:
U  92  0.000000  0.000000  0.000000

interpreted as

Element  AtomicNumber  X  Y  Z

docs.title: Atom index, element, atomic number, and coordinates
docs.text:
1  U  92  0.000000  0.000000  0.000000

interpreted as

Index  Element  AtomicNumber  X  Y  Z

Only the element symbol and the three Cartesian coordinates are retained internally. Atom indices and atomic-number columns, when present, are not stored as part of the coordinate tuple.

Lines that do not match one of the supported coordinate patterns are skipped.

docs.title: ORCA output files
docs.text:
For .out and .log files, PCS Analyzer searches for ORCA Cartesian-coordinate sections with headers of the form

CARTESIAN COORDINATES (ANGSTROEM)

or

CARTESIAN COORDINATES (BOHR)

Coordinate rows are read as

Element  X  Y  Z

until the coordinate block ends.

docs.title: Multiple coordinate blocks
docs.text:
ORCA calculations may contain several Cartesian-coordinate blocks, for example during a geometry optimization.

The standard PCS Analyzer structure loader uses the last detected coordinate block, which normally corresponds to the latest geometry written to the output file.

Internally, the parser also supports extraction of the first block or all coordinate blocks, although the normal loading workflow uses the last block.

docs.title: Unit conversion
docs.text:
Coordinates reported by ORCA in Å are used directly.

Coordinates reported in Bohr are converted according to

\[ 1\ \mathrm{Bohr} = 0.529177210903\ \text{Å}. \]

All structures therefore enter the main PCS Analyzer workflow in Å.

docs.title: Internal processing
docs.text:
After parsing, supported structure formats are represented by the same internal atom list and pass through a common processing sequence.

Input structure file
        ↓
File-extension dispatch
        ↓
XYZ or ORCA coordinate parsing
        ↓
Internal atom list: (element, x, y, z)
        ↓
Store original/raw coordinates
        ↓
Identify the selected paramagnetic centre
        ↓
Generate optional symmetry-averaged coordinates
        ↓
Translate working coordinates relative to the centre
        ↓
Apply coordinate-frame rotation
        ↓
Calculate geometrical quantities
        ↓
PCS analysis, fitting, and visualization

docs.title: Raw and original coordinates
docs.text:
Immediately after loading, PCS Analyzer stores the parsed coordinates as the original and raw structure representations.

The atom reference IDs initially correspond to the one-based order of atoms in the parsed structure:

1, 2, 3, ...

The raw coordinates remain in the absolute coordinate frame of the input file.

docs.title: Paramagnetic-centre identification
docs.text:
The user-specified centre element is searched in the parsed atom list from the beginning of the structure.

The first exact matching element label is selected. Its original Cartesian coordinates are stored as the paramagnetic-centre position.

If no matching atom is found, structure initialization is stopped and an error is reported.

The raw structure itself is not permanently translated at this stage. Instead, the centre coordinate is subtracted when centre-relative working coordinates are required.

docs.title: Effective structure representation
docs.text:
If coordinate symmetry averaging is disabled, the effective structure is identical to the raw structure.

If symmetry averaging is enabled, PCS Analyzer creates a separate effective atom list while preserving the raw coordinates. The averaging procedure is described in Symmetry Averaging.

docs.title: Centre-relative coordinates
docs.text:
For geometrical PCS analysis, the paramagnetic-centre coordinate

\[ \mathbf r_\mathrm{M} = (x_\mathrm{M},y_\mathrm{M},z_\mathrm{M}) \]

is subtracted from each working coordinate,

\[ \mathbf r_i^{\,0} = \mathbf r_i-\mathbf r_\mathrm{M}. \]

The selected centre therefore becomes the origin of the PCS coordinate system without modifying the stored raw structure.

docs.title: Coordinate-frame rotation
docs.text:
Centre-relative coordinates are then rotated according to the current coordinate-frame orientation.

The rotation implementation and coordinate conventions are described in Coordinate Handling.

docs.title: Geometrical quantities
docs.text:
The transformed coordinates are used to derive the geometrical quantities required by PCS analysis.

For a coordinate

\[ (x,y,z), \]

the radial distance is

\[ r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2}, \]

and the polar angle relative to the \(z\)-axis is

\[ \theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{z}{r}\right). \]

When a rhombic contribution is evaluated, the azimuthal orientation in the \(xy\)-plane is additionally relevant.

These centre-relative geometrical quantities are subsequently used by the PCS calculation, fitting, diagnostics, and visualization routines.

docs.title: Parsing limitations
docs.text:
The structure loader is intentionally lightweight and geometry-oriented.

It does not reconstruct chemical connectivity from the input file during basic parsing, and it does not use bond-order or electronic-structure information from ORCA output as part of the structure representation.

Bond connectivity required by features such as symmetry averaging is inferred separately from Cartesian distances and covalent radii.

Project files

PCS Analyzer project files (.pcsp) are application project containers rather than structure-file formats. They are handled separately from the XYZ/ORCA structure parser described on this page.

See Projects and Persistence for the embedded structure, restored analysis state, schema behavior, and recalculation performed when a project is opened.

docs.title: Symmetry and Torsional Ensemble Averaging
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer provides two complementary averaging approaches for PCS analysis:

  1. Local symmetry averaging for locally threefold groups such as methyl and trifluoromethyl groups.
  2. Torsional ensemble averaging for conformational motion about rotatable bonds, including automatically detected planar ring systems and manually defined torsional fragments.

Both approaches distinguish between a representative averaged coordinate used for display and an averaged geometrical factor used for PCS calculation.

Averaged coordinates are not used to approximate averaged PCS

PCS geometrical factors depend non-linearly on position through their angular terms and the \(r^{-3}\) distance dependence.

Therefore, in general,

\[ G(\langle \mathbf r \rangle) \neq \langle G(\mathbf r)\rangle. \]

PCS Analyzer consequently averages the geometrical factors calculated from the underlying atomic or sampled coordinates rather than evaluating \(G\) at the averaged coordinate.

docs.title: Averaging Settings
docs.text:
Averaging is configured from the dedicated Averaging Settings window.

Open Control Panel → Symmetry averaging → Options.... Enable the required local groups or Rotational ensemble averaging, review the detected groups, and choose Apply. Use Refresh detection after changing structure or detection settings. Group membership and motion must be scientifically appropriate; detection is a convenience, not evidence of rapid exchange.

The Nd(iPr₂BA)₃ documentation project already enables methyl averaging and three phenyl rotational groups. Its status summary is visible in the main workspace.

docs.title: Connectivity detection
docs.text: Groups are inferred from atom distances and covalent radii. Missing atoms, distorted geometry or ambiguous connectivity can produce missing or unsuitable groups. Inspect the detected membership before applying averaging. Bond-tolerance controls in viewers affect guide lines only, not averaging-group detection.

docs.title: Methyl and CF3 sites
docs.text:
Enable Local symmetry averaging, then CH₃ or CF₃, when the three nuclei represent an equivalent observed site on the NMR timescale. Each detected group is represented by one pseudo atom, labelled for example MeH@C12 or CF3F@C7, with a new Ref ID. Its display coordinate is the centroid,

\[ \mathbf r_\mathrm{avg}=\frac{\mathbf r_1+\mathbf r_2+\mathbf r_3}{3}. \]

This centroid is a visual representative, not the position used to calculate PCS. Check experimental assignments against the effective Ref IDs after changing averaging. Original unaffected atom IDs remain unchanged.

docs.title: Averaging disabled
docs.text: When the corresponding local-symmetry averaging option is disabled, no pseudo atom is generated for that group type and the original structure is retained.

docs.title: Keep original atoms disabled
docs.text:
When local symmetry averaging is enabled and Keep original atoms is disabled, the three original H or F member atoms are removed from the effective representation and replaced by one pseudo atom.

Conceptually,

H1 + H2 + H3        F1 + F2 + F3
     ↓                   ↓
   H_avg               F_avg

docs.title: Keep original atoms enabled
docs.text:
When Keep original atoms is enabled, the original member atoms remain visible and the corresponding pseudo atom is displayed in addition to them.

This option affects the representation only; the pseudo atom still represents the averaged local-symmetry site for PCS analysis.

docs.title: Local-symmetry geometrical-factor averaging
docs.text:
The pseudo-atom centroid is a representative coordinate only. PCS geometrical factors are calculated from the original member positions.

For the axial PCS model,

\[ G_{\mathrm{ax,avg}} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_i G_{\mathrm{ax},i}. \]

For a threefold group,

\[ G_{\mathrm{ax,avg}} = \frac{ G_{\mathrm{ax},1} + G_{\mathrm{ax},2} + G_{\mathrm{ax},3} }{3}. \]

When rhombicity is included, the axial and rhombic terms are averaged independently. Main predictions include the rhombic term only under Full tensor with rhombicity enabled; standard fitting uses its own fitted/fixed component choices:

\[ G_{\mathrm{ax,avg}} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_i G_{\mathrm{ax},i}, \] \[ G_{\mathrm{rh,avg}} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_i G_{\mathrm{rh},i}. \]

The averaged PCS is then

\[ \delta_{\mathrm{PCS,avg}} = \frac{10^4}{12\pi} \left( \Delta\chi_{\mathrm{ax}}G_{\mathrm{ax,avg}} + \Delta\chi_{\mathrm{rh}}G_{\mathrm{rh,avg}} \right). \]

For symmetry-equivalent nuclei with equal statistical weight, this is equivalent to averaging their individual PCS values.

docs.title: Concept
docs.text:
Torsional ensemble averaging represents conformational motion about a rotatable bond by explicitly sampling a set of molecular geometries.

For a torsional coordinate \(\phi\), the ensemble average of a geometrical factor is

\[ \langle G\rangle = \int G(\phi)P(\phi)\,d\phi, \]

where \(P(\phi)\) is the torsional probability distribution.

In the discrete implementation used by PCS Analyzer,

\[ \langle G\rangle \approx \sum_k w_k G_k, \qquad \sum_k w_k=1. \]

For uniform sampling,

\[ w_k=\frac{1}{N}. \]

The current controls use equal sample weights. They do not derive conformer populations from energies or steric accessibility.

docs.title: Phenyl-style rotational groups
docs.text: Auto planar rings proposes planar ligand fragments and their attachment axes, including phenyl-like and fused planar systems. Review the Ring and Axis entries and enable only the intended groups. Labels such as Phenyl-like describe geometry; they do not establish aromaticity, bond order, protonation or a unique chemical assignment. A fragment can include substituents that rotate with the ring. Metal-containing axes are excluded from automatic ligand-ring averaging.

docs.title: Manual torsion definition
docs.text:
When automatic detection is not appropriate, a torsional group can be defined manually.

The manual workflow specifies:

  • Manual axis A and B: the two Ref IDs defining the axis; and
  • Moving-side Ref: a Ref on the fragment that should rotate.

Choose Add manual, then review the group and its angular range.

Manual definition is useful for non-standard rotors, unusual connectivity, or cases where automatic cycle detection does not capture the intended motion.

docs.title: Angular range
docs.text: A torsional ensemble can represent either a full rotation or a restricted angular interval.

docs.title: Full rotation
docs.text: For full rotational averaging, the interval is sampled over 0–360° without duplicating the 360° endpoint.

docs.title: Restricted rotation
docs.text: A user-defined start and end angle can be used when the motion is known or assumed to occupy only part of the full torsional coordinate.

docs.title: Sampling density
docs.text:
The available sampling presets are:

Preset Samples Angular spacing for 360° Fast 12 30° Normal 24 15° Fine 72 5° Custom user-defined user-defined

Normal is the default compromise between angular resolution and computational cost.

docs.title: Ensemble-averaged coordinates
docs.text:
Each atom in a torsionally averaged fragment retains its original reference ID.

For atom \(i\), the representative averaged Cartesian coordinate is

\[ \langle \mathbf r_i\rangle = \sum_k w_k\mathbf r_{i,k}. \]

This coordinate is used for table display and structural visualization.

It should not be interpreted as a necessarily populated physical conformer. For a wide rotational distribution, the Cartesian average may lie at a position that is not occupied by any individual member of the ensemble.

No new pseudo atom is created for torsional averaging.

docs.title: Torsional geometrical-factor averaging
docs.text:
For each atom \(i\), geometrical factors are calculated for the sampled coordinates and then averaged:

\[ \bar G_{\mathrm{ax},i} = \sum_k w_kG_{\mathrm{ax},i,k}, \]

and, when rhombicity is included,

\[ \bar G_{\mathrm{rh},i} = \sum_k w_kG_{\mathrm{rh},i,k}. \]

The PCS for that atom is calculated as

\[ \delta_{\mathrm{PCS},i} = \frac{10^4}{12\pi} \left( \Delta\chi_{\mathrm{ax}}\bar G_{\mathrm{ax},i} + \Delta\chi_{\mathrm{rh}}\bar G_{\mathrm{rh},i} \right). \]

The PCS is therefore not calculated from

\[ G(\langle\mathbf r_i\rangle). \]

docs.title: Coordinate transformations during fitting
docs.text:
During fitting or tensor-frame transformations, the sampled conformer coordinates are transformed into each trial frame before their geometrical factors are evaluated and averaged.

This preserves the relationship between the torsional ensemble and the current susceptibility-tensor frame throughout the fitting procedure.

docs.title: Multiple torsional groups
docs.text:
Multiple torsional groups can be enabled in the same structure.

The current workflow treats separate local torsions independently rather than constructing the full Cartesian product of all torsional samples.

For example, two independently sampled 24-point torsions are not automatically expanded into a 24 × 24 = 576-member global conformational ensemble.

Overlapping rotating fragments require caution because independent averaging is not appropriate when the same atoms participate in coupled torsional motions. Fused planar systems are therefore merged where appropriate, while more general coupled torsions remain outside the scope of the current local-averaging model.

docs.title: Grouped experimental observations
docs.text: Symmetry and torsional averaging describe how calculated member PCS values are obtained. Separately, a structured experimental target can group members within one NMR site and combine several sites into one observation. The current arithmetic reduction averages predictions within each site, then averages the site predictions. It does not evaluate PCS at a mean coordinate or repeat one experimental value as independent measurements for every atom. Sites of different sizes therefore need not give the same result as a flat atom mean. See Structured observations.

docs.title: Relationship between the two averaging approaches
docs.text:
Local symmetry averaging and torsional ensemble averaging use the same central PCS principle but represent different physical situations.

Feature Local symmetry averaging Torsional ensemble averaging Typical use CH\(_3\), CF\(_3\) rotating planar ring / defined torsion Representative coordinate pseudo-atom centroid per-atom ensemble-averaged coordinate New reference ID yes, for pseudo atom no Original atom identity collapsed or retained for display retained PCS geometry average member \(G\) values average sampled \(G\) values

docs.title: 2D Polar PCS Plot
docs.text:
PCS Analyzer distinguishes reference and averaged representations visually.

  • Reference atoms are shown as filled circles using element CPK colors.
  • Torsional ensemble-averaged coordinates are shown as hollow circles with element-colored outlines.
  • CH\(_3\) pseudo atoms are shown as × markers using a dedicated warm-orange representation color.
  • CF\(_3\) pseudo atoms are shown as × markers using a dedicated teal representation color.

The averaging legend is generated dynamically and contains only representations that are currently visible.

The Reference legend entry is shown only when a reference representation is actually displayed, for example when Keep original atoms or Keep reference structure is enabled.

If no averaging representation is active, no averaging legend is displayed.

The PCS contour legend remains separate from the averaging-representation legend.

docs.title: 3D structure view
docs.text:
The 3D structure view follows the same reference-versus-averaged representation concept.

When torsional averaging is active, the ensemble-averaged geometry can be displayed as the active structural representation. If Keep reference structure is enabled, the reference geometry is retained as an overlay for comparison.

The reference overlay is visual only and does not create duplicate PCS observations or fitting rows.

docs.title: Table representation
docs.text:
Torsional ensemble averaging does not create additional table rows.

Each atom retains its original reference ID, while the displayed Cartesian coordinates and geometrical factors correspond to the ensemble-averaged values.

For clarity, torsionally averaged atoms can be marked in the Atom field using a display-only suffix, for example:

C ⟨avg⟩
H ⟨avg⟩
N ⟨avg⟩

The suffix does not modify the internal element identity.

Local-symmetry pseudo atoms retain labels such as:

MeH@C12
CF3F@C7

docs.title: Local symmetry
docs.text:
Local symmetry recognition infers connectivity from distances and covalent radii. Display bond-tolerance controls do not change group detection.

Consequently, unusual geometries, distorted bond distances, missing atoms, non-standard element labels, or structures near the bond-distance threshold can affect group detection.

The automatic local-symmetry workflow is specifically configured for CH\(_3\) and CF\(_3\) groups with the expected substituent connectivity. It should therefore be interpreted as a geometry-based analysis convenience rather than a general chemical-symmetry engine.

docs.title: Torsional ensemble averaging
docs.text:
Automatic torsional detection is also dependent on the inferred molecular graph and Cartesian planarity.

Potential limitations include:

  • incomplete or unusual ligand connectivity,
  • strongly distorted rings,
  • ambiguity in the external attachment bond,
  • coupled torsional degrees of freedom,
  • sterically inaccessible sampled orientations,
  • non-uniform conformational populations.

Uniform torsional sampling is a geometrical averaging model. It does not by itself provide an energetic or Boltzmann-weighted conformational distribution.

For systems where conformer energies or experimentally determined populations are important, the sampled-state weights should be interpreted accordingly or a more explicit conformational-ensemble treatment should be used.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: B. Cordero, V. Gómez, A. E. Platero-Prats, M. Revés, J. Echeverría, E. Cremades, F. Barragán, S. Alvarez, Covalent radii revisited, Dalton Transactions (2008), 2832–2838. DOI: 10.1039/B801115J.

docs.title: 3D PCS Plot
docs.text:
View → 3D PCS Plot opens the PCS Field Viewer — Controls window. Its Open / Refresh Viewer action builds an interactive PyVista scene containing PCS isosurfaces, optional slices, and a molecular overlay.

This viewer requires PyVista and VTK. If PyVista cannot be imported, PCS Analyzer reports the import error and suggests installing pyvista and vtk. Availability therefore depends on the source environment or packaged build.

docs.title: Field and grid generation
docs.text:
The viewer samples the current analytic PCS expression on a uniform Cartesian grid around the visible structure. Coordinates are in the current metal-centred, rotated tensor frame; Δχ_ax and Δχ_rh come from the current tensor inputs. Prediction model: Axial excludes the rhombic term; Full tensor (Axial + Rhombic) includes it only when Enable Δχ_rh is on. See Prediction policy.

The result is a visualization grid, not a new fit or an independently refined field. PyVista extracts surfaces between sampled voxels, so apparent surface smoothness and position depend on the chosen grid spacing. Do not interpret the display resolution as additional experimental or numerical precision.

docs.title: Grid Parameters
docs.text:
Control Effect on the sampled field Grid spacing (Å) Distance between grid samples; smaller values increase spatial sampling and cost Padding (Å): Auto/Manual Extent added around the molecular coordinate bounds; Auto estimates an extent from the tensor and lowest requested level Metal mask r (Å) Sets samples nearer than this metal-centred radius to missing values, suppressing the singular near-origin region Clip ±ppm Optionally clips scalar values before slices and surfaces are generated

These controls affect the numerical display grid. They do not modify the structure, tensor, experimental data, fitting objective, or main calculated atom PCS values.

docs.title: Isosurfaces and slices
docs.text:
Each Isosurface Levels row specifies a positive ppm magnitude. The viewer extracts both \(+\text{level}\) and \(-\text{level}\) surfaces with separate Pos and Neg colors. Style supports surface, mesh, or both, and Opacity applies to that level. Rows can be added or removed.

The Isosurfaces toggle controls all level surfaces. Slice planes adds three orthogonal planes through the metal-centred origin, colored by PCS with a scalar bar. Slice opacity affects only their appearance. Grid and Outline display PyVista aids for the sampled volume.

Clipping is not merely a color-range option: because it changes stored grid values, a clip magnitude below a requested isosurface level can remove or alter that surface.

docs.title: Molecular overlay and appearance
docs.text:
Atoms, H atoms, Bonds, and Labels control the molecular overlay. Atoms use element CPK colors, while labels use Ref:Atom text. Background, Bond color, Bond radius (Å), Ambient light, surface colors, opacity, and mesh style are visual settings.

Bond lines are distance-based guides. Bond tolerance scales the sum of the two covalent radii by 1 + tolerance: increasing it admits longer pairs. The default 0.05 uses a scale of 1.05. This changes displayed connectivity, not molecular coordinates, chemical bonding assignments or PCS calculations.

The molecular overlay follows the active 3D coordinate pipeline and main element filter, but the field viewer does not provide atom-picking or main-table selection synchronization. It also does not render the integrated 3D viewer's reference-versus-average overlay legend.

docs.title: Camera and view preservation
docs.text:
Camera Preset choices are Iso, Top, Front, and Side. Projection selects perspective or orthographic. Apply sends the chosen combination to the live viewer.

Save view stores the complete current camera state in memory; Restore reapplies it while the application is running. Open / Refresh Viewer also preserves the current live camera when rebuilding an existing scene.

Save Preset and Load Preset use a workflow-specific JSON file for grid, level, display, named-camera, and export controls. The JSON preset does not store the structure, calculated field, or arbitrary camera position saved by Save view. See File Formats.

docs.title: PNG export
docs.text:
Save PNG supports only PNG and requires the live viewer to be open.

  • Export view: current captures the live viewer at its current window resolution.
  • Export view: preset rebuilds an off-screen square scene at Width (inch) × DPI pixels and copies the live camera state.

Transparent background applies to either path. The “preset” export mode means high-resolution off-screen rendering; it does not replace the current camera with the named camera preset automatically.

docs.title: Memory and performance
docs.text:
Grid memory and work scale with \(N_xN_yN_z\). Halving Grid spacing (Å) over the same volume creates approximately eight times as many grid points, before accounting for temporary coordinate arrays, contour meshes, and rendering objects. Large padding, small spacing, many surface levels, and simultaneous slices can therefore use substantial memory and make refresh or high-resolution export slow.

Start with coarser spacing and the lowest number of scientifically relevant levels. Refine only after checking the region of interest, and remember that a denser display grid does not improve the underlying structure, tensor, or experimental data.

docs.title: 3D Structure Viewer
docs.text: Use View → 3D Structure or the 3D Structure button to inspect molecular geometry, calculated PCS colors and atom selections in the PyVista viewer. It follows the active PCS document and the main application's structure controls.

docs.title: Open and navigate
docs.text:
You can open the viewer before loading a structure. Load a structure in PCS Analyzer to display it; the first visible structure is fitted automatically. If the view is empty after loading, check the main element and ligand filters. Opening the viewer again brings the existing window forward.

Drag in the structure view to rotate the camera, use the mouse wheel to zoom, and use Camera → Fit to molecule to bring the visible structure into view. Hover over toolbar icons for their descriptions. The Sidebar toggle opens or hides the permanent Display and Figure tabs. You can also open either page from the viewer's View menu. The sidebar has a fixed width; its contents scroll vertically.

Click an atom to select its Ref in the main table. Selecting a table row highlights that atom when it is visible. The viewer highlights the primary selected Ref, rather than the entire regression subset. Selection and ordinary updates retain the camera.

docs.title: Display options
docs.text:
Use the toolbar's Color mode: selector for Element (CPK colors) or PCS (calculated shifts in ppm). The adjacent Atom labels icon toggles labels. Hydrogen and other element visibility follow the main application filters.

In the Display tab, expand a group to reach its controls. Reset icons restore that group's options. Collapsing a group retains its values.

Control Use Preset Basic restores default appearance; Figure uses smoother, higher-detail surfaces and cylinder bonds; Custom retains individual choices. Background Choose a color from the swatch or enter a HEX code. Atom size Adjust atom-marker size; shared with the main application. Bond thickness Adjust Line bonds. Thickness follows zoom relative to the first fitted view. Atoms Set finish, detail and smooth shading. Bonds Set distance tolerance, Line/Cylinder display, finish and color. Cylinder mode uses Radius instead of line thickness. Lighting Adjust illumination, reflections and anti-aliasing. Auto uses the selected finish.

Color controls provide a swatch and HEX field. Click the swatch to choose a color, or enter a code such as #808080. Invalid entries and cancelled color choices keep the previous value.

Bond tolerance determines which visible atom pairs receive distance-based guides; these guides do not indicate bond order. Bond color, thickness, radius and finish change their appearance without changing coordinates or PCS values. The Figure appearance preset does not set export dimensions or DPI.

docs.title: PCS colors and legend
docs.text:
In Color mode: PCS, expand Display → PCS colors.

Control Use Range Auto follows visible PCS values. Manual enables Min/Max in ppm; values beyond the limits use endpoint colors. Centre at zero Use symmetric Auto limits around zero; enabled by default. Palette / Reverse Choose a gradient and its direction. The default is RdBu_r. Missing PCS Choose the color for atoms without calculated PCS; gray by default. Legend Show or hide the PCS color bar, tick labels and PCS (ppm) title. Tick step Auto chooses readable intervals; enter a positive interval in ppm for fixed spacing. Very dense requests fall back to Auto. Legend font Auto follows the plot fonts; set a point size to override it.

These options change the color display, not calculated PCS. If no visible atom has a calculated PCS value, the default display uses element colors and no PCS color bar. Averaged and reference markers retain their distinct representation.

docs.title: Camera and axes
docs.text:
Camera action Use Fit to molecule Fit visible working/reference geometry while keeping view direction and projection. Reset camera Restore the initial camera and fit the current structure. Projection Choose Perspective or Orthographic. Standard views Look from +X, −X, +Y, −Y, +Z, −Z or the Isometric direction.

Camera movement changes your viewpoint, not molecular coordinates or tensor orientation. A signed standard view looks from that side of the working frame towards the molecule. Camera actions are unavailable without visible geometry.

In Display → Axes, choose Metal centre, Screen corner, Both or Hidden. Metal-centre controls set arrow length, thickness, tip shape and labels. Corner controls set position, size and labels; the marker follows camera rotation. X / Y / Z provides individual visibility and color controls for both placements. Axis label sizes use renderer pixels; Figure output label sizes use points.

docs.title: Coordinates and averaging
docs.text:
The view uses the real working structure, including the active metal centre, applied fit override, main X/Y/Z rotations and visibility filters. Coordinates are displayed in the metal-centred working frame. See Fitting Overview for applied-fit orientation and centre behavior.

When torsional averaging is enabled, the active averaged geometry can replace raw positions. Averaged atoms are hollow markers. Keep reference structure adds filled reference markers for moving atoms and a separate Averaging legend. The reference overlay is visual only and adds no observations or fitting rows.

Local CH₃/CF₃ pseudo atoms used by the table and fitting are not substituted into this real-structure view. See Symmetry and Torsional Ensemble Averaging.

docs.title: Figure and export
docs.text: Choose Figure output for an image prepared at a chosen size and DPI, or Viewport capture for the current view. Both are available in File and the toolbar's Export menu.

docs.title: Prepare a figure
docs.text:
Open the Figure tab and set Width, Height, Units (mm, in or px), DPI and Background. Defaults are 180 × 135 mm, 300 DPI, White. Viewport uses the current display background; Transparent removes it. With pixel units, changing DPI changes physical size rather than pixel dimensions.

Expand Style to set margins, label size and line width. Explicit label/line sizes are in points. Auto scales Line bonds to output magnification and PCS legend typography to output DPI; other annotations retain their existing sizing behavior. Check the preview at the intended output size.

Expand Include to exclude axes, atom labels, PCS/Averaging legends, selection highlighting or reference structure from the output. These controls only include layers already visible in the view. All are enabled by default. Each section has its own reset; the footer reset restores all Figure options.

Use Preview to inspect a snapshot, then Save to choose PNG, PDF (image) or SVG (image). Regenerate the preview after changing the camera or settings. Output does not resize the live view. A different aspect ratio or large margin can crop the structure, so check framing before saving.

docs.title: Choose an output format
docs.text:
Output Contents Figure PNG Prepared image with the selected size, DPI, margins and layers. Figure PDF/SVG (image) The same prepared image embedded in a document at its physical size. Viewport PNG Current viewport at its current pixel size, including visible annotations. Viewport PDF/SVG (experimental) Graphics export that may contain rasterized geometry or annotations. Transparent layers are unsupported.

PDF/SVG and vector editing

Figure PDF/SVG contain an embedded image; atoms, bonds and labels are not editable vector objects. Experimental viewport PDF/SVG are also not guaranteed to be purely vector. Inspect the saved file before publication.

PDF Figure output requires White or Viewport background; SVG supports Transparent. Figure output supports DPI from 72 to 1200, at most 16 million pixels and 8192 pixels per side. The panel shows output dimensions and explains invalid requests. If the document changes during an export dialog, reopen export.

docs.title: Save and reuse visualization settings
docs.text:
Choose File → Visualization settings → Save… / Load… to reuse appearance, background, PCS colors, axes and Figure options. The same menu is available through Export. These JSON files contain display choices, not molecular structures, calculated results or a complete session.

State How it is retained Color mode and atom-label visibility Saved in the PCS .pcsp project. Atom size and bond tolerance Shared main-application display controls; excluded from visualization JSON. Appearance, PCS colors, axes and Figure options Retained during updates to the same document; reset on document switch. Save visualization JSON to reuse them. Camera, selection, window layout and expanded groups Temporary viewer state; not saved in visualization JSON.

Viewer-local display options are not stored in .pcsp or application settings. Older visualization files without PCS color options load with their defaults. See Projects and Persistence and File Formats for other saved data.

docs.title: Availability and legacy viewer
docs.text:
The PyVista molecular viewer replaces the legacy Matplotlib viewer used as the main structure viewer through v1.3.4. The legacy viewer remains available under View → Open Matplotlib viewer…; its export uses its own camera.

The default viewer requires PySide6, PyVista, VTK and pyvistaqt. If it cannot start, or the structure exceeds the current limit of 1000 visible working/reference markers, PCS Analyzer offers the Matplotlib viewer. See Installation for source dependencies.

Mixed-monitor DPI behavior, packaged execution and PDF/SVG output quality still need broader verification. Check labels, colors, legends and framing in saved figures. For the separate volumetric field viewer, see 3D PCS Plot.

docs.title: Practice: Averaging and PCS visualization
docs.text: The existing examples/documentation_demo/Nd_iPr2BA3_demo/Nd_iPr2BA3_axial.pcsp is suitable for molecular display and averaging practice. Keep its original experimental assignment caveats: disabling averaging does not turn a group observation into independent measurements of all member atoms. Use File → Open PCS Project... for that project; see finding the examples for its location.

docs.title: Compare views using the Nd project
docs.text:
Open the project with its original tensor/frame. Compare methyl symmetry averaging on/off and phenyl rotational averaging on/off. Inspect Ref membership and pseudo- or group targets. Keep the tensor fixed when comparing the 2D polar plot, Projection Viewer and 3D molecular viewer. Choose PCS coloring and show hydrogens in the molecular viewer to inspect the scientific color scale; color changes are not numerical fits.

In 3D PCS Controls, compare positive/negative isosurfaces and slice planes at the same levels. Change grid spacing/padding deliberately; the sampled analytic field is a display calculation, not extra experimental precision. Mask the near-metal singular region. Save review settings and exported figures separately from the canonical input project.

docs.title: Additional CF₃/tBu fixture
docs.text:
examples/averaging_visualization_demo/groups.xyz supplies synthetic disconnected fragments with three methyl groups, one CF₃ group and one tBu centre. These are topology/detection examples, not optimized chemistry or experimental PCS data. Ref 2 is the tBu centre, Refs 4–6 are its methyl carbons, and Ref 17 is the CF₃ carbon. Nd at Ref 1 is a display reference, not a validated coordination site. Click + in the document tab strip, then use File → Load XYZ... to load groups.xyz in that new document to inspect grouping controls; do not assign it the Nd example's experimental data.

Raw Ref IDs and generated pseudo-atom indices are distinct. Group detection does not by itself establish rapid exchange, equivalence or a physical tensor.

docs.title: Chemical Map
docs.text: Open View → Chemical Map or Ribbon → Data → Chemical Map with a structure loaded. Inspect coordinating ligand instances, Ref IDs, and NMR sites while assigning experimental observations.

docs.title: Views and selection
docs.text: Control Purpose Ligand / Instance Choose a ligand group and a particular matching instance. Chemical Compact depiction, including collapsed hydrogen/site representations where applicable. Atom Map Inspect individual atom correspondence and Ref IDs. Geometry Projection Inspect a projection of existing 3D coordinates. Layout CoordGen, RDKit 2D, or Graph 2D for the 2D depiction; engines depend on installed dependencies. H, Ref IDs, NMR sites, Matching Show information needed for atom/site mapping.

docs.title: Chemical
docs.text: Chemical view with Ref IDs and NMR-site markers.

docs.title: Atom Map
docs.text: Atom Map with hydrogens and Ref IDs.

docs.title: Geometry Projection
docs.text:
Geometry Projection view.

Hover for atom/Ref details; click atoms or site representations to publish a selection to PCS Analyzer. Shared selection links the map, main table, and Workbench structural context. Grouped sites can select multiple members. Use Use in PCS Preparation in the Workbench to accept an inspected target explicitly. Selection synchronization does not verify an assignment.

docs.title: Editing: three different meanings
docs.text:
• Bond Edit changes connectivity/bond-type interpretation. This can affect ligand recognition, site detection, and matching. Check inferred bonds before using those groups for experimental observations.
  • 2D Edit, Cleanup, rotation/flip/scale, and resetting a 2D layout adjust the depiction. They do not move molecular XYZ coordinates or change distances and angles used in PCS calculations.
  • Geometry Projection displays existing 3D geometry; Cleanup is disabled in this view, and 2D dragging is not geometry refinement. Use structure/orientation workflows for scientific coordinate changes.

Apply to matching ligands can propagate applicable edits beyond the shown instance. Check that scope before editing; Undo reverses the last map edit. Bond inference and ligand/site matching need review for unusual coordination environments. A clean diagram does not prove correct bonding, chemical equivalence, or an appropriate PCS averaging model.

docs.title: 2D Polar PCS Plot
docs.text:
The 2D Polar PCS Plot places the current structure on an axial PCS contour map. Open it with View → 2D PCS Plot or Open viewers → 2D PCS Plot. The same rendering also appears in the main workspace.

This view remains an axial diagnostic even when Prediction model is Full tensor (Axial + Rhombic): its contours use the current Δχ_ax and the axial \(r,\theta\) expression. A single polar contour cannot represent the full \(\phi\)-dependent rhombic field. See PCS Contour Plots for the scientific interpretation and Projection Viewer or 3D PCS Plot for tensor-aware angular views.

docs.title: Contours and angular domain
docs.text:
PCS plot range (ppm) and PCS plot interval (ppm) choose the contour values. Positive contours are drawn on a red scale, negative contours on a blue scale, and the legend is titled PCS legend (ppm). Dashed lines mark the axial magic angles. The radial scale is displayed in Å and the current plot is limited to 10 Å.

The Half/Quarter plot toggle selects the actual angular domain:

  • Half-plane: \(0^\circ\leq\theta\leq180^\circ\).
  • Quarter-plane: \(0^\circ\leq\theta\leq90^\circ\).

In Quarter view, atom positions with \(\theta>90^\circ\) are folded to \(180^\circ-\theta\). The axial contours are mirrored consistently. This is a compact display of axial symmetry; it does not change coordinates, geometrical factors, calculated PCS values, regressions, or fits.

docs.title: Atom markers and bonds
docs.text:
Markers use element CPK colors. Atom radii switches between fixed marker sizes and sizes scaled from covalent radii; Atom scale multiplies the display size. These controls affect marker appearance only.

Bonds draws guide lines between currently displayed atoms. The test uses their three-dimensional distance and

\[ d_{ij}\leq(r_i^\mathrm{cov}+r_j^\mathrm{cov})(1+\text{tol.}). \]

width changes line thickness and tol. changes this visualization-only cutoff. These lines do not encode bond order or experimentally determined connectivity, and the tolerance is unrelated to the fixed connectivity rules used by functional-group or torsional detection. See Symmetry and Torsional Ensemble Averaging.

docs.title: Averaging and reference overlays
docs.text:
The plot distinguishes active averaging representations:

  • ordinary/reference positions are filled element-colored circles;
  • torsional ensemble-average positions are hollow element-colored circles;
  • CH₃ symmetry pseudo atoms are warm-orange × markers; and
  • CF₃ symmetry pseudo atoms are teal × markers.

When Keep original atoms or Keep reference structure produces a reference overlay, the plot shows it separately. The Averaging legend is dynamic and lists only representations that are currently visible; it is separate from the PCS contour legend.

An averaged marker is a representative coordinate. PCS Analyzer calculates averaged PCS geometry from member/sample geometrical factors rather than from that marker position. The precise distinction is documented in Symmetry and Torsional Ensemble Averaging.

docs.title: Selection synchronization
docs.text:
Clicking a marker selects, focuses, and scrolls to its Ref row in the main table. Selecting a table row redraws both the embedded and popup polar plots; the selected atom is enlarged and, for circular markers, surrounded by a yellow ring.

Only visible effective atoms have clickable markers. A folded Quarter-view position still selects the atom's original Ref ID.

docs.title: Calculation controls versus display controls
docs.text: Control or input Effect Δχ_ax, structure, metal centre, rotations, and averaging model Changes the scientific coordinates and/or PCS calculation used by the view PCS plot range and interval Changes which axial contour levels are drawn Half/Quarter toggle Changes only the displayed angular domain Atom radii and Atom scale Changes marker size only Bonds, width, and tol. Changes visual connectivity guides only

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
The popup includes the standard Matplotlib navigation toolbar. In addition, File → Save plot data... supports:

  • PNG for the currently open 2D PCS plot;
  • XLSX with PCS Data and Atom Coordinates sheets; or
  • CSV as separate _pcs.csv and _atoms.csv files.

PNG export through this command requires the popup to be open. Exported Theta values in the numerical plot-data files are radians. See File Formats for exact outputs.

docs.title: Projection Viewer
docs.text: Open View → Projection or Open viewers → Projection to display the current PCS angular field at a fixed radius. The viewer uses the current Δχ_ax, Δχ_rh, tensor-frame rotation, effective atom coordinates, and main-window element filter.

docs.title: Projection modes
docs.text:
The Projection mode: control provides two representations of the same angular field:

  • φ / cos(θ) is a rectangular map with \(\phi\) from \(-\pi\) to \(\pi\) and \(\cos\theta\) from −1 to 1.
  • Mollweide maps longitude \(\phi\) and latitude \(\pi/2-\theta\) onto a Mollweide globe projection.

Both modes show a filled red/blue PCS map, white contour lines, and a PCS (ppm) color bar. The UI calls the first mode φ / cos(θ); it is a rectangular angular projection, not a plot of molecular Cartesian coordinates.

docs.title: Fixed radius
docs.text:
Fixed r [Å]: is the radius used to calculate every background grid point. The background PCS therefore scales with \(r^{-3}\). A blank, nonnumeric, or non-positive value falls back to 10 Å.

The fixed radius is a scientific input to this projection map, not merely a zoom control. Atom markers, however, are placed from their angular direction only; their actual distance from the metal does not move them radially within the map. The projection is therefore useful for orientation, not for reading an atom's complete distance-dependent PCS directly.

See Axial and Rhombic PCS and Tensor Conventions for the underlying terms.

The projection follows Prediction model: Axial excludes Δχ_rh, while Full tensor (Axial + Rhombic) includes it only when Enable Δχ_rh is on. A stored nonzero Δχ_rh alone does not activate a rhombic field. See Prediction policy.

docs.title: Atoms, filtering, and selection
docs.text:
Show atoms overlays the currently effective, rotated atom set. Marker colors follow element CPK colors. The main Select elements to display checklist applies first; Show H provides an additional hydrogen-only filter inside the viewer.

The current Projection Viewer has no atom-label control. Click a marker to select and reveal its Ref row in the main table. Selection is one-way in this viewer: selecting a main-table row does not currently add a projection-marker highlight.

Symmetry pseudo atoms and torsionally averaged positions can appear because the viewer uses the effective main-workflow coordinates. Their marker positions remain a geometric display; averaging calculations follow the rules in Symmetry and Torsional Ensemble Averaging.

docs.title: Refresh and export
docs.text:
Changing the projection mode or committing Fixed r [Å] redraws the map. Use ⟳ Refresh after changing relevant main-window state if the open view has not otherwise redrawn.

💾 Export Figure saves the current figure as PNG, PDF, or SVG at 600 dpi. The Matplotlib toolbar also provides its normal pan, zoom, and save controls. The export contains the rendered map and optional atom markers; it does not write a numerical projection grid.
